conflicts.issue: Southwest Durham Urban Growth Area (UGA) Boundary Amendment Along NC 751
conflicts.summary: Council divided 5-2 over whether to amend the Urban Growth Area boundary in Southwest Durham to incorporate parcels near the proposed 751 Assemblage development.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the staff-recommended UGA boundary amendment now.
side_a_arguments: Planning staff rigorously reviewed the boundary and recommended aligning it with the 2006 watershed/normal-pool interpretation.
Extending the UGA allows consideration of future utility extension, job creation, and increased tax revenue.
Amending the UGA boundary does not obligate Council to extend water and sewer or approve rezoning without further review.
conflicts.side_b_position: Delay extending the UGA boundary pending resolution of the utility extension agreement and county litigation.
side_b_arguments: Extending the UGA is not legally required immediately and implicates all municipal services, not only water and sewer.
Council should wait for the outcome of the pending county lawsuit affecting the 751 project and reconsider the utility extension agreement first.
Expanding the UGA southward sets a long-term precedent encouraging additional development along the NC 751 corridor.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted 5-2, with Mayor Bell, Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden, and Council Members Clement, Brown, and Ali voting Aye, and Council Members Catotti and Woodard voting Nay.

conflicts.issue: Resolution Supporting Recognition of the Matricula Consular as Valid Identification
conflicts.summary: Council voted 5-2 to adopt a non-binding policy resolution supporting recognition of the Matricula Consular as valid identification, with Eugene Brown and Howard Clement III dissenting.
conflicts.side_a_position: Adopt the resolution expressing Council support for accepting the Matricula Consular as valid identification.
side_a_arguments: The City Attorney confirmed the resolution is a non-binding statement of Council policy rather than a law or ordinance.
Police leadership had worked with advocates and indicated no objection to treating the card similarly to other valid forms of ID.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose adopting the Matricula Consular recognition resolution.
side_b_arguments: Eugene Brown and Howard Clement III had previously raised questions at work sessions regarding sheriff alignment, other North Carolina cities' practices, and minor traffic-stop enforcement.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 5-2.

conflicts.issue: Donation of Surplus City Equipment to the Town of Princeville (Item 3)
conflicts.summary: Council approved donating surplus city vehicles and equipment to the Town of Princeville by a 5-2 vote, with Mike Woodard and Eugene Brown dissenting.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the donation of surplus city equipment to support the Town of Princeville.
side_a_arguments: Supporting Princeville's request helps the town bring municipal services in-house and save money (as presented at the Feb 4 work session).
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose donating auctionable surplus equipment to another municipality.
side_b_arguments: Mike Woodard and Eugene Brown recorded No votes on Item 3 (consistent with Eugene Brown's Feb 4 work session concern over giving away $25,000+ in auctionable equipment amid Durham's own budget cuts and layoffs).
conflicts.resolution: Item 3 passed 5-2 (Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Diane Catotti, Farad Ali; Nays: Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown).

conflicts.issue: Hope Valley Farms Rezoning Drive-Thru Orientation and Parkway Buffering (Item 39)
conflicts.summary: Council divided 5-2 over whether proffered committed elements—a 36-inch masonry wall, no fuel sales/convenience store, and keeping drive-thru windows off the southwest neighborhood-facing side—adequately protected Martin Luther King Jr. Parkway aesthetics and adjacent homes.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the rezoning with the three proffered committed elements shielding the adjacent neighborhood and prohibiting fuel sales.
side_a_arguments: The applicant agreed to bar convenience stores and gas pumps and prohibit drive-thru order windows facing the southwest neighborhood.
A 36-inch masonry wall paired with landscaping provides standard headlight screening along the parkway.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose the rezoning due to drive-thru orientation, parkway visual character, and neighborhood impacts.
side_b_arguments: Placing the drive-thru away from the southwest houses pushes the drive-thru circulation toward Martin Luther King Jr. Parkway, undermining its parkway character.
Deciduous tree buffers offer limited visual and noise screening for neighbors during winter months.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 5-2 with the three proffered committed elements.

conflicts.issue: Proposed Billboard / Sign Ordinance Text Amendment
conflicts.summary: Moved with stated intention of voting no after staff confirmed retaining the existing billboard ordinance causes no harm to the city and carries existing U.S. Supreme Court-tested legal protections.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Failed 0-7)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Failed (0-7)

conflicts.issue: West Village II Second Amendment (Use of EDA Funds for Underground Power Lines and Youth Space)
conflicts.summary: Council split 3-3 on approving the Second Amendment to the West Village II Agreement, leading to an initial tie failure before Council unanimously voted to reconsider and postpone the item to January 4, 2010.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the Second Amendment to restore $1 million in EDA funds for alternate streetscape projects while advancing West Village II.
side_a_arguments: The amendment restores $1 million of EDA money (against $4 million general money) previously tied up, making it available for alternate streetscape projects.
Delaying risks time-constraint complications on project administration.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose or withhold approval due to continued opposition to EDA-funded Main Street power-line undergrounding and unanswered questions on youth space commitments.
side_b_arguments: EDA funds should not be used to underground electrical power lines along Main Street, which Council had not originally committed to funding.
Further follow-up is needed from the developer regarding promised youth/community space.
conflicts.resolution: Failed 3-3 on the initial vote; subsequently reconsidered (6-0) and postponed (6-0) to the January 4, 2010 agenda cycle.

conflicts.issue: Local Funding Commitment for Southside Phase 1 Submission to NC Housing Finance Agency (Item 8)
conflicts.summary: Council divided 6-1 on committing local city funds for the Southside Phase 1 submission to the North Carolina Housing Finance Agency, with Council Member Eugene Brown casting the sole dissenting vote.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the local funding commitment to support the Southside Phase 1 North Carolina Housing Finance Agency submission.
side_a_arguments: Providing the local funding commitment enables the Southside/Rolling Hills Phase 1 mixed-income housing application to proceed to the state housing finance agency.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose the local funding commitment for Southside Phase 1.
side_b_arguments: Consistent with concerns raised in prior Southside financing deliberations regarding long-term city financial exposure and reliance on CDBG/Section 108 commitments, Eugene Brown voted no on the commitment.
conflicts.resolution: Motion passed 6-1 after Eugene Brown corrected the record at 03:36:54 to register his no vote.

conflicts.issue: Statutory Vested Rights Exemption from November 4 Riparian Buffer Amendments (Bethpage Village & Chin Page Office Park, VR10-01)
conflicts.summary: Council voted 6-1 to grant a five-year vested rights determination shielding a 468-acre mixed-use project from newly adopted riparian buffer rules, with Diane Catotti voting Nay.
conflicts.side_a_position: Grant the five-year statutory vested rights determination under the stream buffer rules contemplated in the 2008 master plan.
side_a_arguments: Staff determined the application met all statutory vested rights standards.
The developers argued the 50-foot buffer framework matched the 2008 master development plan and enabled a major mixed-use competitor to Brier Creek.
conflicts.side_b_position: Do not exempt the project from the recently adopted November 4 riparian buffer ordinance amendments.
side_b_arguments: Diane Catotti questioned the applicants specifically regarding the November riparian buffer text amendments, including buffering underground/interrupted stream gaps of 300 feet or less.
conflicts.resolution: Vested rights determination VR10-01 passed 6-1.

conflicts.issue: Greystone Baptist Church Street Closing vs. Neighborhood Plan Precedent and Bike/Pedestrian Easement
conflicts.summary: Neighborhood speakers opposed closing the street segment without connectivity safeguards, and Council rejected Mike Woodard's 2-5 substitute motion requiring a 10–12 foot bike/pedestrian easement before unanimously approving the unconditional street closing 7-0.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the street closing promptly without deferral or an added easement mandate to support Greystone Baptist Church's daycare expansion.
side_a_arguments: Demand for quality daycare exceeds supply in Durham, and neighborhood plans should be flexible rather than 'etched in stone.'

Church representatives warned that deferring action would cost thousands of dollars in pre-construction expenses, and nearby Warner Street/15th Street provided adjacent access between Hillsborough Road and Main Street.
conflicts.side_b_position: Defer for neighborhood consultation or require committed design assurances and a 10–12 foot bike/pedestrian connectivity easement.
side_b_arguments: Old West Durham Neighborhood Association argued the street closing chipped away at the Ninth Street / West Durham plan and set a harmful precedent.
Retaining a 10–12 foot easement or committed site-plan elements would preserve bicycle and pedestrian connectivity between Hillsborough Road and Main Street.
conflicts.resolution: Mike Woodard's substitute motion for a committed 10–12 foot easement failed 2-5, and Council then approved Howard Clement III's main motion for the street closing 7-0.

conflicts.issue: PAC Review Compliance for Beer and Wine Privilege Licenses (Item 7)
conflicts.summary: Council divided 6-1 over approving 51 beer and wine privilege license renewals and new applications, with Council Member Howard Clement III dissenting over whether Partners Against Crime (PAC) districts had actually been given an opportunity to review them.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the beer and wine privilege license issuances based on staff's checklist confirmation.
side_a_arguments: Police/staff represented that PAC notification—either at PAC meetings or over the PAC listserv—is a required part of the application checklist.
conflicts.side_b_position: Vote no because PAC districts, including PAC 4, had not actually reviewed the 51 applications.
side_b_arguments: As chair of PAC 4, Clement stated he did not recall 51 new and renewal applications coming before PAC 4 since Council last raised the issue.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 6-1 with Howard Clement III voting Nay.

conflicts.issue: Full Frame Documentary Film Festival Request (Item 14)
conflicts.summary: Council voted 6-1 to approve Item 14 for the Full Frame Documentary Film Festival, with Howard Clement III dissenting.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the Full Frame Documentary Film Festival request.
side_a_arguments: Majority supported advancing the General Business Agenda item as presented.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose the organization's request on Item 14.
side_b_arguments: Howard Clement III stated he opposed the request by the organization and cast the lone Nay vote.
conflicts.resolution: Item 14 passed 6-1 (Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Farad Ali; Nay: Howard Clement III).

conflicts.issue: Harvard Avenue Sidewalk Request (Item 13)
conflicts.summary: Council Member Eugene Brown cast the lone Nay vote in a 5-1 approval of the Harvard Avenue sidewalk request following neighborhood questions and earlier Council debate over prioritizing Harvard Avenue ahead of other petitioned sidewalk projects.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the Harvard Avenue sidewalk request while directing staff to inspect and resolve temporary erosion-control concerns on the roadway.
side_a_arguments: Public Works confirmed Harvard Avenue construction would proceed as proposed and agreed to inspect the temporary erosion-control measures.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose the Harvard Avenue sidewalk request.
side_b_arguments: Eugene Brown voted Nay on the item (no floor debate remarks by Brown were recorded during the December 20 vote itself).
conflicts.resolution: Item 13 passed 5-1 (with Diane Catotti absent/excused).

conflicts.issue: McDonald's Parking Lot Expansion Special Use Permit and Site Plan (Items 27 & 28)
conflicts.summary: Council voted 5-1 on both the Major Special Use Permit (Item 27) and, upon reconsideration, the companion Major Site Plan and Floodplain Development Permit (Item 28) for the McDonald's parking lot expansion, with Diane Catotti dissenting.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the Major Special Use Permit (Option 1 with staff-recommended conditions) and companion site plan/floodplain permit.
side_a_arguments: The site plan complied with all Unified Development Ordinance standards.
Staff recommended approval conditioned on substantial consistency with submitted plans (D07-548) and completion of site improvements prior to compliance.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose granting the Major Special Use Permit and companion site plan/floodplain permit.
side_b_arguments: Specific reasons for Diane Catotti's Nay vote were not preserved in the truncated portion of the transcript digest.
conflicts.resolution: Both Item 27 and reconsidered Item 28 passed 5-1 (Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Eugene Brown, and Farad Ali voting Aye; Diane Catotti voting Nay; Mike Woodard absent).

conflicts.issue: Proposed Donation of Surplus City Equipment to the Town of Princeville
conflicts.summary: Following Princeville Mayor Priscilla Everette-Oates's request for surplus trucks and police cars, Council Member Eugene Brown questioned donating over $25,000 in auctionable equipment to another municipality while Durham faced staff layoffs, foreclosures, and budget shortfalls.
conflicts.side_a_position: Prepare a resolution to donate surplus city vehicles to assist the Town of Princeville.
side_a_arguments: Mayor Bill Bell invited the Princeville Mayor and noted staff compiled available surplus vehicles for Council consideration on February 15.
Princeville sought dump trucks, trash trucks, and three police cars to perform services in-house, save funds, and create local jobs.
conflicts.side_b_position: Question donating $25,000+ in auctionable surplus equipment away from Durham taxpayers.
side_b_arguments: Durham had already laid off staff and cut budgets and faced another difficult budget retreat.
Durham County averaged seven foreclosures per day in January, and auctioning the surplus equipment could yield over $25,000.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken at the work session; the item remained on the February 15 Consent Agenda, where it later passed 5-2 with Eugene Brown and Mike Woodard voting Nay.

conflicts.issue: Administrative Hiring Policy vs. Immediate Directive to Draft a 'Ban the Box' Ordinance
conflicts.summary: Following Second Chance Alliance testimony, Council Member Howard Clement III pushed to instruct staff immediately to draft a binding 'Ban the Box' ordinance, while Mayor Bill Bell favored receiving the staff hiring policy first and studying Philadelphia's ordinance before drafting.
conflicts.side_a_position: Receive the administration's city-hiring policy update first and study Philadelphia's ordinance and experience before deciding on a broader ordinance.
side_a_arguments: The administration's proposed procedure already addresses criminal-background barriers for city employment.

Council had no draft ordinance in hand to evaluate citywide implications, and Bell committed to retrieving Philadelphia's ordinance and consulting Philadelphia Mayor Nutter for fuller debate after the July recess.
conflicts.side_b_position: Instruct the City Manager and City Attorney immediately to draft a binding ordinance incorporating advocates' proposals.
side_b_arguments: Leaving the meeting without a clear-cut directive to draft an ordinance after extensive public testimony would be meaningless.
The City Attorney has criminal-law expertise needed to participate in drafting an ordinance.
conflicts.resolution: Council voted 7-0 to receive the background investigation policy report with Council's comments incorporated, with the manager instructed to obtain Philadelphia's ordinance for an anticipated August discussion.

conflicts.issue: Codifying 'Ban the Box' Hiring Policy: Ordinance vs. Resolution
conflicts.summary: Council debated whether to codify Durham's 'ban the box' policy removing criminal-conviction questions from initial city employment applications via a permanent city ordinance or a Council resolution/administrative directive.
conflicts.side_a_position: Enact a permanent codified ordinance banning the box on city employment applications.
side_a_arguments: An ordinance creates a permanent legal standard not contingent on who serves as HR director or City Manager.
A resolution lacks the permanence and binding force of an ordinance.
conflicts.side_b_position: Adopt a Council resolution affirming current administrative practice (or pair a resolution with staff review of personnel ordinances).
side_b_arguments: City Attorney noted only 12-13 personnel policies are codified as ordinances while hundreds are handled via flexible City Manager directives.
A resolution can affirm current practice immediately and keep the issue on the Council's radar while staff evaluates ordinance options.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; Council directed the City Manager and City Attorney to review existing personnel ordinances and return with a recommendation.

conflicts.meeting_title: Special City Council Meeting - 751 South Project Voluntary Annexation
conflicts.issue: Purpose of Special Informational Session and Fairness Amid Pending 751 South Lawsuit
conflicts.summary: Council Members Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti expressed differing views on holding a non-decision informational session while neighbors' litigation against the 751 South project remained pending.
conflicts.side_a_position: Questioned holding the special meeting without making a decision and warned that indefinite litigation delays are unfair to the developer.
side_a_arguments: Project opponents could keep the matter in court indefinitely through trials and appeals while the developer continues absorbing carrying costs.
With Council unable to affect the lawsuit and taking no decision at the session, holding the meeting without a decision timeline raised fairness concerns.
conflicts.side_b_position: Defended the meeting as a necessary educational session given the project's legal and fiscal complexity.
side_b_arguments: The 751 South annexation involves highly complicated fiscal, legal, environmental, and infrastructure issues requiring a dedicated learning ('didactic') session.
Council also needed detailed analysis on alternatives such as extending utilities without immediate annexation while preserving future annexation rights.
conflicts.resolution: No vote was taken on the annexation; staff committed to returning a consolidated written response package to Council's questions in two to three weeks.

conflicts.issue: Conditioning Durham Transit Sales Tax Implementation on Orange and Wake County Referenda
conflicts.summary: Mayor Bill Bell and Council Member Diane Catotti disagreed on whether Council's resolution supporting the regional bus and rail investment plan should recommend delaying Durham's half-cent sales tax until Orange or Wake counties approve similar referenda.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support the regional transit plan while recommending the County delay levying the tax until Orange County and/or Wake County pass a referendum.
side_a_arguments: The bus and rail investment plan is a regional system requiring state, federal, and multi-county participation rather than Durham taxpayers funding it alone.
Implementing a half-cent sales tax solely in Durham could put local small businesses at a competitive disadvantage against neighboring counties.
conflicts.side_b_position: Prefer the original unamended resolution without tying Durham's tax implementation to Orange and Wake counties.
side_b_arguments: Durham should not have its hands tied by neighboring counties' timelines.
Durham would realize significant benefits from expanding bus service hours prior to regional rail coming online.
conflicts.resolution: Mike Woodard moved Mayor Bill Bell's amended resolution, and Council adopted it 7-0.

conflicts.meeting_title: City Council Budget Review FY 2011-12 - Flagged Items
conflicts.issue: Referring Low-Income Durham Residents to Outside HUD Housing Counseling Agencies
conflicts.summary: Council members challenged staff's reliance on external HUD-funded agencies outside Durham after local partners declined to provide unfunded housing counseling.
conflicts.side_a_position: Questioned referring Durham residents to out-of-city agencies like Chapel Hill and urged local service delivery.
side_a_arguments: Referring low-income Durham residents—particularly Southside and Rolling Hills prospects who may lack vehicles—to Chapel Hill is burdensome and problematic.
With three of four remaining agencies refusing unfunded referrals, the city should consider handling counseling in-house or arranging MOUs for HUD-funded partners to come to Durham.
conflicts.side_b_position: Explained budget limits restrict direct city funding to residents tied to city homeownership programs (<=80% AMI) while broader counseling relies on external HUD partners.
side_b_arguments: City-funded pre-purchase counseling supports specific city homeownership initiatives, and the city had already ended its 100% police mortgage program due to cost.
Staff noted all suggestions for local MOUs and serving unbanked/unemployed residents were under internal departmental discussion.
conflicts.resolution: Informational review only; staff agreed to continue exploring local MOUs and in-house counseling options.

conflicts.issue: Placement of Matricula Consular Resolution on Regular Session GBA
conflicts.summary: Council Member Howard Clement III requested additional background and full-council regular session deliberation on the Matricula Consular resolution rather than taking immediate action at the work session.
conflicts.side_a_position: Advance the Matricula Consular resolution promptly given police chief support and City Attorney revisions.
side_a_arguments: Chief Lopez met with citizens and expressed no objection, the Attorney's office reworked the draft, and advocates hoped for immediate passage.
conflicts.side_b_position: Move the resolution to the November 15 General Business Agenda and gather answers on statewide municipal and sheriff practices.
side_b_arguments: More information was needed on which other North Carolina cities adopted the policy, whether the Durham County Sheriff accepted it, and how minor traffic-stop citation discretion operates.
conflicts.resolution: Placed on the November 15 Regular Session General Business Agenda for debate and vote.

conflicts.issue: Using Future Federal CDBG/HOME Entitlements for Rolling Hills / Southside Redevelopment (Item 25)
conflicts.summary: Public speakers, nonprofit housing providers, and Council members debated whether committing millions in future federal CDBG/HOME entitlements to MBA Development Corporation for Rolling Hills/Southside ($5.49M subordinate financing and up to $3.89M site/infrastructure) unfairly diverted funds from community nonprofits and existing Southside homeowners amid severe municipal budget constraints.
conflicts.side_a_position: Advance the Rolling Hills/Southside conditional financing commitment to catalyze neighborhood revitalization while exploring alternative funding for nonprofits.
side_a_arguments: The Rolling Hills project offered the best hope to address safety and disinvestment in a challenged neighborhood.

Council had already unanimously asked the administration to identify alternative financing plans, and Mayor Bell noted roughly half a cent on the property tax could replace the peak $1.3 million in prior annual nonprofit funding.
conflicts.side_b_position: Question committing future federal entitlements and reducing support for nonprofit housing and service providers or existing Southside residents.
side_b_arguments: Nonprofit developers such as Builders of Hope and Southside advocates warned that diverting funds left existing Southside homeowners without rehab support and threatened nonprofit housing/job-training capacity.
Critics on Council expressed shock at pledging future entitlements during a tight budget cycle when the City could not even afford a new 15-officer police academy.
conflicts.resolution: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved the conditional commitments for MBA Development Corporation at [04:08:03]–[04:09:09]; the vote occurred in an omitted 8-second gap in the transcript digest before [04:09:17].

conflicts.issue: Item 6: Second Amendment to West Village II Agreement
conflicts.summary: Mike Woodard and Diane Catotti opposed undergrounding Main Street power lines with EDA funds, and Cora Cole-McFadden voted no seeking follow-up information on community/youth space.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Failed 3-3)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Failed (3-3)

conflicts.meeting_title: City Council Budget Review FY 2011-12 - Flagged Items
conflicts.issue: Funding Critical Deferred Facility Maintenance vs. Preserving Street Resurfacing Allocation
conflicts.summary: Council and administration weighed whether to redirect $500,000 from street resurfacing to address urgent building maintenance like the $425,000 fleet maintenance roof immediately or wait for year-end fund balance.
conflicts.side_a_position: Keep the $500,000 in the street resurfacing operating line and revisit deferred maintenance using FY11 carry-forward fund balance in two to three months.
side_a_arguments: Removing the $500,000 from street resurfacing would send a poor signal regarding commitments made during the 2007 bond referendum to transition paving into the operating budget.
Returning after June 30 fiscal closeout allows Council to target carry-forward funds toward the ~$1.0 million in critical Priority 1 repairs.
conflicts.side_b_position: Questioned keeping $500,000 unspent in street resurfacing while critical city building roofs continue to deteriorate.
side_b_arguments: Fixing leaky roofs, including the $425,000 fleet maintenance building roof left out of the initial Priority 1 bundle, is a prudent move to prevent additional deterioration.
Staff acknowledged the street resurfacing money would not be spent this year aside from updating the street study.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; the City Manager agreed to return within two to three months after year-end closeout with carry-forward fund balance options.

conflicts.meeting_title: Special City Council Meeting - Southside Revitalization and City Council Work Session
conflicts.issue: Southside Revitalization / Rolling Hills Phase 1 Section 108 Loan and CDBG Exposure
conflicts.summary: Council Member Eugene Brown challenged staff's preferred option to finance Rolling Hills Phase 1 site preparation and infrastructure via a 20-year Section 108 loan backed by CDBG funds and non-CDBG city collateral, citing severe federal CDBG cut risks.
conflicts.side_a_position: Proceed as planned with Rolling Hills Phase 1 using a 20-year Section 108 loan ($3.9M for infrastructure) to leverage $48.5M in mixed-income redevelopment.
side_a_arguments: Proceeding as planned achieves the transformative RFQ objective, reconnects Rolling Hills to Southside, paves the way for Whitted School, Heritage Square, and Fayette Place, and addresses affordable rental housing needs.
Stretching the Section 108 loan to the 20-year maximum produces the lowest annual debt service obligation.
conflicts.side_b_position: Question or oppose locking the city into a 20-year CDBG-dependent Section 108 commitment collateralized by non-CDBG city funds.
side_b_arguments: A new Congressional majority already passed HR 1 in the House proposing a 62% cut to CDBG funding, which narrowly failed in the Senate.
If CDBG funding is cut or eliminated over the next 20 years, the city's non-CDBG collateral requirement would force Durham to pay roughly $750,000 per year out of local funds.
conflicts.resolution: Informational special meeting deliberation; no formal vote was taken on April 7, 2011 (the item later returned for formal action on May 2, 2011).

conflicts.issue: Placement and Scope of Matricula Consular Identification Resolution
conflicts.summary: While advocates and police leadership supported adopting a resolution recognizing the Matricula Consular as valid ID during minor traffic stops, Council Member Howard Clement III sought additional information and deferred action to the regular session General Business Agenda.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support recognizing the Matricula Consular as valid identification to improve policing efficiency and community trust.
side_a_arguments: Police officers wrote roughly 100 citations/year for minor offenses like driving without a license; accepting valid consular ID lets officers complete a stop in ~10 minutes instead of spending over two hours on jail transport.
Police Chief Lopez reviewed the proposal, officers retain full arrest discretion, and the Consulate provided Lexan tools to detect fraudulent cards.
conflicts.side_b_position: Defer final action to the regular session General Business Agenda for additional comparative data.
side_b_arguments: Questions remained about whether the Durham County Sheriff and other major North Carolina cities had adopted similar policies and how officers handle stops involving other non-licensed drivers such as 16-year-olds.
conflicts.resolution: Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden placed the item on the regular session General Business Agenda rather than voting in the work session.

conflicts.issue: Leasing vs. Purchasing Computer Equipment (Item 14 — ePlus Group)
conflicts.summary: Council Member Eugene Brown criticized spending roughly $377,000 over five years to lease 25 laptops and two workstations rather than purchasing them outright for ~$307,000.
conflicts.side_a_position: Budget capital purchases or alternative installment structures in future cycles to avoid paying a ~$70,000 leasing premium.
side_a_arguments: Paying $377,000 over five years for equipment priced at $307,000 costs the city roughly $70,000 more than buying outright.
conflicts.side_b_position: Use five-year leasing when upfront capital funds are unavailable in the departmental budget.
side_b_arguments: Leasing spreads payments at one-fifth per year when the department lacks lump-sum purchase funds upfront, and staff has also reduced computer costs by extending equipment lifecycles and renegotiating Dell pricing.
conflicts.resolution: Left for consideration in future Capital Improvements / operating budget deliberations without halting the pending item.

conflicts.issue: Beer and Wine Privilege License PAC Notification and Revenue Focus (Item 28)
conflicts.summary: Howard Clement III criticized the City's handling of 16 new beer and wine privilege license applications, arguing the City appeared overly focused on fee revenue while failing to route permit modifications and renewals to Partners Against Crime (PAC) districts.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the 16 privilege licenses under current statutory rules and address PAC notification processes during the upcoming budget review.
side_a_arguments: License issuance follows existing administrative requirements and can be acted on without delay.
Process changes for notifying PAC districts can be flagged for review during the budget process.
conflicts.side_b_position: Require stronger neighborhood/PAC review of alcohol permit renewals and modifications rather than prioritizing license revenue.
side_b_arguments: Only one of the 16 businesses had appeared before PAC 4.
The City makes it look as though it is only interested in collecting license fee income rather than supporting community oversight.
conflicts.resolution: Council flagged PAC notification procedures for review during the upcoming budget process and passed Item 28 by voice vote.

conflicts.issue: Timing, Stakeholder Consultation, and Governance Scope for Supplemental Item 19 (Homeless Prevention Plan)
conflicts.summary: Council members debated whether to suspend the rules and immediately authorize implementation of the City-County homeless prevention restructuring report before external stakeholders reviewed the draft or before resolving appointment discretion details.
conflicts.side_a_position: Suspend the rules and authorize staff immediately to advance accountability and conflict-of-interest reforms in homeless prevention.
side_a_arguments: The framework addresses long-standing accountability and conflict-of-interest challenges and establishes a solid base to put staff in place.
Opposition from those resistant to change is expected, and delaying further stalls contractual coordination with the county.
conflicts.side_b_position: Clarify whether affected stakeholders saw the proposal and avoid locking future Council appointment discretion into the document.
side_b_arguments: Members asked who had been party to the draft and cautioned against incorporating policy bullets that could restrict future Council appointment latitude.
Action should authorize contractual moves while bringing detailed governance recommendations back and coordinating with County Commissioners.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved unanimously by adopting the recommendation subject to parallel action by the Durham Board of County Commissioners at their April 4 work session.

conflicts.issue: Film Festival Beer and Wine Service Permit and Suspension of Rules
conflicts.summary: Following a speaker's request citing the film festival's 12-year track record of incident-free beer and wine service, Council split 6-1 on both suspending the rules to vote at the work session and approving the item.
conflicts.side_a_position: Suspend the rules and approve beer and wine service for the film festival.
side_a_arguments: Act in the interest of time at the work session.
Festival demonstrated a 12-year track record of beer and wine service without issue.
conflicts.side_b_position: Opposed suspending the rules and approving the item.
side_b_arguments: Single dissenting 'No' vote recorded by voice without floor remarks in the transcript.
conflicts.resolution: Both the procedural motion to suspend the rules and the main motion passed 6-1 by voice vote; individual member names were not identified in the transcript.

conflicts.issue: Item 17: Resolution Amending Southwest Durham Urban Growth Area (UGA) Boundary
conflicts.summary: Extended the UGA boundary west of NC 751 to include parcels from the 2006 Planning Director interpretation near the proposed 751 Assemblage project.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Passed 5-2)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Passed (5-2)

conflicts.issue: 751 Assemblage Utility Extension Agreement (Item 18) Timing and Litigation Hold
conflicts.summary: Council divided 6-1 over whether to refer the 751 Assemblage utility extension agreement back to the administration amid pending litigation and public controversy versus moving forward to mitigate developer economic and financing pressures.
conflicts.side_a_position: Refer Item 18 back to the administration until external litigation and procedural concerns are resolved cleanly.
side_a_arguments: Citizens felt the prior UGA and legal steps were manipulative and bombarded Council with emails questioning why the item was moving forward.
Council had already amended the UDO so similar UGA boundary disputes could not recur, and residents deserved a clean resolution.
conflicts.side_b_position: Avoid holding the project in abeyance due to economic development and bank financing pressures.
side_b_arguments: The property remained outside city jurisdiction pending annexation, and holding the agreement in abeyance played into opponents' hands while awaiting lawsuit resolution.
Delaying action carried economic implications and complicated loan refinancing in a difficult financing environment.
conflicts.resolution: Council voted 6-1 to refer Item 18 back to the administration (individual Aye and Nay member names were not identified in the transcript digest), with staff instructed to prepare an informational annexation fiscal report without scheduling formal public-hearing action.

conflicts.issue: Harvard Avenue Sidewalk Addition vs. Petitioned Sidewalk Backlog and School Sidewalk Priorities
conflicts.summary: Council members questioned using ~$650,000 in street-paving savings for a sidewalk on Harvard Avenue—not originally on the petition list—while six approved sidewalk petitions remained unfunded and the November street bond allocated zero dollars to sidewalks.
conflicts.side_a_position: Add the Harvard Avenue sidewalk now using existing paving contract savings and contingency.
side_a_arguments: Favorable construction bids left capacity inside the existing $650,000 project authorization.
Harvard Avenue has steep slopes and adjoining property grades that leave pedestrians with little room off the roadway, making it safer and more efficient to build while crews are already mobilized.
conflicts.side_b_position: Ensure equitable sidewalk funding priorities, address the six waiting approved petitions, and prioritize sidewalks near schools.
side_b_arguments: Harvard Avenue represented roughly 85% of a typical annual sidewalk budget while six approved petitions waited for funding.

The November street bond allocated 0% to sidewalks, and petition sidewalk funding ($100,000/year after a multi-year hiatus, at ~$50/linear foot) only covers about one multi-block project per year, leaving many schools without sidewalks.
conflicts.resolution: Staff agreed to return during the upcoming budget workshops with a comprehensive update on sidewalk funding, school sidewalk priorities, and high-pedestrian areas.

conflicts.issue: Advisory Board Term-Limit Policy on RDU Airport Authority Reappointment
conflicts.summary: Council members noted that the RDU Airport Authority reappointment was a second appointment beyond standard term limits and discussed referring term-limit rules to the Procedures Committee.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support the reappointment given strong performance as authority treasurer and lack of other applicants.
side_a_arguments: There were no competing applications, and the incumbent served effectively as treasurer for the authority.
conflicts.side_b_position: Review recurring term-limit exceptions through the Procedures Committee rather than repeatedly overriding policy ad hoc.
side_b_arguments: Repeatedly granting appointments beyond term limits warrants clarification by the Procedures Committee.
conflicts.resolution: Council cast 7 ballot votes for the appointment while concurring that term-limit procedures should be reviewed by the Procedures Committee.

conflicts.issue: Old North Durham Park Revised Master Plan — Public Input, Park Access, and Field Conditions
conflicts.summary: Residents and Council members criticized inadequate community input on the Old North Durham Park Revised Master Plan and questioned future access and control, leading Council to pull it from the upcoming agenda and send it back to the City Manager's Office.
conflicts.side_a_position: Adopt the revised master plan featuring a walking path, picnic shelter, and rainwater features while addressing drainage constraints.
side_a_arguments: Adopting the plan would not transfer ownership or public access away from the city, and a shallow diagonal storm drain limits heavy athletic-field grading without major capital funding.
conflicts.side_b_position: Refer the plan back to the City Manager's Office for inclusive PAC, InterNeighborhood Council, and neighborhood input.
side_b_arguments: Multiple residents testified they had no input into the proposed plan, indicating a flaw in the public outreach process.
Affirmative outreach through PACs and the InterNeighborhood Council is needed before Council acts on any master plan.
conflicts.resolution: Removed from the November 1 agenda and referred back to the City Manager's Office for further public engagement.

conflicts.meeting_title: Special City Council Meeting - Rolling Hills/Southside Redevelopment Initiative
conflicts.issue: Rolling Hills / Southside Redevelopment Financing Risk, Entitlement Concentration, and Rental-vs-Ownership Mix
conflicts.summary: During the nearly three-hour presentation and work session on the ~$19.8 million Southside tipping-point financing plan, Council members questioned staff and developers over financial risk, multi-year entitlement commitments, security planning, and the heavy proportion of rental units relative to homeownership.
conflicts.side_a_position: Concentrate public Section 108/HOME commitments and start with mixed-income rental phases to overcome neighborhood stigma and attract major private capital.
side_a_arguments: Investing ~$14 million in public funds could leverage ~$70 million in private investment into Southside.
Given disinvestment and stigma in the area, rental development was a necessary initial step to establish stability before broader ownership sales.
conflicts.side_b_position: Scrutinize financial exposure, protect momentum in other target neighborhoods, and prioritize higher homeownership shares and clear security planning.
side_b_arguments: Members worried heavy commitments to Southside could stall progress in Southwest Central Durham and recalled a prior failed venture costing the City $6–7 million.
Speakers argued the ratio of rental to ownership units was 'definitely off' and should be reversed, and requested clear security/policing plans and historical CDBG accountability.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken at the April 29 special meeting; the financing commitment returned for formal action as supplemental Item 25 at the May 3, 2010 regular meeting.

conflicts.issue: Item 39: Hope Valley Farms Zoning Map Change (with Three Proffered Committed Elements)
conflicts.summary: Rezoning approval including committed elements for a 36-inch masonry wall with landscaping, prohibiting restaurant drive-thru windows facing the southwest neighborhood, and prohibiting fuel sales/convenience stores.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Passed 5-2)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Passed (5-2)

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 22, 2011 City Council Work Session—opened by Mayor Bill Bell and later chaired by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden—the Council unanimously approved two excused absence motions, time-certain scheduling for five presentations, two closed-session attorney-client requests (including Weekly/Weakley v. City of Durham), and the City Clerk's request to refer October 20 work session minutes back for correction. During agenda review, Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden pulled Item 2 (Citizens Advisory Committee appointments) to hold for one cycle to review applicants for potential conflicts of interest. Budget Director Bertha Johnson presented the FY 2011–2012 First Quarter Financial Report showing property taxes up 16.9%, utility taxes up 5.3%, a $400,000 November sales tax gain, and $419,000 in personnel savings. Following a truncated middle section, Council reviewed the proposed Durham County Board of Health smoking ordinance—debating whether County rules automatically govern City property such as the Transportation Center or require a City Council resolution incorporating the County ordinance by reference—before unanimously setting the December 5 agenda and entering closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Excused Absences, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council opened with roll call and passed two unanimous voice votes excusing absent members (names garbled in ASR). Council then unanimously approved the City Manager's priority schedule for Items 24–26, 28, and 29, the City Attorney's request for two closed sessions (including Weekly/Weakley v. City of Durham under GS 143-318.11(a)(3)), and the City Clerk's request to refer the October 20, 2011 work session minutes back to the Clerk's office.

agenda_items.title: December 5 Draft Agenda Review and Citizens Advisory Committee Appointment Pull
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff read the draft December 5 agenda covering Items 6–26 and public hearings 30–31. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden pulled Item 2 (Citizens Advisory Committee appointment) to hold for one cycle to check applicants for potential conflicts of interest, and Council unanimously approved adding a street-acceptance priority item by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Item 24: FY 2011–2012 First Quarter Financial Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson presented the first-quarter financial report (July–September 2011), noting property taxes were up 16.9% year-over-year, utility taxes were up 5.3%, November sales tax collections rose $400,000, and projected personnel cost savings totaled $419,000.

agenda_items.title: Item 25: Proposed Durham County Board of Health Smoking Ordinance and Jurisdiction Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle section truncated in the transcript, public health staff presented proposed amendments to the 1993 smoking ordinance (covering building entryways, cigar bars, private clubs, and a three-month education campaign funded from home health agency sale proceeds). City Attorney's Office counsel Don O'Toole and County/Board of Health counsel Mr. Wardell expressed differing legal views on whether the County rule automatically applies to City property or requires a City Council resolution adopting it by reference under 2007–2010 state statutes, with City Manager Tom Bonfield directing staff to submit formal comments by mid-December.

agenda_items.title: Setting the December 5, 2011 Agenda and Motion to Enter Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, Council unanimously voted by voice vote to set the December 5 agenda (Consent Items 1, 3, 4, 6–23; GBA Items 2 and 27; GBA Public Hearings 30 and 31) and then voted unanimously to enter closed session.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 21, 2011 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council opened with recognitions for Omega Psi Phi Fraternity, city Public Affairs and Police Department communications awards, remarks by Howard Clement III on local court system rancor, and the swearing-in of Larry Dixon. Council unanimously (7-0) approved the consent agenda—excluding pulled Items 5, 12, and 21—covering the public art policy, financial reserve policies, Hillandale Golf Course transfer, and the Orange County Eno water/sewer interlocal agreement, and held a public hearing on a Yorktown Avenue sidewalk petition before a mid-transcript truncation. Following the gap, Council unanimously (7-0) designated the Golden Belt Manufacturing Complex as a local historic landmark, approved Item 5 (third-party claims administration via the NC League of Municipalities, 7-0) after requesting EEO/diversity verification, and passed Item 12 (Durham Walks unfunded sidewalk priority list) with a technical adjustment to segment #23. In the evening's final vote on Item 21 (Council ward redistricting), speaker Bill Kalkhof advocated Option A to keep Woodcroft and West Durham unified while deferring to Ward 2 Member Howard Clement III, who moved adoption of staff's original Option B, passing unanimously 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Proclamations, Awards, and City Attorney Priority Item
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order with all seven members present, and young scholars from Parkwood Elementary led the Pledge of Allegiance. Recognitions honored Omega Psi Phi Fraternity Achievement Week, Public Affairs and Police communications awards, Larry Dixon's swearing-in, and Rosalie Bachelli Hernandez, while Howard Clement III voiced concern over rancor in the local court system and the City Attorney noted a clarifying amendment to the Hillandale Golf Course management assignment on consent.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Excluding Pulled Items 5, 12, and 21)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously (7-0) approved the consent agenda excluding pulled Items 5, 12, and 21, enacting items including the public art policy, general fund and water/sewer reserve policies, the 2012 Council meeting schedule, the Orange County Eno economic development water/sewer interlocal agreement, the Hillandale Golf Course transfer, American Tobacco Trail funding and schedule, and JARC/New Freedom transit grants.

agenda_items.title: Item 16: Public Hearing to Order Sidewalk on Yorktown Avenue
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater Manager Ed Menel presented a petitioned 400-foot sidewalk resolution along Yorktown Avenue connecting Cornwallis Road and Martin Luther King, Jr. Boulevard. Tarlton West Homeowners Association Vice President Josh Hoot spoke in favor to improve safety for children waiting for school buses and transit riders; the vote occurred in the subsequent truncated segment.

agenda_items.title: Item 5 (Pulled): Third-Party Administrative Services (NC League of Municipalities)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After remarks critiquing workplace diversity hiring at the North Carolina League of Municipalities and asking the City Attorney to verify Equal Employment Opportunity requirements in city contracts, Council unanimously (7-0) approved Item 5.

agenda_items.title: Item 19: Golden Belt Manufacturing Complex Local Historic Landmark Designation (LD110001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Lisa Miller presented LD110001, an application by Keenan/Neen & Capital LLC to designate a portion of the Golden Belt manufacturing complex structures and land as a local historic landmark, noting unanimous Historic Preservation Commission recommendation. Following the public hearing, Council approved the designation 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 12 (Pulled): Durham Walks Pedestrian Plan Revised Rankings and Unfunded Sidewalk Priority List
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Diane Catotti moved a technical adjustment to item #23 near the bottom of the unfunded sidewalk construction priority list, clarifying that two Horton Road segments (#5 and #12) remained unaffected. Council opened and closed the vote on the adjusted item.

agenda_items.title: Item 21 (Pulled): City Council Ward Redistricting (Option B Adopted)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell reviewed the census redistricting process that produced staff Option B alongside two alternative maps (Options A and C). Speaker Bill Kalkhof urged Option A to keep Woodcroft in Ward 2 and West Durham neighborhoods together while deferring to Ward 2 Member Howard Clement III; Clement then endorsed and moved Option B (keeping Precinct 16 in Ward 3), which Council adopted unanimously 7-0.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved all unpulled consent agenda items by single 7-0 vote.

votes.notes: Mover and seconder not named in transcript digest.

votes.notes: Mover and seconder not named in transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved Item 5 after requesting City Attorney review of EEO contract language with NC League of Municipalities.

votes.notes: Vote was opened and closed at [02:25:09] without a spoken numerical tally in the transcript digest; all seven members were present and voted 7-0 on adjacent items.

votes.notes: Seconder not named in transcript digest.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 10, 2011 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, the Council opened with a quorum and unanimously passed an excused absence motion covering Eugene Brown and Howard Clement III by voice vote. Council approved the City Manager's priority items scheduling the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (BPAC) annual report and adding supplemental items on Duke Energy rate increases (Item 20) and ward redistricting (Item 21), though Council initially lacked the five votes needed to suspend rules for immediate action on Item 20. Council Members discussed Item 3 (public art policy procedures) and received the 2010–2011 BPAC annual report highlighting over 150 site-plan reviews and a request for a full-time bike/pedestrian coordinator. Following a mid-transcript truncation, Council revisited Item 20, unanimously voted to suspend the rules and adopt an amended resolution opposing Duke Energy electricity rate increases while urging the NC Utilities Commission to adopt equitable rates encouraging energy conservation and efficiency, reviewed Options A–C for ward redistricting (Item 21), and unanimously set the November 21 regular meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excused Absences (Brown and Clement), Staff Introduction, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the meeting to order with a quorum and Council unanimously approved an excused absence for Eugene Brown with a friendly amendment excusing Howard Clement III. Staff introduced new City Manager's Office addition Marcel Bronner, and Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (Item 15 BPAC report, Item 20 Duke Energy rate resolution, Item 21 redistricting update), while noting Council was one vote shy of suspending rules at the start of the session.

agenda_items.title: Draft Agenda Review and Item 3 Public Art Policy Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed the draft November 21 agenda (Items 2–21) and pulled Items 3 (public art policy), 9 (Hillandale Golf Course), 12 (sidewalk priority list), and 19 (Golden Belt landmark) for questions. Council Member Mike Woodard questioned Item 3 regarding procedures and advisory board vs. Council input before projects are finalized.

agenda_items.title: Item 15: Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (BPAC) Annual Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: BPAC presented its 2010–2011 accomplishments, reporting reviews of more than 150 site plans and 20 rezoning requests to ensure UDO sidewalk and bike-lane compliance, input on the NC 54 corridor study and Durham-Wake-Orange Transit Plan, and a 2012 goal requesting expansion of the half-time bicycle/pedestrian coordinator position to full-time.

agenda_items.title: Item 20: Resolution Opposing Duke Energy Electricity Rate Increases
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle section truncated in the transcript, discussion addressed Duke Energy's proposed rate increase (including street-lighting and base-load plant costs) ahead of a November 28 NC Utilities Commission hearing in which Durham is an intervenor. Council unanimously suspended the rules and adopted an amended resolution opposing the rate increase and urging the NC Utilities Commission to adopt equitable rate structures that encourage energy conservation and efficiency.

agenda_items.title: Item 21: Ward Redistricting Options (A, B, and C) and Setting the November 21 Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council and staff debated how to advance three redistricting maps (Options A, B, and C) for the November 21 regular meeting, with comments favoring Option A's unification of Watts Hospital and Old West Durham neighborhoods while agreeing to place the options on consent so Council or the public could pull them for a formal vote. Council then unanimously set the November 21 agenda by voice vote.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote; exact number of members present (quorum of 4, since they later noted being one shy of 5 to suspend rules) is not stated in a roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to excuse Eugene Brown, amended by friendly amendment to also excuse Howard Clement III.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Set 1:30 p.m. presentation for BPAC annual report and added supplemental items on Duke Energy rate increases and redistricting.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote; earlier at [00:04:24] Council noted needing five members to suspend rules, indicating at least five were present by this point in the meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to suspend Council rules to adopt the Duke Energy rate resolution ahead of the November 28 NC Utilities Commission hearing.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Amended Resolution Opposing Duke Energy Electricity Rate Increases
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted amended resolution urging the NC Utilities Commission to adopt equitable rate structures encouraging energy conservation and efficiency while opposing Duke Energy's proposed rate hike.

votes.item_title: Set the Agenda for the November 21, 2011 Regular City Council Meeting

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 20, 2011 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden (with Mayor Bell and Council Member Farad Ali expected shortly after opening), the Council unanimously approved an excused absence for Howard Clement III by voice vote. During agenda review, Council unanimously suspended the rules and approved Item 10, the Southside architect and engineering contract amendment for the Piedmont assemblage, while pulling Items 9, 16, and 22 (following a request regarding Hillandale Road waterline negotiations). Triangle Transit General Manager David King presented first-year oversight highlights for Durham Area Transit Authority (DATA), citing real-time bus arrival signs at Durham Station, 13 monthly rider feedback sessions, and $90,000 in capital upgrades. Following a mid-transcript truncation, Council heard updates on Southside Phase II tax-credit apartment scope changes, failed developments (including pothole repairs and Riverside repaving), NCDOT progress on the Alston Avenue widening project, City Attorney ward redistricting proposals (moving Precinct 13 from Ward 1 to Ward 2 without displacing any incumbents), watershed land-acquisition surcharge usage, and Arizona conference travel policy before unanimously setting the upcoming regular agenda.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excused Absence for Howard Clement III, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the work session to order, noting Mayor Bell and Farad Ali would arrive shortly, and Council unanimously excused Howard Clement III by voice vote. The City Manager presented priority items requesting immediate action on Item 10 (Southside contract amendment) and scheduling Item 26 (Triangle Transit oversight report), and a Council member requested an update on the Alston Avenue widening project.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Item 10 (Southside Architect/Engineering Contract Amendment)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During agenda review, Council unanimously suspended the rules and approved Item 10, the Southside architect and engineering contract amendment in the Piedmont assemblage. Council also pulled Items 9 (FY 2010–2011 budget carryover), 16 (failed developments update), and 22 (Hillandale Road dual water line replacement phase 2, after an attorney asked to keep it off Monday's consent agenda pending staff talks).

agenda_items.title: Item 26: Triangle Transit First-Year Oversight Report on DATA Transit Services
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Triangle Transit's David King reviewed first-year oversight accomplishments for DATA, including real-time bus arrival displays at Durham Station, renewing the DATA Pride Ambassador program, holding 13 monthly 7 p.m. customer meetings at Durham Station, building in-house financial and transit management capacity, and investing $90,000 in capital improvements such as fencing at the Fay Street maintenance facility.

agenda_items.title: Updates on Southside Phase II, Failed Developments, and Alston Avenue Widening
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle segment, Interim Community Development Director Reginald Johnson explained NC Housing Finance Agency rule changes required scaling down Southside Phase II tax-credit apartments. Public Works staff reported no new failed developments, near-completion of pothole repairs, stormwater bond collection efforts, and Riverside repaving, while Transportation Director Mark Ahrendsen reported positive progress with NCDOT on the Alston Avenue widening project.

agenda_items.title: Item 23: Ward Redistricting Update, Water-Rate Surcharge, Arizona Travel Resolution, and Setting the Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Attorney presented ward redistricting maps keeping each ward within 5% of one-third of population without splitting precincts—moving Precinct 13 from Ward 1 to Ward 2 while keeping all incumbents in their existing wards. meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 17, 2011 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with six members present, the Council unanimously (6-0) approved an excused absence for Council Member Howard Clement III. Mayor Bell presented a proclamation honoring Jennifer Forsyth and Jill Cranwinkle for their heroic compassion after a fatal July 5, 2011 wrong-way crash on US 64 near Rocky Mount, joined by the McLaughlin family of El Paso, Texas, while Council Member Farad Ali thanked Durham Police for arresting a suspect in a fatal IHOP shooting. Acting on Mayor Bell's priority item, Council unanimously (6-0) adopted two resolutions endorsing the countywide November 8 ballot referendums for a quarter-cent education sales tax and a half-cent public transportation sales tax after the City Attorney confirmed legal authority for endorsing county-sponsored referendums. Council then unanimously (6-0) approved the consent agenda (Items 1–13), Item 17 (Continuum of Care funding recommendations, 6-0), and Item 15 (initial Residential Rural and Falls/Jordan B translational zoning for 12 newly annexed acres at 809 Scott King Road, 6-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Excused Absence for Howard Clement III, Proclamation, and Council Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order (inadvertently saying April 17 before reading October 17 in the proclamation) with six members present (Bell, Cole-McFadden, Ali, Brown, Catotti, and Woodard), and Council voted 6-0 to excuse Howard Clement III. Mayor Bell honored Jennifer Forsyth and Jill Cranwinkle alongside James and Joan McLaughlin of El Paso, Texas for aiding victims of a July 5 US 64 crash, Farad Ali thanked Durham Police for making an arrest in an IHOP shooting and recognized White Rock Baptist Church's 255th group, and Cora Cole-McFadden thanked Project Homeless Connect volunteers.

agenda_items.title: Mayor's Priority Item: Resolutions Endorsing November 8 Countywide Education and Transit Sales Tax Referendums
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell introduced two City Attorney-drafted resolutions endorsing the November 8, 2011 Durham County ballot referendums for a quarter-cent local sales and use tax for public education and a half-cent local sales and use tax for public transportation. After the City Attorney confirmed Council could legally endorse county-sponsored referendums, Council Member Mike Woodard moved adoption with minor typo corrections and Council passed both resolutions 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items 1–13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read Consent Agenda Items 1–13, including board/committee appointments, Amerinational mortgage loan servicing extension, fair housing contract, law enforcement reimbursement and firearms analysis apprenticeship funds, Governor's Highway Safety grant, NCSU Triangle Regional Model agreement, sewer lift station rehab, and Raleigh interconnection project amendment #1. Council approved the consent agenda 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 17: Continuum of Care Funding Recommendation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved approval of Item 17, the Continuum of Care funding recommendation, and later thanked Citizens Advisory Committee Chair Dewarren Langley for his committee's work on the application process. Council approved the item 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 15: Initial Zoning Map Change at 809 Scott King Road (Z1100007A/B)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Steve Medlin presented initial translational zoning for a 12-acre parcel at 809 Scott King Road annexed October 3, 2011, recommending Residential Rural and Falls/Jordan B protected watershed overlay matching county zoning and the Comprehensive Plan. Following a public hearing with no speakers, Council approved the zoning 6-0 before adjourning at 7:20 p.m.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 6, 2011 City Council Work Session, Mayor Bill Bell opened the meeting after closed session, heard citizen remarks on poverty and workforce issues, and received staff news of a Transportation Department employee killed in a car accident. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority agenda requests (referring Item 10, the Sonoco recycling contract amendment, back to administration and prioritizing Item 14, the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority annual report), heard an RDU update highlighting Terminal 2's opening, 9.1 million 2010 passengers, and a newly hired airport director, and reviewed the December 11 Triangle Expressway segment opening. Council also questioned Interim Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and Durham Housing Authority CEO Dallas Parks on supplemental Item 17 (Continuum of Care funding recommendations, including a 10-6 split vote at the external Homeless Services Advisory Committee) and discussed legal and utility-planning implications of Durham County's proposed sewer extension to the 751 South project under the 1972 boundary practice. Council concluded with 7-0 ballot votes for Convention & Visitors Bureau Authority and Workforce Development Board appointments and unanimously settled the upcoming regular agenda, with no split or contested Council votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Citizens' Matters, and Staff Announcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:16 p.m. following a closed session and thanked Faith Jones for leading the Pledge of Allegiance on Monday night. A resident (Ralph) addressed Council for three minutes on generational poverty, schools, and Durham's workforce environment, and staff reported that a Transportation Department employee had died in an East Durham car accident that morning with two small children seriously injured.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items and Consent Agenda Readout
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested referring Item 10 (Sonoco recycling contract amendment #1) back to administration due to a discrepancy between the agenda and memo recommendations, flagged supplemental Item 17 (Continuum of Care funding recommendations), requested an end-of-meeting discussion on County sewer service extension to 751 South, and recommended hearing Item 14 (RDU Airport Authority) first. Council unanimously approved the priority items by voice vote and read through Consent Items 1–13 and Public Hearing Item 15 (Scott King Road initial zoning Z1100007B).

agenda_items.title: Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority (RDU) Annual Report and Triangle Expressway Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: An RDU Airport Authority presenter reported that Terminal 2 opened January 23, 2011 and was operating efficiently with 10 major airlines, 37 destinations, 200 daily departures, and 9.1 million passengers in 2010 (1.5% growth, the first increase since 2007). He noted RDU was ranked second most efficient in the U.S. by airline operating cost, announced a new airport director to be introduced Monday at 4:30 p.m., highlighted the new pre-security USO facility, and reviewed the Triangle Expressway opening in Durham County on December 11 (with transponders on sale October 11 and Phase 2 to Holly Springs opening August 2012).

agenda_items.title: Continuum of Care (CoC) Funding Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and staff explained HUD's transition to annual renewals and competitive allocation of remaining funds, while Council questioned why the Homeless Services Advisory Committee had a 10-6 split vote and why Transitions to Permanence scored seven points under HUD priorities. Staff explained that evaluation lacked collaboration letters of support at the time of review and outlined HUD priorities for chronic, veteran, and family homelessness, while Durham Housing Authority CEO Dallas Parks addressed rental versus homeownership aspects.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of Durham County Sewer Extension to the 751 South Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and attorneys from the City Attorney's Office (Patrick and Don) reviewed the urban growth boundary, water/sewer rate structures east of Research Triangle Park, and the longstanding 1972 utility boundary practice with Durham County. Speakers noted that even if the County extended sewer service in violation of historical practice, developments would likely still need to seek City water service unless they relied on private or community wells.

agenda_items.title: Board/Commission Appointments and Settling the Regular Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ballot results confirmed seven votes each for Ron Hanna and Deanna Crossman to be reappointed to the Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau Authority, and seven votes each for George Hining and Marilyn Rochelle to be appointed to the Workforce Development Board. Council then unanimously voted to set the upcoming regular agenda (Consent Items 1–9 and 11–13, GBA Item 17, and GBA Public Hearing Item 15) and adjourned.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Manager's Priority Items (Refer Item 10 Back, Reorder Item 14, Add Supplemental Item 17 and 751 Sewer Discussion)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote; mover and seconder not named in transcript digest. Later 7-vote ballot tallies indicate all seven seated members participated in the meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the City Manager's requests to refer Item 10 back to administration, take Item 14 first after consent readout, add Item 17 as a supplemental item, and discuss the 751 South sewer extension.

votes.item_title: Appointments to Durham Convention & Visitors Bureau Authority (Ron Hanna, Deanna Crossman) and Workforce Development Board (George Hining, Marilyn Rochelle)
votes.notes: Seven votes cast out of seven seated Council members.
votes.discussion_detail: Ballot totals announced at the work session confirmed seven votes each for all four appointees.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeeting
meetings.executive_summary: With Mayor Bill Bell and Council Member Howard Clement III excused (approved 5-0), Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presided over the October 3, 2011 Regular City Council Meeting and opened with four proclamations, including National Disability Employment Awareness Month and Project Homeless Connect Day. Council unanimously (5-0) approved the Consent Agenda covering audits, fuel contracts, Series 2011 private-placement financing, a Central Warrant Control interlocal agreement with Durham County, an NCDOT culvert agreement for University Drive, Teer Quarry raw water storage engineering, and the failed and struggling developments update. On the General Business Agenda, Council voted 5-0 to adopt Item 26 calling on Congress to redirect military spending to domestic priorities, voted 5-0 after a public hearing on Item 18 to extend the PSNC Energy natural gas franchise through September 30, 2012, and voted 5-0 after a public hearing on Item 21 to approve the Scott King Road voluntary annexation petition. All five recorded votes were unanimous among the five members present, with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, Roll Call, and Excused Absences
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the meeting to order, held a moment of silence, and invited Duke School student Faith Jones to lead the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll call confirmed five members present (Cole-McFadden, Ali, Brown, Catotti, and Woodard), and Council voted 5-0 to grant excused absences to Mayor Bill Bell and Council Member Howard Clement III.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations: National Disability Employment Awareness Month, Project Homeless Connect Day, and Infrastructure Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council presented four proclamations, recognizing October 2011 as National Disability Employment Awareness Month (received by committee chair Mark Roth) and proclaiming Project Homeless Connect Day (noting 500–600 homeless residents on any given night). Remarks also highlighted national water and sewer infrastructure needs.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1–3, 5–10, 12–17, 19)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no priority items from the City Manager or City Clerk and no items pulled by Council or the public, the chair read the Consent Agenda, including the Durham Housing Authority appointment, August 2011 bid and collections audits, WIA adult/dislocated worker contract amendment, gasoline and diesel fuel bids, Series 2011 private-placement financing, Central Warrant Control interlocal agreement, failed developments update, University Drive NCDOT culvert agreement, and Teer Quarry raw water storage engineering. Council approved the Consent Agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Calling on Congress to Redirect Military Spending to Domestic Priorities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered General Business Agenda Item 26, a resolution urging Congress to redirect federal military spending toward domestic priorities. Without debate, Council approved the resolution 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: PSNC Energy Natural Gas Franchise Renewal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater Manager Ed Venable presented the Public Works recommendation to extend the existing Public Service Company of North Carolina (PSNC Energy) natural gas franchise until September 30, 2012. No Council questions or public hearing speakers came forward, and Council approved the extension 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Voluntary Annexation Petition — Scott King Road
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Robin Bibby of Budget Management Services presented the administration's recommendation to adopt a voluntary annexation petition for the Scott King Road residential development in southern Durham. Project engineer Jared Aiden appeared at the public hearing to answer questions (none were asked), and Council approved the annexation 5-0 before closing remarks on MED Week, early voting, and adjournment.
