meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden opened the September 22, 2011 City Council Work Session while Mayor Bill Bell attended a community resolution presentation for Geneva Dillard, and Council unanimously excused Council Member Farad Ali's absence. During Citizens' Matters, Council heard testimony and staff updates on Stonehill Estates (currently in bond/surety litigation over unfinished asphalt, sidewalks, manholes, and stormwater work) and on the InterNeighborhood Council / Duke Park Preservation request for a $600,000 capital commitment to renovate the closed Duke Park bathhouse community center, which staff referred to the upcoming CIP budget cycle. Council approved the City Manager's and City Attorney's priority items (including moving PSNC franchise Item 18 to a public hearing, adding Southside revitalization supplemental Item 25, and scheduling closed sessions), reviewed SDBE reciprocity with NCDOT, HUD Section 3 hiring preferences, and JobLink/OEWD workforce training for Southside East and West, and discussed a template resolution on redirecting military spending and technical questions for Durham County on its 751 sewer proposal. Council concluded by recording David Haley's 5-0 ballot reappointment to the Durham Housing Authority Board of Commissioners, unanimously settling the October 3 agenda, and entering closed session, with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Excused Absence for Farad Ali
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden opened the work session, noting Mayor Bill Bell was presenting a resolution for Geneva Dillard of Dillard's Barbecue and would join afterward. Following roll call, Council voted unanimously by voice vote to grant Council Member Farad Ali an excused absence.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matters: Stonehill Estates Failed Subdivision Litigation and Repairs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A Stonehill Estates resident (noting Council Member Eugene Brown had previously visited to photograph conditions) raised safety concerns after a visitor broke her leg tripping over a manhole cover. Public Works staff explained that Stonehill Estates is in active litigation over bond and surety amounts, and while streets and sidewalks remain passable, final asphalt lift, base course repairs, sidewalk work, valve/manhole adjustments, and stormwater facilities remain incomplete.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matters: Duke Park Bathhouse and Community Center Renovation Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Representing the InterNeighborhood Council and neighborhood advocates, Mr. Anderson asked Council to pull back a draft lease and commit $600,000 in the upcoming budget cycle toward renovating the Duke Park bathhouse, citing Inspector Tony Alderman's finding that the structure was sound aside from plumbing, floor work, and lead-paint abatement. Staff noted the facility was closed as unsafe, DPPI had not yet raised matching funds, and any $600,000 commitment would be evaluated through the upcoming CIP and budget process.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items: PSNC Public Hearing Correction, Southside Update, and Closed Session Requests
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager flagged that Item 18 (PSNC Energy franchise renewal) should be a public hearing rather than consent, added supplemental Item 25 (Southside revitalization update), noted the Mayor's request to discuss a military-spending redirection resolution, and requested a real-property closed session (NCGS 143-318.11(a)(5)). The City Attorney requested a litigation closed session for Frankie Washington v. Tracy Cline et al. (NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3)), and both priority slates passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Southside Regional Revitalization Project: SDBE, HUD Section 3, and Workforce Strategy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle transcript gap, staff including Deborah Giles, Interim Community Development Director Reginald Johnson, and OEWD Director Kevin Dick briefed Council on SDBE certification reciprocity with NCDOT, HUD Section 3 hiring priorities (directing jobs first to certified Southside residents under 80%/50% AMI guidelines), and an on-site Section 3 coordinator funded by OEWD. Staff confirmed these rules apply to both McCormick Baron Salazar (Southside East) and Self-Help (Southside West) and noted on-the-job maintenance training and an October 6 culinary training graduation.

agenda_items.title: Military-Spending Resolution Template and Durham County 751 Sewer Proposal Memo
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council agreed to prepare a city-formatted version of the U.S. Conference of Mayors resolution on redirecting military spending to domestic priorities for the upcoming regular agenda. Council Member Mike Woodard also questioned staff on the city's memo seeking technical information from Durham County regarding its 751 sewer proposal, including whether alignments could use NCDOT rights-of-way rather than city rights-of-way.

agenda_items.title: Durham Housing Authority Reappointment, Agenda Setting, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ballot results confirmed five votes for David Haley's reappointment to the Durham Housing Authority Board of Commissioners. Council then voted unanimously by voice vote to settle the October 3, 2011 regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1–3, 5–17, and 19; GBA Item 26; GBA Public Hearings 18 and 21) and voted unanimously to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Council Member Farad Ali
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Granted Council Member Farad Ali's request for an excused absence.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Manager's Priority Items
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Corrected Item 18 to public hearing, added supplemental Item 25 (Southside), noted the military-spending resolution, and added a real-property closed session.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Attorney's Priority Items (Closed Session — Frankie Washington v. Tracy Cline et al.)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Added closed session for attorney-client consultation pursuant to NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3).

votes.notes: Farad Ali was excused; exact subset of five voting members among the remaining six was not read aloud in the digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Ballot count announced as five votes for David Haley's reappointment.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session for property acquisition and litigation matters.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Bill Bell opened the September 8, 2011 City Council Work Session with six members present (Mike Woodard absent/excused), announced that Council had completed evaluations for the City Clerk and City Manager (including an August 14 unanimous vote extending the City Manager's contract to August 1, 2016) while continuing the City Attorney's evaluation to September 19, and handed the chair to Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden before departing to attend President Obama's address to Congress with Congressman Butterfield. Council unanimously approved priority items, heard a City Manager update that recent rainfall lifted reservoir capacity from 70% to roughly 82% and averted water restrictions for the week, and suspended the rules to unanimously adopt Item 4 commemorating the 10th anniversary of September 11. Following a truncated middle section covering Southside Rental Phase One pre-development costs, Council reviewed the FY 2010–11 fourth-quarter financial report across enterprise and special funds (Transit, Solid Waste, Stormwater, Parking, Ballpark, DPAC, and the new Debt Reserve Fund) and received an update from Transportation Director Mark Ahrendsen and staff on American Tobacco Trail I-40 bridge bid and funding options. Council concluded by unanimously settling the upcoming regular agenda and entering closed session, with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Appointed Officer Evaluation Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:01 p.m. with six members present (Council Member Mike Woodard had a previously approved excused absence) and asked Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden to conduct the remainder of the meeting after 1:30–1:45 p.m. Mayor Bell announced that Council had completed performance evaluations for the City Clerk and City Manager—unanimously extending the City Manager's contract to August 1, 2016 with additional community-event expense funds—and continued the City Attorney's evaluation to September 19 at 5:30 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items and Reservoir Water Supply Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously accepted priority items from the City Manager (pulling Item 5 on Southside Rental Phase One for early discussion, scheduling Q4 financial and tax settlement presentations, and adding an American Tobacco Trail I-40 bridge update), the City Attorney (attorney-client closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3)), and the City Clerk (referring Item 1 minutes back and suspending rules for Item 4). The City Manager reported that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain raised reservoir capacity from ~70% to ~82%, above the 75% restriction threshold.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matters and Transit Outreach Update (DATA / TTA Route Changes)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following citizen comments on national readiness and workforce training, Council heard an update on DATA/TTA transit route changes after residents raised concerns at a Durham Station outreach meeting. Staff reported that TTA agreed to meet with affected residents over the next two weeks to explore options.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Recognizing the 10th Anniversary of September 11 National Moment of Remembrance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because Council would not hold another regular meeting before September 11, Council voted unanimously by voice vote to suspend the rules and adopt Item 4 recognizing the City of Durham joining the national moment of remembrance.

agenda_items.title: Southside Rental Phase One Pre-Development Costs (McCormick Baron Salazar)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The chair introduced Item 5 regarding public and private pre-development costs for Southside Rental Phase One with McCormick Baron Salazar immediately before a truncated middle gap in the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: FY 2010–11 Fourth-Quarter Financial Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget staff presented year-end results across major city funds: Transit ($15.9M revenues vs. $16.0M expenditures, 9.4% fixed-route ridership growth), Solid Waste ($20.0M revenues vs. $21.8M expenditures due to consolidation accounting and diesel prices), Stormwater ($63,000 surplus to fund balance), Parking ($331,000 fund balance draw vs. $400,000 budgeted), Ballpark ($140,000 surplus to fund balance), DPAC (revenues above budget with no fund balance draw needed), and the newly separated Debt Reserve Fund ($24M property tax revenue). Staff projected departments spending within appropriation while noting unemployment remained a concern for sales tax growth.

agenda_items.title: American Tobacco Trail I-40 Bridge Bid Update, Agenda Setting, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Director Mark Ahrendsen and staff briefed Council on NCDOT communications and options for lowering construction costs on the American Tobacco Trail I-40 bridge bid, with Council members indicating support for moving forward to rebid within budget constraints. Council then voted unanimously to settle the regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 2, 3, 6–10, and 12–20; GBA Item 11) and voted unanimously to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Manager's Priority Items
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved priority scheduling for Item 5, Q4 financial report, tax settlement, and ATT I-40 bridge update.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Attorney's Priority Items (Closed Session)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Added closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3).

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Clerk's Priority Items (Refer Item 1 Back, Suspend Rules on Item 4)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Referred Item 1 minutes back to the Clerk's office and placed Item 4 for same-day rule suspension.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Vote on Item 4 (9/11 10th Anniversary Resolution)
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended work-session rules to act on Item 4 before September 11.

votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted resolution commemorating the 10th anniversary of September 11, 2001.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session for attorney-client consultation.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 6, 2011 Regular City Council Meeting with all seven members present, Mayor Bill Bell presented proclamations for Constitution Week, Durham's third consecutive Playful City USA designation, and National Recovery Month, while the City Manager announced the city was entering Phase 1 water restrictions through at least late October. Council voted unanimously (7-0) across every action item: accepting priority agenda adjustments, referring Rochelle Araujo's Environmental Affairs Board appointment back to the Clerk's office due to an EPA conflict of interest, approving the Consent Agenda (excluding pulled Items 8, 9, and 10), adopting Item 17 to amend the 2010–2015 Consolidated Plan and 2011–2012 Annual Action Plan for Neighborhood Revitalization Strategy Area (NRSA) flexibility and CDBG Section 108 loan eligibility, and approving supplemental Item 22 for an RDU International Airport FAA development grant. Council also voted 7-0 on pulled Community Development items—Item 8 (CDBG Section 108 loan application), Item 9 ($950,000 Neighborhood Stabilization Program 3 grant ordinance), and Item 10 (consolidating Self-Help NSP subrecipient contracts)—after residents and advocates raised questions about minority contractor and workforce participation in Southside revitalization, with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Proclamations (Constitution Week, Playful City USA, Recovery Month)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m., Council Member Howard Clement III led the Pledge of Allegiance, and roll call confirmed all seven members present. Proclamations were presented for Constitution Week (Sept. 17–23, Daughters of the American Revolution), KaBOOM!'s Playful City USA designation (third consecutive year), and National Recovery Month.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items, Phase 1 Water Restrictions Announcement, and Withdrawal of Item 2 Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to approve the City Manager's priority items (hearing Item 8 after Public Hearing Item 17 and adding supplemental Item 22, an RDU FAA grant offer), while the City Manager announced Phase 1 water restrictions would take effect and remain at least until the end of October. Council then voted 7-0 to refer Item 2 (Rochelle Araujo's Environmental Affairs Board nomination) back to the Clerk's office after she withdrew due to an EPA conflict of interest.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1, 3–5, 7, 11–13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell pulled Items 8, 9, and 10 for separate discussion. Council voted 7-0 to approve the remaining Consent Agenda items, including minutes, board appointments (City-County Affairs, BPAC, DOST), the mortgage loan portfolio semi-annual report, a 2011 Carolina Panthers Charities grant, FY 2011–12 stormwater CIP amendment, and an Obie Drive floodplain/FEMA permitting contract amendment.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Amendments to 2010–2015 Consolidated Plan and 2011–2012 Annual Action Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and Federal Programs Coordinator Wilma Conyers presented substantial HUD plan amendments to establish a Neighborhood Revitalization Strategy Area (NRSA) for job-creation documentation flexibility and to authorize a CDBG Section 108 loan application. No citizens spoke at the public hearing, and Council approved the amendments 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Raleigh-Durham International Airport FAA Grant Offer for Airport Development
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed supplemental Item 22 accepting an FAA airport development grant offer and inquired about the scope of work and minority/disadvantaged business participation on the contract awarded to Harper Construction Company of Kentucky. Council approved the grant offer 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Section 108 Loan Application
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers Victoria Peterson, Phil Jackson, and Durham Affordable Housing Coalition interim executive director Aloresa Sivol raised concerns regarding local hiring, minority business percentages, and stakeholder coordination for Southside redevelopment. Council approved the Section 108 loan application 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Stabilization Program 3 (NSP3) Grant Project Ordinance ($950,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development staff member Larry Jarvis explained the grant project ordinance recognizing $950,000 in NSP3 funds and clarified in response to Victoria Peterson that contractors already working in Southside were Durham-based firms. Council approved the ordinance 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Amendment to Subrecipient Contract with Center for Community Self-Help (NSP)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained the amendment consolidates two NSP contracts with Self-Help into a single contract, retaining Self-Help as acquisition agent while routing Southwest Central Durham parcels through an allocations committee for any interested nonprofit. Following brief discussion of Salem Street transitional housing and training, Council approved the amendment 7-0 and Mayor Bell affirmed his commitment to substantial minority participation on Southside Rolling Hills before adjourning at 8:04 p.m.

votes.notes: Electronic vote passed 7-0 with all seven members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Reordered Item 8 after Item 17 and added supplemental Item 22.

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted HUD Consolidated Plan and Annual Action Plan amendments after public hearing with no speakers.

votes.discussion_detail: Accepted FAA grant offer with Harper Construction Company contract.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved CDBG Section 108 loan application following public comments.

votes.discussion_detail: Recognized receipt of $950,000 in NSP3 grant funds.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - 751 South Voluntary Annexation Project and City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 18, 2011 Special City Council Meeting and Work Session, Mayor Bill Bell convened a 10:00 a.m. follow-up to the June 27 special meeting on the 751 South voluntary annexation request, where Budget Management Services staff (Robin Bibby) and Transportation staff (Wesley Parham) presented revised fiscal break-even projections (Scenario A in FY 2014–15 versus Scenario B in FY 2016–17) and explained why corridor-wide NC 751 widening was excluded from the rezoning traffic study and fiscal break-even tables. Following a truncated middle section, Council received the Durham Performing Arts Center (DPAC) Season 3 recap and community-outreach report showing regional ticket draw, 96% patron return intent, and 340+ complimentary student tickets through the Books to Broadway library program. During the work session portion, Council unanimously suspended the rules to approve Items 14 and 15, heard Public Works updates from Ed Venable on failed subdivisions (pothole repairs and completed repair cost estimates) and NCDOT's sudden requirement to rebid the American Tobacco Trail I-40 bridge, recorded 4-0 ballot votes for Environmental Affairs, Bicycle & Pedestrian, and Open Space & Trails appointments, and unanimously settled the next regular agenda before moving into closed session, with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: 751 South Voluntary Annexation Project — Financial and Transportation Impact Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell opened the 10:00 a.m. special meeting to review staff responses to Council's June 27 questions on the 751 South voluntary annexation. Robin Bibby of Budget Management Services presented Scenario A (FY 2014–15 break-even, viewed as unlikely) and Scenario B (FY 2016–17 break-even, front-loading police beat and fire station costs into year one of annexation), while Transportation staff Wesley Parham explained why NC 751 segment widening was not required in the UDO traffic impact study despite cumulative traffic from Jordan at Southpoint and Westpoint at 751. Council members pressed staff on buildout timing, paratransit costs, and the exclusion of road-widening costs from positive fiscal projections.

agenda_items.title: Durham Performing Arts Center (DPAC) Third Season Annual Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, DPAC management presented a recap of its third season and fourth-season preview, sharing regional zip-code attendance maps, reader-choice awards (Independent Weekly, Herald-Sun, Metro Magazine), and a 96% patron likelihood-to-return rating. Presenters also highlighted outreach programs, including Blue Man Group school drumming workshops, $6,500 raised for Prevent Child Abuse NC via Shrek, and over 340 complimentary Broadway tickets provided to students through Books to Broadway.

agenda_items.title: Work Session Rule Suspensions and Approval of Items 14 and 15
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the Mayor's request to return to requested items 14 and 15, Council voted unanimously by voice vote to suspend the rules and approve Item 14, and then voted unanimously by voice vote to suspend the rules and approve Item 15.

agenda_items.title: Failed and Struggling Developments and American Tobacco Trail I-40 Bridge Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater Manager Ed Venable reported no newly added failed subdivisions, noted city crews completed pothole repairs in three developments and finished street/stormwater repair cost estimates, and said staff would coordinate with the City Attorney's Office on funding and liable parties. On the ATT I-40 bridge, Venable reported NCDOT reversed earlier expectations within the past two weeks and required rebidding; staff was evaluating whether foreign steel (unlikely to yield the required 25% project savings) or median lane closures could reduce costs.

agenda_items.title: Board Appointments, Agenda Setting, and Motion to Enter Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ballot results showed applicants for the Affairs Commission, Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission, and Open Space and Trails Commission each received four votes. Council clarified Item 6 (DPAC report) was received rather than placed on consent, unanimously settled the upcoming regular agenda (Consent Items 1–5 and 7–13; GBA Public Hearing Item 17), and moved to enter closed session.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present at the August 15, 2011 Regular City Council Meeting, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden and staff inducted members of the Durham Youth Commission, Mayor Bell reported on an August 10 criminal justice coordination meeting with the District Attorney, Police Chief, City Manager, and Chief District Court Judge, and Council unanimously (7-0) approved the Consent Agenda (including board appointments, street acceptance, a sodium contract, and delinquent sewer-only disconnection/reconnection fees). On GBA Item 11 (Ban the Box), the City Manager and City Attorney reported that Durham's administrative policy deferring criminal background checks until a job offer was stronger than Philadelphia's ordinance while NC law barred citywide private-employer mandates, whereas Durham Second Chance Alliance attorney Daryl Atkinson urged an ordinance covering city employees and contractors akin to the living wage ordinance under NCGS 160A-174 and 160A-164.2. Following a truncated middle section, Council concluded public hearings on Items 21 and 22 (Ample Storage Center on Club Boulevard, approving both the Comprehensive Plan amendment despite staff's denial recommendation and the companion rezoning Z1000012 by 7-0 votes after neighborhood support and an 8-4 Planning Commission recommendation). Council also voted 7-0 on Items 23, 24, and 25 to adopt initial city zonings for newly annexed Bivins Road, NC 54, and I-40 rights-of-way, with no split or contested Council votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Youth Commission Induction, and Criminal Justice Meeting Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with all seven members present. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden led the induction of new Durham Youth Commission members, and Mayor Bell reported on his August 10 meeting with judicial, prosecutorial, and police leadership regarding bond and probation issues.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1–10, 12)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Items 11 and 13 on the General Business Agenda and Items 15–25 set as public hearings, Council approved the Consent Agenda 7-0, including DCVB/TDA, Convention Center Authority, and Citizens Advisory Committee appointments, the June 2011 bid report, street acceptance, a sodium contract, and a disconnection/reconnection process and fee schedule for delinquent sewer-only and fixed sewer accounts.

agenda_items.title: Update on 'Ban the Box' Administrative Policy vs. Municipal Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager and City Attorney explained that Durham lacked home-rule authority to impose Philadelphia's private-sector Ban the Box ordinance citywide, while Durham's existing hiring practice (deferring background checks until a conditional offer) went further than Philadelphia's pre-interview standard. Attorney Daryl Atkinson of Durham Second Chance Alliance clarified the group sought an ordinance for city employees and contractors modeled on Durham's living wage ordinance under NCGS 160A-174 and 160A-164.2; the City Attorney confirmed Council had legal authority to codify city personnel rules by ordinance if it chose to depart from past practice, before a transcript gap.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Comprehensive Plan Amendment — Ample Storage Center (A1000009)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle section, Council concluded the public hearing on amending the Future Land Use Map for less than an acre fronting Club Boulevard (recommended for denial by Planning staff under UDO 3.4.7, but recommended for approval 8-4 by the Planning Commission). K&L Gates attorney Lewis Cheek, Northgate Park resident Mike Shiflet, and adjacent business owner Jeff Roach supported the change, citing neighborhood backing and commitments restricting the site to self-storage; Council approved the amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change — Ample Storage Center (Z1000012)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Scott Whiteman presented the companion rezoning case (consistent with the newly amended Comprehensive Plan and recommended 8-4 by the Planning Commission on June 14). Applicant attorney Craig Sanders confirmed text and architectural commitments limiting use exclusively to self-storage, and Council approved the rezoning 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Initial Zoning — Bivins Road Right-of-Way (Z1100012B)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented an initial city zoning of RS-20, PDR 2.0, and PDR 2.02 for newly annexed Bivins Road right-of-way as a direct translation of county zoning, recommended by staff and the Planning Commission. With no public speakers, Council approved the zoning 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Initial Zoning — NC 54 Right-of-Way (Z1100013)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented an initial city zoning of PDR 9.4 and RS-10 for newly annexed NC 54 right-of-way matching existing county zoning, recommended by staff and the Planning Commission. With no public speakers, Council approved the zoning 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Initial Zoning — I-40 Right-of-Way (Z1100014)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented an initial city zoning (CC, CG, OI, MU, and PDR 9.4) for newly annexed I-40 right-of-way translating county zoning, consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and recommended by the Planning Commission. With no public speakers, Council approved the zoning 7-0 and adjourned at 10:15 p.m.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden opened the August 4, 2011 City Council Work Session with six members present while Mayor Bill Bell was en route, and Bell later joined and chaired the remainder of the session. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items, granted excused absences to Farad Ali (August 18) and Mike Woodard (September 8), and received an Emergency Communications briefing on Durham's pilot program with Verizon Wireless enabling text-to-911—the first in North Carolina and second jurisdiction nationwide—as well as state-authorized voice alteration on released 911 audio. After a truncated middle section, Council reviewed the City Manager and City Attorney's comparison of Durham's 'Ban the Box' administrative policy against Philadelphia's citywide ordinance, discussed whether an ordinance was appropriate or necessary, and agreed to place the item on the August 15 General Business Agenda; Engineering Manager Ed Venable also reported that American Tobacco Trail I-40 bridge bids came in at $7.7 million against a $5.8 million budget and proposed deferring other capital projects to meet the 60-day award window. Council concluded with 6-0 and 7-0 ballot appointments for the Tourism Development Authority and Citizens Advisory Committee and unanimously settled the August 15 agenda, with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Priority Items, and Excused Absence Requests
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden opened the work session with six members present as Mayor Bill Bell was on his way. Council unanimously accepted the City Manager's priority adjustments (noting citizen speakers for Items 27 and 28 would not appear and adding updates on 911 texting, failed developments, and stormwater) and approved excused absences for Farad Ali (August 18) and Mike Woodard (September 8, National League of Cities).

agenda_items.title: Agenda Preview and Pulled Item 12 (Delinquent Sewer Disconnection/Reconnection Fees)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff previewed upcoming items including Water Management Item 12 (pulled by a Council member for the work session), the Q1/Q2 2011 crime report (Item 13, set for August 15), groundwater performance standards (Item 14), street/assessment hearings (Items 15–17), and planning/rezoning cases (Items 20–24: Guest Road Family Care, Ample Storage Center, Bivins Road, and NC 54).

agenda_items.title: Emergency Communications Briefing: Next-Generation 911 Texting Trial and Voice Alteration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emergency Communications staff briefed Council on Durham's new Verizon Wireless text-to-911 pilot—making Durham the first city in North Carolina and the second jurisdiction nationally (after Black Hawk County, Iowa) to launch it, addressing national survey findings that 48% of respondents with hearing, mobility, or cognitive disabilities prefer texting 911. Staff also highlighted implementation of a state law enabling voice alteration on all 911 audio released to media to protect caller identity.

agenda_items.title: 'Ban the Box' Hiring Policy Comparison and Legal Authority Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap, the City Manager reported Durham's practice of deferring criminal history questions until a job offer is made goes further than Philadelphia's pre-interview ordinance, while Mayor Bell recounted his discussion with Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter and the City Attorney noted North Carolina lacks home-rule authority to regulate private employers without General Assembly action. Council members debated whether to codify the internal policy by ordinance, noted a future council could undo any ordinance, and agreed to place the update on the August 15 General Business Agenda.

agenda_items.title: American Tobacco Trail I-40 Bridge Bid Results and Capital Funding Reallocation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater Manager Ed Venable reported that the low bid for the American Tobacco Trail I-40 bridge came in at $7.7 million compared to a $5.8 million engineering estimate and budget. Staff outlined a plan to defer existing funded projects to future years so the bridge contract could be awarded within the 60-day bid and NCDOT permitting window.

agenda_items.title: Board/Commission Appointments and Settling the August 15 Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ballot results confirmed six votes for Summer Bicknell to the Convention & Visitors Bureau Tourism Development Authority and seven votes for an appointee to the Citizens Advisory Committee. Mayor Bell then called for and Council unanimously approved setting the August 15 regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1–10 and 12; GBA Items 11 and 13; GBA Public Hearings Items 15–25).

votes.discussion_detail: Granted Mike Woodard an excused absence for September 8 to attend a National League of Cities meeting.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 1, 2011 Regular City Council Meeting with all seven members present, Mayor Bill Bell presented the 28th Annual National Night Out proclamation to Police Chief Jose Lopez and recognized a Liberty Mutual check supporting the 'Bringing Back the Fourth' celebration. Council voted unanimously (7-0) across all six recorded actions: approving the City Manager's priority request to refer Item 17 (Durham Central Park shade structure donation) back to administration, accepting the City Clerk's notice of a valid protest petition on Item 32, and adopting the Consent Agenda covering board appointments, historic preservation and planning work programs, stormwater updates, and water/sewer infrastructure contracts. Following public discussion on Item 23 (the Leesville Road / Del Webb utility extension agreement, where Council questioned developer-funded sewer easement condemnation) and a truncated middle section, Council voted 7-0 to approve Item 32 (Leesville Road Active Adult Community / Del Webb rezoning), voted 7-0 on Item 33 to adopt the Downtown Preservation Plan update, and voted 7-0 on a quasi-judicial major special use permit allowing A1 Sandrock to process construction and demolition debris at 1017 South Hoover Road with 11 staff conditions. Mayor Bell closed by requesting a cross-agency review with police, prosecutors, probation, and judges after armed robbery suspects were released on reduced bonds.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and National Night Out Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order with all seven members present and presented Police Chief Jose Lopez and community partners with a proclamation for the 28th Annual National Night Out on August 2, 2011 (noting over 100 registered neighborhoods and Durham's ninth-place national peer-city ranking in 2010). Remarks also recognized Liberty Mutual's check for the 'Bringing Back the Fourth' July 4th event and the NCBEMO conference.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items and Consent Agenda (Items 1, 3–6, 8, 18–22, 24–26)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to refer Item 17 (Durham Central Park shade structure donation) back to administration and 7-0 to acknowledge the Clerk's report of a valid protest petition on Item 32. Council then approved the Consent Agenda 7-0, including board/commission appointments, the Historic Preservation Fund grant, the FY 2011–12 Planning work program, Brenrose Circle assessment rescission, stormwater updates, a US 70/Raleigh Interconnection change order, Endion Avenue storage tank land purchase, and water reclamation nutrient analyzers.

agenda_items.title: Utility Extension Agreement with Pulte Homes — Leesville Road Active Adult Community (Del Webb)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff confirmed the utility extension agreement with Pulte Homes was standard (with a Raleigh service section deleted), while proponent Ron Horvath spoke in support of extending utilities near RTP. Council members questioned the City Attorney regarding contract language allowing developer-funded city condemnation for off-site sewer easements and whether it satisfied public-purpose requirements, before a middle gap in the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change — Leesville Road Active Adult Community (Del Webb)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion, Council concluded questioning on failed subdivisions and the Leesville Road / Del Webb active adult community rezoning, noting Council had previously approved two similar age-restricted communities unanimously. Council closed the public hearing and approved the rezoning 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Downtown Preservation Plan Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Lisa Miller presented the first update in over 20 years to the 1989 Downtown Local Historic District overlay preservation plan, adding recent history and updated structure inventories and noting unanimous recommendations from the Historic Preservation Commission (9-0) and Planning Commission (12-0). Council Member Mike Woodard commended staff's extensive work, and Council approved the update 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Quasi-Judicial Major Special Use Permit — 1017 South Hoover Road Recycling Center (A1 Sandrock)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented A1 Sandrock's application to modify a 1999 major special use permit (M99-1, household recyclables) to process construction and demolition debris under UDO Section 3.9.8 with 11 recommended special conditions. A1 Sandrock Business Development Manager Chad Morris testified to the company's 59%+ recycling rate, and on a motion by Council Member Mike Woodard, Council granted the permit with staff's 11 conditions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Mayor's Remarks on Armed Robbery Bond Reductions and Probation Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell praised Durham Police for apprehending armed robbery suspects but raised concern that suspects under probation supervision had previously been released after bond reductions from $500,000 to $200,000 and $100,000, asking the City Manager to convene Police, the District Attorney's office, probation, and judicial representatives to review the paper trail. Council Member Eugene Brown asked to participate in the meeting, and the meeting adjourned at 9:13 p.m.

meetings.executive_summary: At the July 21, 2011 City Council Work Session—chaired by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden with six members present (Diane Catotti absent/excused, though emailing support from Florida)—Council welcomed new Public Works Director Marvin Williams and unanimously approved priority items for the City Manager, City Attorney (three closed-session claims items), and City Clerk. Council voted unanimously by voice vote to suspend the rules and adopt Item 2 (setting municipal candidate filing fees ahead of the July 25 filing opening), Item 39 (Durham City-County HOME Consortium Joint Cooperation Agreement), and a resolution introduced by Council Member Mike Woodard opposing General Assembly bills SB 106 and HB 777 (proposing a statewide constitutional ban on same-sex marriage). Assistant Manager Robert Joyner also presented an expanded failed-subdivisions update adding Amberlyn Valley Townhomes Phase 2, Colony at American Village Phases 3–4, Emerywood Estates, Forest Brook, and 18 phases/tracts of Brightleaf at the Park, alongside HOA outreach for Category 4 subdivisions. Council concluded by suspending the rules to approve two reappointments ahead of a July 26 meeting, unanimously settling the upcoming regular agenda, and entering closed session, with no split or contested votes.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - 751 South Project Voluntary Annexation
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 27, 2011 special informational City Council meeting on the 751 South Project voluntary annexation petition, Mayor Bill Bell opened the session for Council-staff discussion without public comment and instituted a five-minute question rotation. Staff from Budget and Management Services (Annexation Coordinator Robin Bibby), City-County Planning (Pat Young), and the City Attorney's Office (Attorney Baker) presented the 1,300-unit mixed-use project's 10-year buildout, three valuation scenarios—highlighting that Planning's mid-range Scenario B projected roughly 48% of the developer's aggressive Scenario A valuation—and departmental operating, capital, and legal impacts. Council members questioned staff extensively on negative net cash flows prior to 2013 buildout, the developer's choice of an 80% area median income threshold for affordable housing, road capacity and traffic hazards along the corridor, offsite Jordan Lake stormwater compliance, and utility extension without annexation. Council Member Eugene Brown expressed reservations about the pending neighbor lawsuit and questioned holding the session without making a decision, arguing opponents could protract litigation indefinitely at the developer's expense, while Council Member Diane Catotti countered that the session was a necessary learning opportunity on a complex issue; no formal votes were taken on the annexation, apart from a unanimous voice vote approving a Council member's request for an excused absence at the July 21 work session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Special Meeting Ground Rules
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the special meeting to order at 3:00 PM, welcoming attendees and conducting roll call, which recorded Mayor Bill Bell, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and an additional member before moving to introductory remarks. Mayor Bell explained that the session was strictly for Council and staff discussion on the 751 South Project voluntary annexation without public comment and established a five-minute rotation for each member's questions.

agenda_items.title: Staff Overview, Cost-Benefit Methodology, and 751 South Project Features
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Deputy City Manager introduced the city's enhanced cost-benefit analysis capturing operational, one-time, and capital improvement impacts, noting the administration was not making a recommendation at this meeting. Annexation Coordinator Robin Bibby reviewed the 751 South mixed-use development (1,300 residential units across single-family homes, townhomes, apartments, and condos over a 10-year buildout), the April 2010 petition submission and November certification, ongoing plat and legal description review, and preparation of the utility extension agreement.

agenda_items.title: Planning Buildout Scenarios, Valuation Analysis, and Departmental Cost Estimates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young of the City-County Planning Department outlined concurrent approvals required—noting the Planning Commission's April review would stand unless substantial changes occurred—and contrasted the applicant's aggressive Scenario A with Planning's mid-range Scenario B (about 48% of the applicant's valuation, based on Creekside Elementary zone comparables built since 2000) and lower-performance Scenario C. Staff also compiled operational cost projections across Fire, Parks and Recreation, Police, Public Works, Solid Waste, and Transportation.

agenda_items.title: Council Q&A: Pending Lawsuit, Fiscal Timing, Affordable Housing, Infrastructure, and Jordan Lake Rules
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle segment, Council questioned City Attorney Baker and staff on the pending neighbors' lawsuit (noting there is no statute of limitations on litigation pendency and appeals), negative revenues before 2013 buildout, why affordable housing was set at 80% median income rather than 30% or 60%, police/sheriff construction patrols, unbudgeted road capacity hazards, and Jordan Lake rules requiring offsite nutrient reductions. Council Member Eugene Brown voiced concern that litigation delays unfairly impose carrying costs on the developer and questioned why Council was meeting without a decision, whereas Council Member Diane Catotti defended the meeting as an essential learning session and requested details on utility extension without annexation.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Timeline, July 21 Work Session Excused Absence, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson confirmed staff would compile written responses to all Council questions in a single package within two to three weeks. After coordinating around July travel schedules, Council approved a member's request for an excused absence from the July 21 work session by voice vote and adjourned.

votes.item_title: Request for Excused Absence from July 21, 2011 Work Session
votes.notes: Passed by voice vote ('It hit the same eye [all in favor say aye]. The motion passes.'). Mover, seconder, and requesting member were not explicitly named in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: A Council member noted being out of town during the week of the July 21 work session and requested an excused absence.

disagreements.meeting_title: Special City Council Meeting - 751 South Project Voluntary Annexation
disagreements.issue: Purpose of Special Informational Session and Fairness Amid Pending 751 South Lawsuit
disagreements.summary: Council Members Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti expressed differing views on holding a non-decision informational session while neighbors' litigation against the 751 South project remained pending.
disagreements.side_a_position: Questioned holding the special meeting without making a decision and warned that indefinite litigation delays are unfair to the developer.
side_a_arguments: Project opponents could keep the matter in court indefinitely through trials and appeals while the developer continues absorbing carrying costs.
With Council unable to affect the lawsuit and taking no decision at the session, holding the meeting without a decision timeline raised fairness concerns.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defended the meeting as a necessary educational session given the project's legal and fiscal complexity.
side_b_arguments: The 751 South annexation involves highly complicated fiscal, legal, environmental, and infrastructure issues requiring a dedicated learning ('didactic') session.
Council also needed detailed analysis on alternatives such as extending utilities without immediate annexation while preserving future annexation rights.
disagreements.resolution: No vote was taken on the annexation; staff committed to returning a consolidated written response package to Council's questions in two to three weeks.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 20, 2011 Regular City Council Meeting, Mayor Bill Bell and Council Member Mike Woodard presented a proclamation and resolution honoring retiring American Dance Festival Director Charles L. Reinhardt, while Council Member Howard Clement III commended Durham Housing Authority CEO Dallas Parks and staff on the June 15 Durham Conference on Housing. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority agenda changes (7-0) and passed the Consent Agenda (7-0) minus four pulled items (Items 14, 15, 23, and 30). Following public hearings, Council unanimously approved (7-0) the Cardinal Oaks voluntary annexation (Item 49) and initial Rural Residential zoning of 46.86 acres south of Cheek Road (Item 38), three adjacent street-segment annexations (Item 39—where Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden immediately corrected an accidental nay vote to make the final tally 7-0), and Supplemental Item 50 amending Contract ST-250 for Revere Road street repairs and repaving (7-0). meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 9, 2011 City Council Work Session, Mayor Bill Bell reminded the community of the June 25 Jeannie Lucas Luncheon before Council unanimously accepted by voice vote the City Manager's priority agenda—which requested suspending the rules for same-day votes on five HOME affordable housing agreements (Items 9–13) and a University Drive/Chapel Hill Boulevard drainage engineering amendment (Item 47), though one Council member voiced reluctance to vote on Items 11–13 without prior paperwork—alongside the City Attorney's request for a closed session and 2010 Census ward reapportionment briefing. Council reviewed the full draft agenda covering the FY 2011–12 budget and CIP, CDBG/HOME funding, economic development, transit, and multiple zoning and annexation public hearings. Later in the session, intergovernmental staff briefed Council on state legislative crossover activity—including the Durham Small Business Enterprise bill, Senate passage of the Rougemont incorporation bill requiring a November referendum, ratified stormwater fee collection and municipal broadband bills, voter ID amendments, and pending billboard legislation—and the City Attorney presented a draft 10-question FAQ on post-2010 Census ward boundary adjustments noting Ward 2 grew the most and targeting July/August drafts since November 2011 elections are at-large. Council concluded by unanimously setting the regular meeting agenda by voice vote and entering closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), with no split or contested votes recorded.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Priority Items, Rules Suspension Requests, and Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order, noted the June 25 Jeannie Lucas Luncheon, and heard the City Manager's priority requests to suspend rules for same-day votes on HOME housing agreements (Items 9–13: Metropolitan Housing & CDC, DHA Edgemont Elms, Builders of Hope, and Housing for New Hope) and drainage engineering (Item 47), plus supplemental items 43–49. Although a member noted missing packets for Items 11–13 and several supplemental items, Council unanimously approved the priority agenda by voice vote alongside the City Attorney's closed-session and ward-reapportionment briefing requests before reviewing draft agenda items 1–45.

agenda_items.title: State Legislative Update (Crossover Deadline)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle section of the transcript, staff updated Council on North Carolina General Assembly activity on crossover day as legislative leaders aimed to adjourn within a week or so. Highlights included the Durham Small Business Enterprise bill passing the Senate and reaching House Finance, Senate passage of the Rougemont incorporation bill (which would require a November referendum), ongoing redistricting, Durham's inclusion in a ratified stormwater fee collection bill, an expanded voter ID definition, ratification of the municipal broadband bill, and city opposition to House billboard legislation.

agenda_items.title: 2010 Census Ward Boundary Adjustments Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Attorney distributed a draft '10 Frequently Asked Questions' overview on ward boundary adjustments required after the 2010 Census, noting Ward 2 experienced the largest population growth. He explained that because November 2011 municipal elections are at-large rather than ward-based, the charter's six-month deadline does not affect the 2011 election, and outlined plans to present draft maps and scenarios at the July work session for potential August adoption.

agenda_items.title: Set Regular Meeting Agenda and Enter Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved setting the June 20 Regular City Council Meeting agenda—comprising Consent Items 1–5, 8, 14–31, 45–46, and 48; General Business Items 6–7; and Public Hearing Items 33–39 and 49—by unanimous voice vote. Immediately afterward, Council moved into closed session for attorney-client consultation pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3).

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Manager's Priority Items and Attorney Closed-Session Request
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('all the favor and get the same eye... motion passes unanimously'). One member had earlier expressed reluctance to vote on Items 11–13 without receiving paperwork.
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the manager's priority modifications (same-day action requests, 2:00 PM scheduling for Make It Durham, and supplemental items 43–49) and the City Attorney's closed session and ward-reapportionment briefing additions.

votes.item_title: Set Agenda for Regular City Council Meeting (June 20, 2011)
votes.notes: Passed by voice vote before Council adjourned to closed session.
votes.discussion_detail: Set Consent Items 1–5, 8, 14–31, 45–46, and 48; GBA Items 6–7; and GBA Public Hearing Items 33–39 and 49 for the upcoming regular meeting agenda.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 6, 2011 Regular City Council Meeting, Mayor Bill Bell proclaimed June 2011 as Ride to Work Day and honored Special Olympics torch refurbisher Mr. Alston, while Council Member Howard Clement III praised Durham Housing Authority CEO Dallas Parks and his team. Council unanimously approved (7-0) referring the Crown Point rezoning (Item 24) back to staff and adding Supplemental Item 30 for street-segment annexation public hearings, and passed the Consent Agenda (7-0) minus three pulled items (Items 16, 21, and 22). During the Item 23 public hearing on the proposed FY 2011–12 budget and FY 2012–17 CIP, residents criticized proposed property tax and water/sewer fee increases and urged greater investment in Northeast Central Durham. On pulled Item 21—a resolution endorsing the regional bus and rail transit plan and recommending a county half-cent sales tax and motor vehicle tax referendum—Mayor Bill Bell proposed amending the resolution to recommend delaying tax implementation until Orange County and/or Wake County also pass similar referenda, which Council Member Diane Catotti initially opposed in favor of the original text so Durham could expand bus service independently, though Mike Woodard moved Bell's amended resolution and Council passed it 7-0. Council also voted to adopt the proposed FY 2011–12 water and sewer rates (Item 22; exact numerical tally unclear in transcript ASR, with no dissenting voter named), with no recorded split votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Proclamations, Priority Items, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell opened the meeting at 7:02 PM with all seven Council members present, issued a Ride to Work Day proclamation, recognized Mr. Alston for Special Olympics service, and heard remarks from Howard Clement III commending the Durham Housing Authority. Council voted 7-0 to refer Item 24 (Crown Point zoning Z1100003) back to staff and add Supplemental Item 30 (street-segment annexation hearing), and then passed the Consent Agenda 7-0 after pulling Items 16, 21, and 22.

agenda_items.title: Item 23: Public Hearing on Proposed FY 2011–12 Budget and FY 2012–17 Capital Improvement Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson introduced the legally noticed public hearing on the proposed FY 2011–12 budget and FY 2012–17 CIP. Public speakers including Jerry Venachia, Craig Roxbury, Harriett Goodwin, Matt Drew, John Tarantino, and Victoria Peterson raised concerns over high water/sewer bills, objected to the ~$2 million property tax increase and water rate hikes as regressive, and urged directing more city investment to Northeast Central Durham rather than downtown.

agenda_items.title: Item 21: Regional and Local Transit Initiatives (Bus and Rail Investment Plan Resolution)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle transcript gap, Mayor Bill Bell proposed adding language to the transit investment plan resolution recommending that if Durham County voters pass a half-cent sales tax and motor vehicle tax referendum, the County Commissioners should not implement the taxes until Orange County and/or Wake County pass a similar referendum. Diane Catotti preferred the original resolution to avoid tying Durham's hands and allow earlier bus expansion, while Bell emphasized regional interdependence and local business competitiveness; Mike Woodard moved Bell's amended resolution, which passed 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 22: Adoption of Proposed Water and Sewer Rates for FY 2011–12 & Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell called up pulled Item 22 (pulled by Ms. Goodwin) for action on the proposed FY 2011–12 water and sewer rates, and Council moved, seconded, and passed the item by electronic vote. Mike Woodard closed the meeting with a tribute to late civic volunteer Jack Steer before adjournment.

votes.notes: Electronic vote passed 7-0.

votes.notes: Electronic vote passed 7-0 after initial machine troubleshooting.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted Mayor Bill Bell's amended resolution endorsing the bus and rail investment plan while recommending that the Durham Board of County Commissioners delay implementing a passed half-cent sales tax or motor vehicle tax until Orange and/or Wake counties pass a similar referendum.

votes.item_title: Item 22: Adoption of Proposed Water and Sewer Rates for FY 2011–12
votes.notes: Transcript ASR at [01:07:06] garbled the announced tally ('It pants the same as the one') and no dissenting voter was named in the digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the proposed FY 2011–12 water and sewer rates, which had been pulled from Consent by Ms. Goodwin.

disagreements.issue: Conditioning Durham Transit Sales Tax Implementation on Orange and Wake County Referenda
disagreements.summary: Mayor Bill Bell and Council Member Diane Catotti disagreed on whether Council's resolution supporting the regional bus and rail investment plan should recommend delaying Durham's half-cent sales tax until Orange or Wake counties approve similar referenda.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support the regional transit plan while recommending the County delay levying the tax until Orange County and/or Wake County pass a referendum.
side_a_arguments: The bus and rail investment plan is a regional system requiring state, federal, and multi-county participation rather than Durham taxpayers funding it alone.
Implementing a half-cent sales tax solely in Durham could put local small businesses at a competitive disadvantage against neighboring counties.
disagreements.side_b_position: Prefer the original unamended resolution without tying Durham's tax implementation to Orange and Wake counties.
side_b_arguments: Durham should not have its hands tied by neighboring counties' timelines.
Durham would realize significant benefits from expanding bus service hours prior to regional rail coming online.
disagreements.resolution: Mike Woodard moved Mayor Bill Bell's amended resolution, and Council adopted it 7-0.

meetings.title: City Council Budget Review FY 2011-12 - Flagged Items
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 6, 2011 special budget review session on four flagged items for the FY 2011–12 budget—deferred maintenance, the debt model and tax rate adjustment, housing counseling, and Parks and Recreation fees—Mayor Bill Bell presided over Council and staff deliberations with no formal votes taken. On deferred maintenance, the City Manager recommended retaining the $500,000 budgeted for street resurfacing to honor 2007 bond-referendum commitments while returning in two to three months with potential FY11 closeout carry-forward funds to cover critical Priority 1 facility repairs such as the $425,000+ fleet maintenance roof (requiring roughly $1.0–$1.01 million total). Following a middle transcript gap covering the debt model, Community Development staff and Council (including Cora Cole-McFadden, Diane Catotti, and Farad Ali) debated housing and financial literacy counseling after three of four remaining outside agencies declined unfunded referrals, with members objecting to referring low-income Durham residents to Chapel Hill agencies. Parks and Recreation Director Rhonda Parker concluded with attendance figures for Holton and Walltown and cost-recovery comparisons (<11% in Durham versus 23.8% in Greensboro), alongside staff clarifications on water rate units (1 cent per 100 cubic feet) and County Project Build.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Flagged Budget Item 1: Deferred Maintenance vs. Street Resurfacing Fund
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the 5:03 PM special session to order, and the City Manager introduced four flagged items from the May budget workshops: deferred maintenance, the debt model, housing counseling, and Parks and Recreation fees. Staff and Council discussed prioritizing urgent repairs—noting the $425,000+ fleet maintenance center roof was omitted from the initial $500,000 allocation and critical Priority 1 items would require about $1.0–$1.01 million—while the City Manager urged preserving the $500,000 street resurfacing allocation to uphold 2007 bond commitments and using year-end carry-forward fund balance in two to three months.

agenda_items.title: Flagged Budget Item 3: Housing and Financial Literacy Counseling Referrals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap in the digest covering the debt model, Community Development staff (Mike) and Council members examined city-funded housing counseling for low-income (<=80% AMI) city residents and homeownership programs such as Southside and Rolling Hills. Council members expressed concern that three of four remaining external agencies (down from 15) refused unfunded city referrals and objected to sending Durham residents without cars to Chapel Hill agencies, urging staff to explore in-house capacity or MOUs bringing HUD-funded partners into Durham.

agenda_items.title: Flagged Budget Item 4: Parks & Recreation Fees, Water Rate Units, and Project Build
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Parks and Recreation Director Rhonda Parker presented April and year-to-date attendance reports for Holton (5,780 in April; 31,468 YTD) and Walltown (2,555 in April), noting Durham's $1.2 million fee budget recovers under 11% of departmental costs compared to Greensboro's 23.8% in order to keep programs affordable. Staff also clarified that water rates add 1 cent per 100 cubic feet (CCF) and reported discussions with Durham County to assign existing city staff to a program similar to the County's Project Build.

disagreements.meeting_title: City Council Budget Review FY 2011-12 - Flagged Items
disagreements.issue: Funding Critical Deferred Facility Maintenance vs. Preserving Street Resurfacing Allocation
disagreements.summary: Council and administration weighed whether to redirect $500,000 from street resurfacing to address urgent building maintenance like the $425,000 fleet maintenance roof immediately or wait for year-end fund balance.
disagreements.side_a_position: Keep the $500,000 in the street resurfacing operating line and revisit deferred maintenance using FY11 carry-forward fund balance in two to three months.
side_a_arguments: Removing the $500,000 from street resurfacing would send a poor signal regarding commitments made during the 2007 bond referendum to transition paving into the operating budget.
Returning after June 30 fiscal closeout allows Council to target carry-forward funds toward the ~$1.0 million in critical Priority 1 repairs.
disagreements.side_b_position: Questioned keeping $500,000 unspent in street resurfacing while critical city building roofs continue to deteriorate.
side_b_arguments: Fixing leaky roofs, including the $425,000 fleet maintenance building roof left out of the initial Priority 1 bundle, is a prudent move to prevent additional deterioration.
Staff acknowledged the street resurfacing money would not be spent this year aside from updating the street study.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; the City Manager agreed to return within two to three months after year-end closeout with carry-forward fund balance options.

disagreements.meeting_title: City Council Budget Review FY 2011-12 - Flagged Items
disagreements.issue: Referring Low-Income Durham Residents to Outside HUD Housing Counseling Agencies
disagreements.summary: Council members challenged staff's reliance on external HUD-funded agencies outside Durham after local partners declined to provide unfunded housing counseling.
disagreements.side_a_position: Questioned referring Durham residents to out-of-city agencies like Chapel Hill and urged local service delivery.
side_a_arguments: Referring low-income Durham residents—particularly Southside and Rolling Hills prospects who may lack vehicles—to Chapel Hill is burdensome and problematic.
With three of four remaining agencies refusing unfunded referrals, the city should consider handling counseling in-house or arranging MOUs for HUD-funded partners to come to Durham.
disagreements.side_b_position: Explained budget limits restrict direct city funding to residents tied to city homeownership programs (<=80% AMI) while broader counseling relies on external HUD partners.
side_b_arguments: City-funded pre-purchase counseling supports specific city homeownership initiatives, and the city had already ended its 100% police mortgage program due to cost.
Staff noted all suggestions for local MOUs and serving unbanked/unemployed residents were under internal departmental discussion.
disagreements.resolution: Informational review only; staff agreed to continue exploring local MOUs and in-house counseling options.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 19, 2011 City Council Work Session—presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden in Mayor Bill Bell's absence, with all six other seated members recorded at roll call—Council unanimously accepted the City Manager's priority agenda by voice vote, suspended the rules by unanimous voice vote, and unanimously approved Item 9 increasing the Convention Center Phase II project contingency via Change Order Amendment No. 2K to the Skanska USA Building CMAR contract. Council also heard citizen matters from Brian Mulligan alleging stormwater mismanagement supported by seven independent reports, Triangle Citizens Rebuilding Communities seeking continued funding, and Stonehill Estates HOA President Mr. Williams regarding street markings, while pulling Item 6 (establishing three North Carolina Urban Progress Zones) for a full presentation before immediate action. Following a middle transcript gap, Finance reported a $5 million Q3 operating revenue variance offset by lower solid waste expenses, intergovernmental staff reported the Durham Small Business Enterprise bill advancing out of House Government Committee while the Rougemont incorporation bill cleared House Finance despite Council's prior opposition, and development staff updated Council on ~50 failed or struggling subdivisions (including Lynn Hollow, Stonehill Estates, Ravenstone, and Stony Brook Cottages) and minimum-code stabilization at Liberty Warehouse. Council concluded by unanimously setting the regular meeting agenda by voice vote and confirming Candice Brutson's 5-vote ballot selection for the PLS Board, with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Priority Items, and Communication from Philadelphia Mayor
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the work session to order in Mayor Bill Bell's absence, with roll call recording Cole-McFadden, Farad Ali, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Howard Clement III, and Mike Woodard. Council unanimously adopted the City Manager's priority agenda (requesting a presentation on Item 6 Urban Progress Zones and rule suspension/vote on Item 9 Convention Center Phase II, plus follow-up reports), and Howard Clement III shared a letter from Philadelphia Mayor Nutter regarding background/housing legislation.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters: Stormwater Complaint, Community Rebuilding, and Stonehill Estates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Brian Mulligan presented seven independent engineering and landscape architect reports disputing the city stormwater division's findings and alleging two decades of mismanagement damaging his property and natural spring. Triangle Citizens Rebuilding Communities requested continued FY12 budget funding for employment programs (referred to the June 6 budget hearing), and Stonehill Estates HOA's Mr. Williams inquired about street markings, which Development Review's Robert Joyner explained were inspection measurements for upcoming repair quantities.

agenda_items.title: Item 9: Convention Center Phase II Contingency Increase (Skanska USA Amendment 2K) & Item 6 Preview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: While reviewing the draft agenda, Council pulled Item 6 (North Carolina Urban Progress Zones) from immediate vote to hear Kevin Dick's presentation, which began just before the middle transcript gap. For Item 9—increasing Convention Center Phase II project contingency under Amendment No. 2K to the Skanska USA Building CMAR contract—Council unanimously voted by voice to suspend the rules and then unanimously approved Item 9 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Q3 Financial Report and State Legislative Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle segment, Finance staff (Dave) reported a $5 million operating revenue variance—partly due to county pass-through accounting and intentionally reduced solid waste expenses—and clarified that recycling lowers landfill tipping fees rather than generating net profit. Assistant to the City Manager Carmicia Wallace reported that the Durham Small Business Enterprise bill passed the Senate and House Government Committee heading to House Finance, while the Rougemont incorporation bill received a favorable report from House Finance despite Council's prior opposition.

agenda_items.title: Failed & Struggling Subdivisions and Liberty Warehouse Unsafe Building Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Robert Joyner reported on ~50 Category 1–4 developments, adding four subdivisions to the watch list and prioritizing Category 3–4 neighborhoods (Lynn Hollow, Stonehill Estates, Ravenstone, and Stony Brook Cottages) with resident/HOA meetings set for May 24–31, while the City Attorney noted May 31 bond-demand deadlines. Deputy Manager Keith Chadwell also distributed a third-floor diagram of Liberty Warehouse, explaining the city's unsafe-building action aims only at bringing the structure up to minimum building code standards rather than redevelopment.

agenda_items.title: Set Regular Meeting Agenda, PLS Board Appointment, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the upcoming regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1–5, 7–8, 10–12, 14–18, and 21–22; GBA Public Hearing Items 23–24) by voice vote. Staff announced Candice Brutson received five votes for appointment to the PLS Board before Council adjourned at 4:27 PM.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 16, 2011 Regular City Council Meeting—with all seven Council members present—Council unanimously approved the Consent Agenda (7-0) minus pulled Item 6 (Background Investigation Policy) and deferred Item 2 (Margaret Holmes resolution) at the Mayor Pro Tempore's request. The City Manager presented the proposed $362.4 million FY 2011–12 budget (+2.6% overall) and $182.7 million General Fund budget (-11% due to separating debt service and solid waste into standalone funds), noting a reduced $5 million projected shortfall, 43% ($78 million+) dedicated to public safety, 2% projected taxable growth, and alignment with the April 18 Strategic Plan. Following a middle transcript gap, Council took up pulled Item 6 on the Background Investigation Policy ('Ban the Box'), hearing from Second Chance Alliance speakers (including Melvin Whitley, Shonda Elmore, Victoria Peterson, and John Tarantino) urging a binding city ordinance like Philadelphia's rather than an administrative hiring policy. While Howard Clement III moved to direct the City Manager and City Attorney to draft an ordinance immediately and Cora Cole-McFadden emphasized involving the City Attorney on criminal law aspects, Mayor Bill Bell cautioned Council had no draft ordinance before it and committed to obtaining Philadelphia's ordinance and consulting Mayor Nutter for fuller debate in August; Council ultimately voted 7-0 to receive the policy report with Council's comments.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Council Remarks, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:01 PM with all seven Council members present, and Howard Clement III highlighted Reverend Paul Scott's advocacy against high-potency malt liquor in Black neighborhoods before Mayor Bell thanked Reverend Whitley. Council pulled Item 6 (Background Investigation Policy) and noted Item 2 was deferred at the Mayor Pro Tempore's request, approving the remaining Consent Agenda items—including utility revenue/refunding bonds, FY12 employee benefits, DHA inspection fees, Cree Inc. utility agreements, FY14–20 TIP priorities, and a Raleigh interlocal agreement—7-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 16: City Manager's Presentation of Proposed FY 2011–12 Budget and FY 2012–17 CIP
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager presented the proposed FY 2011–12 budget totaling $362.4 million across all funds (a $9.1 million or 2.6% increase) and a $182.7 million General Fund budget (11% lower primarily due to separating debt service and solid waste into distinct funds). He highlighted a smaller $5 million initial shortfall compared to $20–$40 million gaps in prior years, over $78 million (43% of the General Fund) for public safety, conservative 2% property tax base growth, and departmental performance metrics tied to the city's April 18 Strategic Plan.

agenda_items.title: Item 6: Background Investigation Policy ('Ban the Box') Public Comment and Council Action
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap, Second Chance Alliance advocates and residents urged Council to enact an enforceable 'Ban the Box' ordinance modeled on Philadelphia rather than relying on an administrative hiring policy, while staff clarified that expunged, dismissed, or dropped charges are not used in hiring decisions. Howard Clement III pushed for an immediate directive to draft an ordinance and Cora Cole-McFadden asked to involve the City Attorney, whereas Mayor Bill Bell noted Council needed to review a concrete draft first and pledged to retrieve Philadelphia's ordinance and speak with Mayor Nutter ahead of an August discussion; Council voted 7-0 to receive the report incorporating Council's comments.
