meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 5, 2011 City Council Work Session, Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 1:05 PM—recording six seated members present at roll call with Farad Ali noted as late—and Council unanimously approved by voice vote the City Manager's priority modifications scheduling the CPAC report at 2:00 PM, referring FY 2011–12 water and sewer rates (Item 17) back to staff for one cycle, and adding Supplemental Item 28. During Citizen Matters, Stony Brook Cottages HOA President Chris Baker criticized the city's assessment approach for failed subdivisions with underfunded street bonds, while Durham Coalition of Urban Justice and community speakers protested moving Citizen Matters to 1:00 PM and objected to the public-private partnership with Friends of Old North Durham/Durham Park affecting the park's full-size athletic field contrary to 2005 Resolution 981; Mayor Bell pledged to investigate why Resolution 981 was not implemented and Mike Woodard requested a follow-up public meeting. After a middle transcript gap, Engineering Manager Norm Warner outlined faster subdivision repair options—amending an existing contract to save three months and using street crews to ramp asphalt around raised manholes—while legal staff reviewed developer bankruptcy and stormwater-pond title hurdles across eight to nine failed subdivisions including Stonehill Estates. Capital Program Advisory Committee Chair Chuck Watts and Bertha Johnson reported only one red-light CIP project remaining and recommended merging CPAC into CCIP (held for the next cycle's committee review), state transportation officials warned of $1 billion in state and potential federal cuts threatening projects like the East End Connector despite no House gas-tax cap, and Council unanimously set the regular meeting agenda by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Priority Agenda Modifications
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:05 PM with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Howard Clement III, and Mike Woodard present and Farad Ali noted as late. Council unanimously approved by voice vote the City Manager's priority items: scheduling Item 15 (CPAC quarterly report) at 2:00 PM, referring Item 17 (FY 2011–12 water and sewer rates) back to administration for one more cycle, adding Supplemental Item 28 (Brenda Boletti citizen matter), and keeping failed-development and legislative updates on the agenda.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters: Stony Brook Cottages Failed Subdivision and Durham/OMD Park Resolution 981
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Stony Brook Cottages HOA President Chris Baker objected to assessing 36 homeowners for street repairs left by a failed developer who still held eight buildable lots and underfunded bonds. Subsequent speakers, including the Durham Coalition of Urban Justice, criticized shifting Citizen Matters from 4:00 PM to 1:00 PM and challenged the public-private partnership with FOMDP for altering Durham/OMD Park's full-size athletic field in violation of 2005 Resolution 981; Mayor Bell promised to investigate the resolution's status while distinguishing formal public hearings from public meetings, and Mike Woodard asked the manager to follow up on another meeting.

agenda_items.title: Legislative Update and Failed Subdivisions Accelerated Repair & Bankruptcy Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle segment, staff briefed Council on state Senate and House budget debates over fee versus tax classifications and Senator McKissick's meeting with Senator Apodaca. Engineering Manager Norm Warner proposed bypassing a four-month bid cycle by amending an existing contract (saving three months) and deploying street maintenance crews to place asphalt ramps around raised manholes and patch potholes, while legal staff described investigating bankrupt developers and property titles to assess stormwater-pond completion costs across eight to nine failed subdivisions including Stonehill Estates.

agenda_items.title: CPAC Third Quarter Report, Proposed Committee Merger, and State Transportation Funding Outlook
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson and CPAC Chair Chuck Watts reported that red-light CIP projects dropped from 33 in 2008 to just one in January, recommending Council dissolve CPAC and merge its members into the CCIP committee; staff noted formal action would wait for the next cycle's comprehensive committee evaluation. A state transportation official then briefed Council that while the House budget omitted a gas-tax cap, $1 billion in state cuts and potential federal reductions could jeopardize major division projects including the East End Connector.

agenda_items.title: Set Regular Meeting Agenda and Council Announcements (NCBMO & Edge Program)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the upcoming regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1–14, GBA Item 16, and GBA Public Hearing Items 18–24) by voice vote. Cora Cole-McFadden announced Durham's hosting of the NCBMO 30th-anniversary summer conference on July 29–31 and a September NLC Human Development Committee visit, and an Edge Program representative invited Council to its largest GED graduation ceremony.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of City Manager's Priority Agenda Modifications
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('on favor of motion indicate by saying aye. Aye. Those opposed. Motion passes.').
votes.discussion_detail: Approved scheduling Item 15 (CPAC report) at 2:00 PM, referring Item 17 (water and sewer rates) back to administration for one cycle, adding Supplemental Item 28, and retaining failed-development and legislative updates.

votes.item_title: Set Agenda for Regular City Council Meeting
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Set Consent Items 1–14, GBA Item 16, and GBA Public Hearing Items 18–24 for the next regular City Council meeting.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 2, 2011 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council opened with proclamations for Drinking Water Week (and student water conservation poster winners), Peace Officers Memorial Day, National Community Development Week, National Train Day, Municipal Clerks Week, and women's health/leadership, followed by a staff update on the newly adopted 'Durham's Got It' strategic plan. Later in the meeting, after addressing the statutory May 15 HUD deadline and hearing public comment calling for removal of the Southside/Rolling Hills blight designation, the Council voted 7-0 to approve the FY 2011-12 Annual Action Plan for CDBG, HOME, and ESG funds. Council also approved a conditional resolution of support for closing a portion of Pickett Road in Orange County (requiring a traffic signal at Erwin and Randolph roads and bike/pedestrian access) despite neighborhood traffic opposition. On Item 8, the local funding commitment for Southside Phase 1 submission to the North Carolina Housing Finance Agency, the motion passed 6-1, with Ayes from Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Diane Catotti, and Farad Ali, and a Nay from Eugene Brown (who corrected the electronic record after his no vote failed to display).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Silent Meditation, Pledge of Allegiance, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:03 PM and led a moment of silent meditation, followed by the Pledge of Allegiance led by Council Member Howard Clement III. The City Clerk called the roll, confirming all seven seated members were present.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations and Community Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council presented proclamations for Drinking Water Week (May 1-7, 2011) alongside local and statewide winners of the water conservation poster contest (135 entries across 10 schools), Peace Officers Memorial Day (May 6), National Community Development Week's 25th anniversary essay winners, National Train Day (noting a 66% five-year increase in Durham Amtrak ridership), Municipal Clerks Week honoring the City Clerk and staff, and a women's leadership recognition joined by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden.

agenda_items.title: 'Durham's Got It' Strategic Plan Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager recognized Budget Director Bertha Johnson and Project Manager Jay Ronstein for leading the 'Durham's Got It' strategic plan officially adopted by the City Council in April 2011.

agenda_items.title: FY 2011-12 Annual Action Plan for CDBG, HOME, and ESG Funds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle section omitted in the digest, Council discussed budget allocation questions ahead of the May 15 statutory HUD submission deadline (May 14 in Greensboro) to avoid forfeiting entitlement funds, agreeing to resolve remaining philosophical questions during upcoming May budget work sessions. Speaker Denise Hester urged removing the blight designation from Southside/Rolling Hills so CDBG funds could be directed to enhanced policing, streetscape improvements, business development, and job creation. Council then voted 7-0 to approve the proposed Annual Action Plan.

agenda_items.title: Resolution of Support for Closing a Portion of Pickett Road in Orange County
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Deborah Barnes opposed the resolution of support, arguing that closing Pickett Road would shift roughly 500 cars per day onto Randolph Road and was not called for in the New Hope Open Space Plan. Planning staff clarified that Orange County Commissioners hold road-closing jurisdiction and Durham's resolution includes two conditions: installing a traffic signal at Erwin and Randolph roads prior to closure and maintaining bicycle and pedestrian access through the park site. Council Member Howard Clement III questioned Barnes regarding a June neighborhood meeting before the Council voted to approve the resolution.

agenda_items.title: Local Funding Commitment for Southside Phase 1 Submission to NC Housing Finance Agency
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered the local funding commitment required for the Southside Phase 1 submission to the North Carolina Housing Finance Agency. After an initial announcement of unanimous passage, Council Member Eugene Brown stated his no vote had not registered on the electronic display, and Mayor Bill Bell directed the clerk to record Brown's vote against the item for a 6-1 passage.

agenda_items.title: Closing Remarks on National Events and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Howard Clement III remarked on the historic announcement made 24 hours earlier by the President of the United States regarding national security events and thanked the President and his staff. The meeting adjourned at 10:41 PM.

votes.item_title: Approval of FY 2011-12 Annual Action Plan for CDBG, HOME, and Emergency Shelter Grant Funds (Item 9)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest; clerk opened and closed the electronic vote and Mayor Bell announced it passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Staff noted the plan had to be submitted to HUD in Greensboro by May 14 to meet the May 15 statutory deadline; council members agreed to revisit broader allocation questions during May budget briefings.

votes.item_title: Resolution of Support for Closing a Portion of Pickett Road in Orange County (Item 13)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest. ASR rendered Mayor Bell's tally announcement as 'It passed the same one' (consistent with a 7-0 vote, matching his identical phrasing immediately afterward before Eugene Brown corrected Item 8).
votes.discussion_detail: Resolution supported Orange County's closing of a portion of Pickett Road conditioned on installing a traffic signal at Erwin and Randolph roads prior to closure and maintaining bicycle/pedestrian park access.

votes.item_title: Local Funding Commitment for Southside Phase 1 Submission to NC Housing Finance Agency (Item 8)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest. After the initial tally announcement, Eugene Brown stated 'I voted no on that last one. It didn't show up,' and Mayor Bill Bell directed the clerk to record Brown's vote against the motion for a 6-1 tally.
votes.discussion_detail: Local funding commitment for Southside Phase 1 LIHTC/NCHFA application.

disagreements.issue: Local Funding Commitment for Southside Phase 1 Submission to NC Housing Finance Agency (Item 8)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 6-1 on committing local city funds for the Southside Phase 1 submission to the North Carolina Housing Finance Agency, with Council Member Eugene Brown casting the sole dissenting vote.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the local funding commitment to support the Southside Phase 1 North Carolina Housing Finance Agency submission.
side_a_arguments: Providing the local funding commitment enables the Southside/Rolling Hills Phase 1 mixed-income housing application to proceed to the state housing finance agency.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the local funding commitment for Southside Phase 1.
side_b_arguments: Consistent with concerns raised in prior Southside financing deliberations regarding long-term city financial exposure and reliance on CDBG/Section 108 commitments, Eugene Brown voted no on the commitment.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 6-1 after Eugene Brown corrected the record at 03:36:54 to register his no vote.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 21, 2011 City Council Work Session opened and presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden (with Diane Catotti excused absent and Mayor Bill Bell arriving partway through), the Council approved the City Manager's priority items, heard an update on failed and struggling subdivisions, and moved to suspend rules on City Hall Plaza lighting. Following Mayor Bell's arrival, the City Manager noted revised CDBG/HOME/ESG Annual Action Plan recommendations would be delivered the next week ahead of the May 2 public hearing due to federal HUD cuts. In an extended second-half deliberation on Supplemental Item 25, Council and Downtown Durham Inc. (DDI) debated the proposed 7-cent Downtown Business Improvement District (BID) tax rate, alternative rate/tier structures, an operational start date versus a July 1, 2012 effective date, and the mechanics of adopting a resolution of intent on May 2. Council concluded by announcing board nominations, approving the May 2 agenda by voice vote, and voting by voice vote to enter closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the work session to order at 1:19 PM with Farad Ali, Eugene Brown, Howard Clement III, and Mike Woodard present, and Diane Catotti excused absent. The City Manager outlined priority items including a Southside blight follow-up (awaiting Mayor Bell), rule suspension for Item 16 (Lights for City Hall Plaza), non-appearance of citizen Brenda Baletti (Item 21), supplemental Item 24 (Annual Action Plan continued to May 2), supplemental Item 25 (Downtown BID resolution), and legislative updates. Council approved the manager's priority items and the City Attorney's closed-session request by voice votes.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Item Pulls, and Rule Suspension Request for City Hall Plaza Lights (Item 16)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed upcoming agenda items across Audit Services (Item 6 deficit follow-up), Budget, Community Development (Southside Phase 1 and Southside homeownership services), Blue Cross Blue Shield healthy eating grant, Planning (Pickett Road closing, Crown Point expedited zoning C1100003, Historic Preservation report), Public Works (Item 16 Lights for City Hall Plaza), and Transportation studies. Council moved and seconded to suspend the rules on Item 16 (with five members present) and pulled Items 6, 9, 11, and 25 for discussion.

agenda_items.title: Annual Action Plan (CDBG, HOME, ESG) Manager Review Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon Mayor Bill Bell's arrival, the City Manager explained that staff had circulated Citizen Advisory Committee recommendations and that he would deliver revised manager recommendations the following week reflecting federal HUD funding cuts ahead of the May 2 public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Failed and Struggling Developments Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater Manager Ed Venable reported that Public Works and the City Attorney's Office established an assessment checklist for seven identified failed developments. Staff planned to complete the checklists, meet with neighborhood residents and property owners, and return to Council to authorize action plans and any needed special assessments.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Business Improvement District (BID) Proposal Deliberation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle section omitted in the digest, Council members and Downtown Durham Inc. (DDI) discussed the proposed Downtown Business Improvement District (BID), examining the proposed 7-cent tax rate versus a lower rate, $250,000 in existing city/county contributions, $45,000 in partner fundraising, tier-system concerns, SGI contract timing (targeting October 1 operations or a July 1, 2012 effective date), annual Council rate-setting authority, and whether Council would adopt a resolution of intent on May 2 directing staff to draft MOUs and contracts.

agenda_items.title: Board Nominations, Setting the May 2 Agenda, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board nominations were announced: Brian Miles received five votes for reappointment to the Environmental Affairs Board and Reverend Nars Whitaker received five votes for appointment to the Human Relations Commission. Council approved the May 2, 2011 agenda by voice vote (Consent items 1-10, 12-15, 17-18; GBA items 11 and 25; GBA Public Hearing item 24) and voted by voice vote to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Approval of City Manager's Priority Items
votes.notes: Voice vote with five members present before Mayor Bill Bell arrived at 00:19:31; Diane Catotti had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved priority items outlined by the City Manager, including rule suspension request on Item 16 and supplemental Items 24 and 25.

votes.item_title: Approval of City Attorney's Priority Item (Closed Session at Close of Business)
votes.notes: Voice vote with five members present before Mayor Bill Bell arrived; Diane Catotti had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Scheduled a closed session at the close of business to discuss litigation matters.

votes.item_title: Setting the May 2, 2011 Regular City Council Agenda
votes.notes: Voice vote with six members present (Diane Catotti excused absent). Moved and seconded without recorded opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Set May 2 agenda with Consent items 1-10, 12-15, 17-18; GBA items 11 and 25; and GBA Public Hearing item 24.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Voice vote with six members present (Diane Catotti excused absent).
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to move into closed session on litigation matters requested by the City Attorney.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 18, 2011 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with six members present and Eugene Brown excused absent, the Council presented a National Thank You Day proclamation and acted unanimously (6-0) across all formal votes. Council referred Item 9 (Andrew Avenue/Miami Boulevard water tank condemnation) back to the administration following a property-owner agreement, adopted the Consent Agenda—including Durham's first City Strategic Plan, CIP budget amendments, Lake Michie advance land acquisition, and Jordan Lake water interconnection studies—and confirmed South Park Drive and Swansea Drive assessment rolls while continuing an objected assessment to June 6. In public hearings, Council heard Southside/Rolling Hills property owners petitioning to remove their blight designation under the FY 2011-12 Annual Action Plan (continued to May 2) and heard numerous downtown business and property owners opposing the proposed Downtown Business Improvement District (BID) tax before closing the hearing (6-0) and deferring action to May 2.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, Roll Call, and National Thank You Day Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:01 PM, invited Council Member Howard Clement III to lead the Pledge of Allegiance, and confirmed six members present with Eugene Brown excused absent. The City Manager presented a proclamation celebrating April 25, 2011 as National Thank You Day for elected officials sponsored by Hadi Harris Good Spirits Club International.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item: Referral of Elevated Water Storage Tank Condemnation (Andrew Ave / Miami Blvd)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested that Item 9, proposed condemnation of property for an elevated water storage tank and permanent utility easement at Andrew Avenue and Miami Boulevard, be referred back to the administration because an agreement appeared to have been reached with the property owner. Council approved the referral 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval and Strategic Plan Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 6-0 to adopt the Consent Agenda, including appointments to the Firefighters Relief Fund Board and Human Relations Commission, adoption of the City Strategic Plan (Item 4), FY 2010-12 employment and training grant ordinance #14094, FY 2010-11 CIP budget amendment #14025, Lake Michie advance property acquisition (Annie Mae Ellis), Jordan Lake partnership potable water interconnection study, and the report on failed and struggling developments. Following the vote, Council Member Mike Woodard highlighted Item 4 as Durham's first City Strategic Plan incorporating input from 2,200 city employees.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Assessment Rolls for South Park Drive and Swansea Drive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported that properties on South Park Drive and Swansea Drive benefited from water/sewer mains, laterals, and curb, gutter, and paving improvements, noting one objection from property owner Stinson on Swansea Drive. With no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and voted 6-0 to confirm the assessment rolls except for the Stinson property, continuing that hearing to June 6, 2011.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Draft FY 2011-12 Annual Action Plan (CDBG, HOME, ESG Funds)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell opened the public hearing ahead of continuing it to May 2, 2011, taking testimony from signed-up speakers Denise Hester and Larry Hester. Speaking for Fayetteville Street and UCP stakeholders, Denise Hester submitted letters and a petition asking Council to remove the blight designation from 451 parcels in Rolling Hills and Southside (citing lack of notification and inclusion of churches, commercial properties, and Hillside Park) and to use CDBG funds for public safety and Fayetteville Street streetscapes.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Proposed Downtown Business Improvement District (BID) / Municipal Services District
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following an omitted middle section, Council heard numerous business and property owners opposing the proposed BID tax, including speakers raising boundary inequity and CCB Plaza parking closure impacts (TQ Business Complex), arguments that the tax acts as a wealth transfer passed onto small tenants while nonprofits remain exempt (Marcus Hill, Ted Faulkner, L.W. Martin), a reported petition of over 65 owners representing 153 properties in opposition, and arguments that Durham's downtown progress came through public-private partnerships without a BID tax (Eric Sanfajrion, Brian Sherry). Council voted 6-0 to close the hearing and accept public comments, with Mayor Bell stating Council would deliberate and hear his recommendation on May 2.

votes.notes: Eugene Brown was excused absent at roll call; mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager requested referral back to administration because an agreement had been reached with the property owner.

votes.notes: Eugene Brown was excused absent; mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Confirmed water, sewer, curb, gutter, and paving assessment rolls while continuing the objected Stinson assessment on Swansea Drive to June 6, 2011.

votes.notes: Eugene Brown was excused absent; mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Southside Revitalization and City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 7, 2011 Special City Council Meeting and Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, Council held an extended morning policy review on the Southside Revitalization and Rolling Hills mixed-income housing project ($48.5M leveraged investment requiring $3.9M in Section 108 infrastructure financing ahead of a May 13 LIHTC deadline). During the deliberation, Council Member Eugene Brown strongly challenged the reliance on 20 years of CDBG funds to repay the Section 108 loan, warning that proposed federal cuts (such as House HR 1's 62% CDBG reduction) could leave Durham taxpayers covering roughly $750,000 annually out of non-CDBG collateral. In the afternoon work session (following an omitted middle section), Council reached consensus on Option 3 for failed and struggling subdivisions—directing closer monthly coordination between Engineering and the City Attorney's Office, legal action against non-performing sureties, and special assessments as needed—reviewed bridge lighting warranty repairs and General Assembly legislative bills, and approved the April 18 agenda by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Special Meeting Purpose
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the special meeting to order with Cora Cole-McFadden, Farad Ali, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Howard Clement III recorded in the opening roll call excerpt. Bell noted there would be no public comment period as the session was dedicated to a thorough Council-staff review of the Southside revitalization project.

agenda_items.title: Southside Revitalization and Rolling Hills Phase 1 Financing Deliberation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed the Rolling Hills project history (2003 foreclosure, 2005 RFQ selecting Traditional Neighborhood Development Partners / McCormack Baron Salazar), neighborhood connectivity goals, and Phase 1 requirements (211 mixed-income rental units, $3.9M Section 108 loan for site prep/infrastructure, May 13 LIHTC application, and $48.5M total leveraged investment). Staff presented three options: proceeding as planned, land banking, or local nonprofit development. Council Member Eugene Brown warned against locking the city into a 20-year CDBG-backed Section 108 commitment given federal HR 1 proposals to cut CDBG by 62%, arguing the city could be forced to pay $750,000 per year from non-CDBG collateral.

agenda_items.title: Failed and Struggling Developments: Surety Bond Enforcement and Option 3 Consensus
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle section omitted in the digest, Council, Engineering staff, and City Attorney Patrick Baker examined stalled subdivisions (including Stone Hill Estates) where developers defaulted since 2008 and surety companies contested bond language or penal sums. Council reached consensus on Option 3: conducting at least monthly joint Engineering and City Attorney meetings, shortening cure timelines, pursuing judicial enforcement against sureties when necessary, working with homeowners on prioritized repairs, and bringing contracts and special assessments to Council.

agenda_items.title: Bridge Lighting Maintenance and General Assembly Legislative Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported on intermittent cyclic failures in bridge lighting, noting a defective section had been shipped back to the manufacturer in China. Legislative liaison Karmisha Wallace then briefed Council on state bills including the Small Business Enterprise bill, Sen. McKissick's 'Ban the Box' bill, 911 recordings legislation, pistol permits, high-speed rail funding (following Mayor Bell's testimony in Raleigh), gas tax proposals, Durham's addition to the local stormwater utility fee bill via Rep. Luebke's amendment, voter ID legislation, and involuntary annexation bills.

agenda_items.title: Setting the April 18, 2011 City Council Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted by voice vote to set the April 18, 2011 agenda with Consent items 2-4 and 6-10 (moving Item 5 to May 2), no General Business Agenda items, and GBA Public Hearing items 14-19 (with Item 15 to be opened and continued). Council also noted expectations that up to 120 speakers might attend the April 18 Downtown BID public hearing.

votes.item_title: Setting the April 18, 2011 Regular City Council Agenda
votes.notes: Passed by voice vote ('all in favor say aye... motion passes'); exact headcount at the end of the long work session was not stated in the digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Set the April 18 agenda with Consent items 2-4 and 6-10 (Item 5 moved to May 2) and GBA Public Hearing items 14-19 (Item 15 opened and continued).

disagreements.meeting_title: Special City Council Meeting - Southside Revitalization and City Council Work Session
disagreements.issue: Southside Revitalization / Rolling Hills Phase 1 Section 108 Loan and CDBG Exposure
disagreements.summary: Council Member Eugene Brown challenged staff's preferred option to finance Rolling Hills Phase 1 site preparation and infrastructure via a 20-year Section 108 loan backed by CDBG funds and non-CDBG city collateral, citing severe federal CDBG cut risks.
disagreements.side_a_position: Proceed as planned with Rolling Hills Phase 1 using a 20-year Section 108 loan ($3.9M for infrastructure) to leverage $48.5M in mixed-income redevelopment.
side_a_arguments: Proceeding as planned achieves the transformative RFQ objective, reconnects Rolling Hills to Southside, paves the way for Whitted School, Heritage Square, and Fayette Place, and addresses affordable rental housing needs.
Stretching the Section 108 loan to the 20-year maximum produces the lowest annual debt service obligation.
disagreements.side_b_position: Question or oppose locking the city into a 20-year CDBG-dependent Section 108 commitment collateralized by non-CDBG city funds.
side_b_arguments: A new Congressional majority already passed HR 1 in the House proposing a 62% cut to CDBG funding, which narrowly failed in the Senate.
If CDBG funding is cut or eliminated over the next 20 years, the city's non-CDBG collateral requirement would force Durham to pay roughly $750,000 per year out of local funds.
disagreements.resolution: Informational special meeting deliberation; no formal vote was taken on April 7, 2011 (the item later returned for formal action on May 2, 2011).

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 4, 2011 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council issued five proclamations—recognizing Week of the Young Child, Public Safety Telecommunicators, Fair Housing Month, Time Warner Cable's 'Connect a Million Minds' STEM week, and youth mental health/anti-violence initiatives—and voted unanimously (7-0) on every agenda action. Council approved a closed-session request for attorney-client consultation, adopted the Consent Agenda (excluding pulled Item 9) covering the Brownfields job training contract with Durham Tech, Water/Sewer Revenue Bonds Series 2011, Carolina Theatre/Arts Council CMAR amendments, and parking management services, and confirmed a Yorkshire Drive mini-assessment roll (7-0). Following public hearings, Council unanimously approved amendments to the Economic Development Financial Assistance and Job Creation Policy (7-0) to expand signage and facade grant flexibility, and approved pulled Item 9 awarding the police in-car video camera contract to Coban Technologies (7-0) after addressing a resident's question on local IT contracting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Silent Meditation, Pledge of Allegiance, Roll Call, and Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:05 PM, Howard Clement III led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven members answered roll call. Council presented proclamations for Week of the Young Child, Durham Emergency Communications Center (DECC) dispatchers, Fair Housing Month (with Human Relations Manager Jolly Donaldson announcing an April 18 Open House and April 21 HUD seminar), Time Warner Cable's 'Connect a Million Minds' STEM week, and youth mental health/safe communities.

agenda_items.title: City Attorney Priority Item: Closed Session Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager and City Clerk reported no priority items. The City Attorney requested a closed session at the end of the meeting for attorney-client consultation under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), which Council approved 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Excluding Pulled Item 9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Item 9 (Coban Technologies) pulled for discussion, Council voted 7-0 to adopt the Consent Agenda, including minutes, 2010 board/committee attendance reports, February 2011 BID and collections audit reports, Durham Tech Foundation Brownfields job training contract, Water and Sewer Utility System Revenue Bonds Series 2011, Carolina Theatre/Arts Council CMAR amendment, Historic Preservation Commission agreement renewal, USGS stream/rainfall agreement, NCDOT track separation study (P-3309D), parking management amendment #2, and engineering design amendment #3.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Mini-Assessment Roll for Yorkshire Drive Dirt Street Opening
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater Manager Ed Venable recommended confirming the continued mini-assessment roll for the Summerlands property on Yorkshire Drive while relieving the Yorkwood Homeowners Association property until tap-on per city policy. No public speakers appeared; Council closed the hearing and approved the assessment roll 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Amendments to Economic Development Financial Assistance and Job Creation Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Kevin Dick (Office of Economic and Workforce Development) reported that since July 2010 nearly $565,000 in grants leveraged roughly 5-to-1 private investment across three funding rounds, and proposed amendments giving property owners flexibility to pair signage grants with facade improvements. One citizen speaker (Peterson) voiced support for small business expansion efforts, and Council approved the policy amendments 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Coban Technologies In-Car Video Camera System Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen speaker Peterson questioned why an IT contract for police in-car video cameras was awarded to Texas-based Coban Technologies rather than a Triangle-area firm. Staff explained Coban was selected as the specialized prime contractor for the in-car video system and any limited subcontracting remained at the prime contractor's discretion. meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 24, 2011 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, Council paused in memory of City Attorney Patrick Baker's father, Charles S. Baker Sr., heard Mayor Bell's report on NC Metropolitan Mayors Coalition work regarding state billboard, high-speed rail, and involuntary annexation bills, and approved the City Manager's priority items (including an $8.43M Lanier Parking Systems amendment and biweekly legislative briefings). Later in the session, Council unanimously voted by voice vote to suspend the rules and formally oppose North Carolina House Bill 351 and Senate Bill 833 (voter identification bills), citing high fiscal costs and negligible voter fraud. Council also debated Supplemental Item 19 on City-County homeless prevention governance and stakeholder consultation before unanimously suspending the rules and directing the City Manager to collaborate with the County Manager to implement the report's recommendations subject to parallel approval by the Durham Board of County Commissioners on April 4, then set the April 4 agenda.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:03 PM with a quorum confirmed (including Diane Catotti and Howard Clement III). Council observed a moment of silence in memory of Charles S. Baker Sr., father of City Attorney Patrick Baker, who passed away on March 23.

agenda_items.title: Mayor's Update on NC Metropolitan Mayors Coalition and State Legislation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: As chair of the 27-city NC Metropolitan Mayors Coalition, Mayor Bell updated Council on state legislative fronts: unanimous coalition opposition to proposed billboard legislation, a joint letter with the mayors of Raleigh and Richmond to President Obama and U.S. DOT Secretary Ray LaHood seeking reallocation of unused Florida high-speed rail funds to the Charlotte-to-Virginia corridor, and meetings with the NC House Speaker regarding a Senate-passed moratorium on involuntary annexations.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager presented priority modifications including Item 13 (Lanier Parking Systems contract amendment #2 adjusted to $8,430,761.21), a renovation presentation on Item 8 (Carolina Theatre and Arts Council building), supplemental Item 19 (homeless prevention), and biweekly legislative updates from Karmisha Wallace. Council approved the priority items by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Council Positions on State Voter ID Bills (HB 351 / S 833), High-Speed Rail, and HB 343
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following an omitted middle section, Council suspended the rules and voted unanimously by voice vote to oppose House Bill 351 and Senate Bill 833 (voter ID legislation), noting minimal documented fraud (~88 cases nationally) and unfunded budget costs, and directed staff to notify the local legislative delegation. Members also requested tracking high-speed rail funding and discussed church concerns regarding House Bill 343 affecting ESL classes, transportation, food, and shelter services.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Item: City-County Homeless Prevention Plan Implementation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated Supplemental Item 19 establishing a restructured City-County homeless prevention framework centered on accountability and avoiding conflicts of interest. After members questioned whether external stakeholders had been briefed and whether policy bullets would limit future Council discretion on board appointments, Council unanimously suspended the rules and adopted the staff recommendation directing the City Manager and County Manager to implement the report subject to similar action by the County Commissioners on April 4.

agenda_items.title: Setting the April 4, 2011 City Council Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Council Member Howard Clement III inquired about the semi-annual beer/wine privilege license review (scheduled for the May 13 work session), Council voted by voice vote to set the April 4 agenda with Consent items 1-13 and 16-17 (no GBA items; GBA Public Hearing items 16 and 17).

votes.item_title: Approval of City Manager's Priority Items
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote ('all in favor say aye'); full attendance count was not announced at roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved modifications to Item 13 (Lanier Parking Systems), Item 8 presentation, addition of Item 19 (homeless prevention), and regular legislative briefings.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules to Take a Position on House Bill 351 and Senate Bill 833 (Voter ID)
votes.notes: Voice vote ('Opposed? Motion passes unanimously').
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended work session rules to take formal Council action opposing state voter ID legislation (HB 351 and S 833).

votes.item_title: Formal Opposition to House Bill 351 and Senate Bill 833 (Voter ID) and Direction to Notify Delegation
votes.notes: Voice vote ('Opposed? Motion passes unanimously').
votes.discussion_detail: Directed staff to communicate Council's formal opposition to HB 351 and S 833 to Durham's state legislative delegation, citing cost and lack of demonstrated need.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules for Supplemental Item 19 (Homeless Prevention Plan)
votes.notes: Voice vote ('all in favor... those opposed, motion passes').
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended work session rules to act immediately on the City-County homeless prevention report.

votes.item_title: Direct City Manager to Implement Homeless Prevention Report with County Manager Subject to BOCC April 4 Action (Item 19)
votes.notes: Voice vote ('indicate by saying aye... those opposed, motion passes').
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted page-two memo recommendation directing the City Manager, in collaboration with the County Manager, to implement the homeless prevention report subject to similar approval by the Durham Board of County Commissioners on April 4, 2011.

votes.item_title: Setting the April 4, 2011 Regular City Council Agenda
votes.notes: Voice vote ('all in favor of the motion indicate by the sign aye... no opposed').
votes.discussion_detail: Set the April 4 agenda with Consent items 1-13 and 16-17, no GBA items, and GBA Public Hearing items 16 and 17.

disagreements.issue: Timing, Stakeholder Consultation, and Governance Scope for Supplemental Item 19 (Homeless Prevention Plan)
disagreements.summary: Council members debated whether to suspend the rules and immediately authorize implementation of the City-County homeless prevention restructuring report before external stakeholders reviewed the draft or before resolving appointment discretion details.
disagreements.side_a_position: Suspend the rules and authorize staff immediately to advance accountability and conflict-of-interest reforms in homeless prevention.
side_a_arguments: The framework addresses long-standing accountability and conflict-of-interest challenges and establishes a solid base to put staff in place.
Opposition from those resistant to change is expected, and delaying further stalls contractual coordination with the county.
disagreements.side_b_position: Clarify whether affected stakeholders saw the proposal and avoid locking future Council appointment discretion into the document.
side_b_arguments: Members asked who had been party to the draft and cautioned against incorporating policy bullets that could restrict future Council appointment latitude.
Action should authorize contractual moves while bringing detailed governance recommendations back and coordinating with County Commissioners.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved unanimously by adopting the recommendation subject to parallel action by the Durham Board of County Commissioners at their April 4 work session.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 21, 2011 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council recognized Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc. and school board member Omega Curtis Parker before approving the City Manager's priority items (7-0) and Consent Agenda excluding pulled Item 13 (7-0). Council heard public opposition to NCDOT's 90-foot Alston Avenue widening proposal (Item 14, U-2308) and later unanimously (7-0) adopted UDO environmental text amendment TC 10003 expanding tree protection standards, permanently closed Kelsey Street (ST 10008, 7-0), and approved Durham Tech's 1522 Lawson Street rezoning (Z 10013, 7-0). After initially tabling Diane Catotti's early clarifying motion (7-0), Council removed Supplemental Item 25 from the table (7-0) and unanimously (7-0) adopted the FY 2011-12 Budget Development Guidelines with Catotti's amendment specifying $437,500 per year over four years for Southwest Central and Northeast Central Durham housing activities. Council then voted on pulled Item 13 (rescinding a 2007 Umstead Road sewer order at neighbors' request) and concluded with a lighthearted failed motion by Howard Clement III to be excused for not wearing a tie.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, Roll Call, and Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:02 PM, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven members answered roll call. Council presented a proclamation recognizing the Durham Alumnae Chapter of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc. for voter registration and youth mentoring programs, and acknowledged Durham Public Schools Board of Education member Omega Curtis Parker in the audience.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager noted supplemental information at Council's places for Item 14 (U-2308 Alston Avenue widening) and a wording clarification on the final bullet of Item 25 (FY 2011-12 Budget Development Guidelines) regarding funding for existing housing activities in Southwest Central and Northeast Central Durham through FY 2012-16. Council approved the priority items 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Excluding Pulled Item 13)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Item 13 pulled for public comment and discussion, Council voted 7-0 to approve the Consent Agenda, including minutes, board/committee appointments, the Q2 FY 2011 mortgage loan portfolio report, the 2011-12 annual insurance plan, ARRA Third Fork Creek Trail Phase 1B and Leigh Farm Park design amendments, surplus property sales at 104 Flora Drive and 102 Morris Street, BPs 2 LLC lighting license agreement, Andrew Avenue streetscape and Carver Street extension engineering contracts, Automatic Passenger Counters, and the Durham Walks Plan follow-up report.

agenda_items.title: Procedural Tabling of Early Motion on FY 2011-12 Budget Development Guidelines
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Diane Catotti moved to clarify the final bullet of Item 25 to explicitly commit $437,500 per year over four years for Southwest Central and Northeast Central Durham housing activities. Because Item 25 was a General Business Agenda item not yet reached on the order of business, Council voted 7-0 to table the item until its proper place on the agenda.

agenda_items.title: U-2308 Alston Avenue Widening Project Update and Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Director Mark Ahrendsen presented a supplemental memo summarizing post-hearing discussions with NCDOT (including Durham's request for one through-lane in each direction). Wall Street resident Anthony Maglione spoke against NCDOT's 90-foot-wide widening plan, retaining walls, medians blocking left turns, and street closures, arguing it would create a mini-freeway severing the neighborhood.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC 10003 (Environmental Enhancements / Tree Protection)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle section omitted in the digest, Planning staff presented TC 10003, the third environmental UDO text amendment (recommended 12-0 by the Planning Commission on November 9, 2010), expanding tree coverage to the urban tier, crediting smaller trees, allowing flexible tree-save dimensions, modifying allowed uses and survey rules, and incentivizing specimen tree protection. With no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and adopted the amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Street Closing of 516.59 Linear Feet of Kelsey Street (ST 10008)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff (Steve Medlin) recommended permanently closing the entire 516.59 linear feet of Kelsey Street between Winton Road and Alpine Road, certifying proper statutory notice and finding no denial of property access. With no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and approved the street closing 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change for Durham Technical Community College (Z 10013)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Durham Technical Community College's request to rezone a 0.6238-acre tract at 1522 Lawson Street from Office Institutional with a development plan to Industrial Light to remove the existing development plan. With no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and approved the rezoning 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Item 25: Adoption of FY 2011-12 Budget Development Guidelines
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to remove Item 25 from the table. Council Member Diane Catotti then moved to adopt the FY 2011-12 Budget Development Guidelines with an added clarification committing '$437,500 per year over four years' ($1.75M total discussed at the budget retreat) to complete existing housing activities in Southwest Central and Northeast Central Durham; the motion passed 7-0.

meetings.title: City Council Budget Retreat and City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 10, 2011 City Council Budget Retreat and Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, Council received updates on the 'Durham's Got It' strategic plan and employee/website engagement, a water and sewer rate model update projecting a $33M FY12 capital budget ($250M over five years, $200M in planned revenue bonds, and up to a 5% cumulative rate increase for Falls and Jordan Lake compliance), and a stormwater utility model presentation (~$11M annual budget). After an omitted middle section, Council reviewed sidewalk priority lists—with Diane Catotti and Cora Cole-McFadden's concerns incorporated by consensus—and a guaranteed energy savings performance contract schedule leading to an April-June investment-grade audit. In the afternoon work session, Deputy City Manager Wanda Page and DDI briefed Council on revised Downtown Business Improvement District (BID) boundaries, statutory mailings to over 7,100 business personal property owners, and an April 18 public hearing calendar, after which Council voted by voice vote to suspend the rules on Supplemental Item 24, announced Housing Appeals Board nominations, and set the March 21 agenda by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and STARS Recognition Invitation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the second budget retreat to order and the City Clerk called the roll, with Mayor Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, and seated members answering. Vicky Atkinson (Budget and Management Services) invited Council to the inaugural STARS employee recognition luncheon on April 19.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Update and Website Engagement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated Council on strategic plan initiatives, including December employee engagement surveys and a 14-member working group collaborating with TS Public Affairs on city website development.

agenda_items.title: Water and Sewer Rate Model and Stormwater Utility Model Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: John Greeley presented the water and sewer rate model, highlighting Falls Lake and Jordan Lake nutrient management costs, a $33M upcoming capital budget ($250M over five years), $60M in revenue bonds this year plus $140M in two years, and a maximum projected 5% rate increase for FY12 before formal May adoption. Deputy City Manager Ted Voorhees then opened the stormwater utility presentation covering an ~$11M annual budget funding 92 FTEs.

agenda_items.title: Sidewalk Priorities and Guaranteed Energy Savings Performance Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle section omitted in the digest, Council incorporated by consensus sidewalk concerns raised by Diane Catotti and Cora Cole-McFadden, with Catotti clarifying that citizen sidewalk petitions should remain eligible if residents pay 100% of the cost. Staff also outlined the timeline for an investment-grade energy audit (April-June), financing review (July), fall approvals, and January 2012 energy upgrades backed by guaranteed 10-to-15-year savings.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Item: Downtown Business Improvement District (BID) Boundary, Notice, and Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy City Manager Wanda Page and DDI's Bill Kalkhof updated Council on removing specified residential condominiums and Durham School of the Arts from the proposed BID boundaries, mailing statutory 4-week public hearing notices to real property owners and over 7,100 Durham business personal property owners, and targeting an April 18 public hearing with a final vote before June 30. To meet the next-Friday mailing deadline, Council moved and seconded a motion to suspend the rules on Supplemental Item 24, while members requested further review of boundary maps ahead of the public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Housing Appeals Board Nominations and Setting the March 21 Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff announced Housing Appeals Board nomination results (Peter Keats with five votes for regular member and Candice Bronson with two votes), noting Council would decide whether to re-advertise or place the runner-up in the alternate seat. Council then voted by voice vote to set the March 21, 2011 agenda (Consent items 1-13 and 16-17; GBA item 14; GBA Public Hearing items 19-22).

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules on Supplemental Item 24 (Downtown Business Improvement District Notice and Report Preparation)
votes.notes: Motion and second recorded at 05:49:47-05:49:50 followed by further boundary discussion; formal roll-call tally was not spoken in the digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Requested rule suspension so staff could prepare the statutory report and mail four-week public hearing notices the following Friday ahead of an April 18 public hearing.

votes.item_title: Setting the March 21, 2011 Regular City Council Agenda
votes.notes: Moved and seconded at 05:53:06; passed without recorded opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Set March 21 agenda with Consent items 1-13 and 16-17, GBA item 14, and GBA Public Hearing items 19-22.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 7, 2011 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council proclaimed American Red Cross Month, recognized graduates of the Employee Development Forklift Training Course in partnership with the NC Department of Corrections, and acted unanimously (7-0) on all recorded votes. Early in the meeting, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden moved Item 20 (Upper Neuse River Basin Association dues, doubled due to Falls Lake rules and funded via stormwater fees), which passed 7-0, and Council approved the Consent Agenda excluding pulled Item 8 (7-0). Following a public hearing on Yorkshire Drive assessment rolls (Item 16, with two objections proposed for deferral) and a public hearing on the proposed FY 2011-12 Budget and FY 2012-17 CIP (Item 17, where residents raised 2K/3K homebuyer rehab red tape and nonprofit property taxes), Council approved pulled Item 8—a license agreement for Freudenberg IT's private fiber optic cable across 2,500 feet of city right-of-way—by a 7-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, Roll Call, and American Red Cross Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:02 PM, Howard Clement III led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven members were present at roll call. Council presented an American Red Cross Month proclamation to Mark Enozin, recognizing disaster relief, blood collection, and safety training across Durham and Orange counties.

agenda_items.title: Council Remarks and Early Vote on Upper Neuse River Basin Association Dues
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Howard Clement III congratulated four graduates of the second Employee Development Forklift Training Course run with the NC Department of Corrections. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden then brought forward Item 20, explaining that Falls Lake rules doubled the City's Upper Neuse River Basin Association dues, funded from stormwater fees, and moved approval so staff could leave early; Council passed the item 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Excluding Pulled Item 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no priority items from the Manager, Attorney, or Clerk, Council pulled Item 8 and voted 7-0 to approve the remaining Consent Agenda, including Equal Business Opportunity and Citizens Advisory Committee appointments, January 2011 BID report, street acceptances, Carolina Theatre Phase II CMAR amendment #21, Contract SW-26 (2011 sidewalk construction), street repaving testing, Southern Reinforcing Main Phase 2 amendment #1, site improvements Phase 1 design contract, and on-call master service agreements.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Confirmation of Assessment Roll for Yorkshire Drive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater staff (Michael Hughes and Dave McHenry) presented the assessment roll for a minimum dirt street opening on Yorkshire Drive, recommending confirmation except for objections from David Summerland and the Yorkwood Homeowners Association (exempt open-space lot), which staff proposed deferring to a future meeting.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Proposed FY 2011-12 Budget and FY 2012-17 Capital Improvement Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle section omitted in the digest, speakers addressed affordable housing priorities, lender delays with Community Development deeds of trust in the 2K/3K rehab program, and property tax bills charged to nonprofits renovating city-transferred houses such as the Guthrie House (which Mayor Bell noted fall under County Tax Office jurisdiction). Council Member Eugene Brown requested a staff follow-up on the 2K/3K rehab issues for Thursday's budget retreat, and City Manager Tom Bonfield confirmed a report would be distributed and posted online.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Freudenberg IT Fiber Optic Data Center License Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen speaker Peterson asked whether local Durham subcontractors and youth could participate in fiber installation/splicing and inquired about broader municipal broadband access. City Manager and Assistant Engineering Manager Robert Joyner clarified that Freudenberg IT's 16,600-foot private fiber line connecting two data centers (with 2,500 feet on Park Knoll Drive in city right-of-way) was already largely constructed and undergoing after-the-fact permitting; Council approved the license agreement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Birthday Recognition and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden wished Council Member Howard Clement III a happy 77th birthday ahead of the weekend. The meeting adjourned at 7:54 PM.

votes.item_title: Upper Neuse River Basin Association Dues Funded by Stormwater Fees (Item 20)
votes.notes: Moved by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden; seconder was not named in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved doubled Upper Neuse River Basin Association dues driven by Falls Lake regulations, funded out of stormwater fees.

votes.item_title: License Agreement with Freudenberg IT for Data Center Telecommunications Fiber Line (Item 8)
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved right-of-way license agreement covering 2,500 linear feet on Park Knoll Drive as part of a private fiber link between two Freudenberg IT data centers.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 24, 2011 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden with five members present (after voting 5-0 by voice vote to excuse Mayor Bill Bell and Council Member Farad Ali), the Council acted unanimously on all procedural and action items. Council approved the City Manager's priority item (5-0), referred Item 1 (City Council minutes) back to the Clerk's Office (5-0), and voted 5-0 to refer NC House Bill 33—restricting acceptable forms of law enforcement ID and affecting Durham Police policy on the Matrícula Consular—to the City Attorney and City Manager for legal analysis. Council then suspended the rules (5-0) and approved Item 5 for additional police vehicle purchases (5-0), heard staff presentations on Parks and Recreation's 67-park utilization assessment and Planning's UDO environmental tree-protection text amendment (TC 10003), announced committee nominations, set the March 7 agenda (5-0), and voted to enter closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Excused Absences, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the work session to order with Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Howard Clement III, and Mike Woodard present, and Council voted 5-0 by voice vote to excuse Mayor Bill Bell and Farad Ali. Council approved the City Manager's priority request to suspend rules on Item 5 (police vehicle purchases), noted the City Attorney's 10-minute closed session request, and voted 5-0 to refer Item 1 (Council minutes) back to the City Clerk's Office.

agenda_items.title: Council Referral of NC House Bill 33 (Law Enforcement Identification) and Member Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A council member who testified earlier before the House General Government Committee reported that House Bill 33—limiting law enforcement to five acceptable IDs and targeting Durham Police recognition of the Matrícula Consular—passed committee 16-10 on a party-line vote with Rep. Paul Luebke leading opposition. Council voted 5-0 by voice vote to refer HB 33 to the City Attorney and City Manager for legal review (specifically Article 18 Section B on ordinances). Council Member Howard Clement III also praised Durham Congregations in Action youth programs and 11 Milestones culinary graduates.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Matters: Bike Station Concept and Statewide Energy Efficiency Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizens presented on developing a central bike station/alternative transportation hub in Durham and urged Council leadership in supporting draft state legislation for an independently administered statewide energy efficiency program funded by a small systems benefits charge to sustain low-income weatherization jobs.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Additional Police Vehicle Purchases and Consent Item Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reviewing consent items (Capital Program Advisory Committee appointments, Jan 2011 bid report, street acceptances, Carolina Theatre amendment #21, Freudenberg IT license agreement, SW-26 sidewalk contract, and water/sewer contracts), Council voted 5-0 by voice vote to suspend the rules and 5-0 to approve Item 5 (additional police vehicle purchases), while pulling Item 13 (on-call master service agreements) to check Durham firm participation.

agenda_items.title: Parks and Recreation Facility Utilization Assessment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Parks and Recreation staff presented an evaluation of all 67 city parks (dating back to Lakewood playground in 1924) using deed/title reviews and visitor counts. Staff highlighted low-use parcels, neighborhood adoption/management partnerships (such as Cleveland-Holloway and Carroll Street with Self-Help and the Community Land Trust), potential repurposing of eyesore lots for affordable housing, and upcoming early-March mowing schedules.

agenda_items.title: Planning Presentation: UDO Text Amendment TC 10003 (Tree Protection and Coverage Standards)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Aaron Cain and Ann Kramer presented the third environmental UDO text amendment (following erosion control and stream buffers), outlining five recommendations: expanding tree coverage to the urban tier (3% for residential projects of 4+ acres), crediting smaller trees, allowing flexible tree-save dimensions, modifying agricultural offsets, and incentivizing specimen tree protection while keeping the 80% undisturbed protection zone.

agenda_items.title: Committee Nominations, Setting the March 7 Agenda, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff announced five-vote committee nominations for T. Green and Capital Program Advisory Committee nominees Michael Christian and Pam Carrico. Council voted 5-0 by voice vote to set the March 7, 2011 agenda (Consent items 2-4 and 6-13; GBA Public Hearing items 16-17) and moved into closed session.

votes.notes: Voice vote with five members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Excused Mayor Bill Bell (Metropolitan Mayors Association) and Farad Ali (work-related absence).

votes.notes: Voice vote with five members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Referred Item 1 (City Council minutes) back to the City Clerk's Office for review.

votes.discussion_detail: Directed the City Attorney and City Manager to review House Bill 33 (particularly Article 18 Section B on ordinances) and report back on implications for Durham Police Department's identification policy.

votes.notes: Voice vote with five members present.

votes.notes: Voice vote with five members present; Bill Bell and Farad Ali excused absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved purchase of additional police vehicles following rule suspension.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 21, 2011 Durham City Council regular meeting, with all seven members present, Mayor Bill Bell and Council presented proclamations recognizing Boy Scouts of America Day and the 50th anniversary of the Peace Corps, and adopted by a 7-0 vote a supplemental resolution sponsored by Council Member Mike Woodard memorializing civic leader and attorney Edward Knox Poe III. During the business portion, the Police Chief briefed Council on department staffing at 96% capacity, a current Basic Law Enforcement Training academy class of 18 Durham officers, juvenile arrest statistics, domestic violence caseload pressures, and coordination with the state judicial and probation systems. Resident Victoria Peterson pulled Consent Agenda Items 14, 15, 16, and 17—representing more than $16 million in street repair and repaving contracts including ST-250 and ST-251—to question minority- and African-American-owned business tracking, prompting Mayor Bell to direct staff from the Office of Equal Opportunity and Equity Assurance to report back to both Ms. Peterson and Council before Council acted separately on those contracts. All recorded votes in the meeting were unanimous (7-0), with no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Ceremonial Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. with all seven Council members present: Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, and Council Members Farad Ali, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Howard Clement III, and Mike Woodard. Proclamations were presented recognizing Boy Scouts of America Day (noting over 2,800 hours of community service in Durham in 2010) and the North Carolina Peace Corps Association's 50th anniversary and Peace Corps Week at Duke University.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Memorializing Edward Knox Poe III (Priority Item Addition)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Mike Woodard joined Mayor Bell at the podium with members of the Poe family to read a resolution honoring Edward Knox Poe III, a lifelong Durham attorney, World War II veteran, and former State Bar and Durham County Bar president who passed away on February 6, 2011. Under Priority Items, the City Clerk noted the memorial resolution had been added as a supplemental item at Woodard's request, and Council voted 7-0 to add the priority item to the agenda.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read through the Consent Agenda, including DPAC Oversight Committee reappointments, Capital Program Advisory Committee appointments, multiple internal audit reports (inventory, information systems, IT, and external quality control review), special assessment interest rate recommendations, an FY 2010 budget amendment, multi-site park renovations, a 2011 fugitive apprehension task force grant, street repaving contracts ST-250 and ST-251, and an NCDOT FY 2011 transportation planning grant project order. A gap in the transcript digest occurred before the consent vote was recorded.

agenda_items.title: Durham Police Department Staffing, Crime, and Judicial System Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council questioned the Police Chief regarding department staffing levels (reported at 96%), the ongoing Basic Law Enforcement Training academy with 18 Durham recruits, and potential lateral-transfer academy classes. Members also discussed arrest follow-up data, state judicial underfunding, potential city budget support for an additional domestic violence district court judge, and juvenile arrests (747 total, with 93% involving ages 13-17) alongside gang-related activity.

agenda_items.title: Adoption of Supplemental Resolution Memorializing Edward Knox Poe III
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the police briefing, Council formally took up the supplemental resolution memorializing Edward Knox Poe III. The motion was properly moved, seconded, and approved 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items 14–17: Street Repair and Repaving Contracts (ST-250, ST-251, and Companion Contracts)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Victoria Peterson pulled Items 14, 15, 16, and 17—totaling over $16 million in street repair contracts—to question why African-American-owned firms were not tracked separately in subcontractor reporting. The City Manager referred Ms. Peterson to Ms. Giles in the Office of Equal Opportunity and Equity Assurance, and Mayor Bell directed staff to share that analysis with Council; Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden also sought clarification regarding Ms. Peterson's comments on male contractors before Council acted separately on Items 14–17 ahead of adjournment at 8:24 p.m.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Acted on separately (tallies inaudible in transcript)

meetings.title: City Council Budget Retreat
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 11, 2011 Durham City Council Budget Retreat, the City Manager opened the workshop using a four-piece puzzle framework—Structure, People, Process, and Resources—highlighting the three-portfolio management structure, the Culture of Service initiative, unanimous Council backing for the $1,000 employee bonus alongside a commitment to review salary adjustments in July, departmental strategic plans, SharePoint collaboration, and improved performance dashboards. Following a truncated middle section of the recording, Downtown Durham Inc. and Business Improvement District (BID) co-chairs, including Michael Goodmon of Capital Broadcasting and a PAC 5 co-facilitator, presented in support of establishing a downtown BID ahead of an anticipated April 18 Council vote. Council and the City Manager then discussed scheduling a closed session and debated the depth and timing of the retreat's housing strategies discussion regarding Rolling Hills and Southside redevelopment, with members requesting fuller data promised over the preceding 9 to 12 months. No formal votes or split votes were taken during this retreat session.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Opening Remarks: Organization, Workforce Compensation, Process, and Resource Management
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager welcomed Council to the first budget retreat and framed municipal operations around four puzzle pieces: Structure (three deputy-led portfolios: Administrative, Operations, and Community Building), People (thanking Council for unanimous support of the $1,000 employee bonus and pledging to examine salary adjustments with new revenues in July), Process (six departmental strategic plans, solid waste and capital project improvements, and SharePoint rollout), and Resources (quarterly reporting, website transparency, program prioritization, performance measures, and dashboards).

agenda_items.title: Downtown Durham Business Improvement District (BID) Presentation and Budget Timeline

The City Manager noted staff sought budget-guideline direction while keeping the BID policy decision distinct from general budget adoption deliberations.

agenda_items.title: Housing Strategies, Southside/Rolling Hills Redevelopment Discussion, and Closing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A Council member questioned whether 30 minutes was sufficient to discuss housing funding strategies and Rolling Hills/Southside redevelopment given outstanding information requests over the past 9 to 12 months, and emphasized reviewing existing rehabilitation funding, projected unit counts, and maintaining commitment to Southside. The City Manager clarified the item was intended as a philosophical policy conversation to inform budget guidelines ahead of the second budget retreat, before closing the retreat by returning to the puzzle metaphor.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 10, 2011 Durham City Council Work Session, Council unanimously approved priority items including the Campus Hills Park / I.R. Holmes Recreation Center upgrades construction agreement and an FY 2010-11 CIP budget amendment (Ordinance 14025), and heard staff briefings on ADA accessibility compliance (including the Holton Career and Resource Center). On a film festival beer-and-wine service item, Council passed both a motion to suspend the rules and the main motion by 6-1 voice votes, though the transcript digest did not record the names of the six Ayes or the single Nay. Council also held a substantive debate on codifying the city's 'ban the box' criminal-background hiring policy: Council Member Howard Clement III advocated strongly for a permanent ordinance, whereas Council Member Mike Woodard and the City Attorney favored an administrative directive or resolution, with Council Member Farad Ali suggesting a resolution flagging a future ordinance; Council directed the City Manager and City Attorney to review existing personnel ordinances and return with a recommendation.

disagreements.issue: Film Festival Beer and Wine Service Permit and Suspension of Rules
disagreements.summary: Following a speaker's request citing the film festival's 12-year track record of incident-free beer and wine service, Council split 6-1 on both suspending the rules to vote at the work session and approving the item.
disagreements.side_a_position: Suspend the rules and approve beer and wine service for the film festival.
side_a_arguments: Act in the interest of time at the work session.
Festival demonstrated a 12-year track record of beer and wine service without issue.
disagreements.side_b_position: Opposed suspending the rules and approving the item.
side_b_arguments: Single dissenting 'No' vote recorded by voice without floor remarks in the transcript.
disagreements.resolution: Both the procedural motion to suspend the rules and the main motion passed 6-1 by voice vote; individual member names were not identified in the transcript.

disagreements.issue: Codifying 'Ban the Box' Hiring Policy: Ordinance vs. Resolution
disagreements.summary: Council debated whether to codify Durham's 'ban the box' policy removing criminal-conviction questions from initial city employment applications via a permanent city ordinance or a Council resolution/administrative directive.
disagreements.side_a_position: Enact a permanent codified ordinance banning the box on city employment applications.
side_a_arguments: An ordinance creates a permanent legal standard not contingent on who serves as HR director or City Manager.
A resolution lacks the permanence and binding force of an ordinance.
disagreements.side_b_position: Adopt a Council resolution affirming current administrative practice (or pair a resolution with staff review of personnel ordinances).
side_b_arguments: City Attorney noted only 12-13 personnel policies are codified as ordinances while hundreds are handled via flexible City Manager directives.
A resolution can affirm current practice immediately and keep the issue on the Council's radar while staff evaluates ordinance options.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; Council directed the City Manager and City Attorney to review existing personnel ordinances and return with a recommendation.
