meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 7, 2011 Durham City Council regular meeting, with all seven members present, Mayor Bill Bell delivered his ninth annual State of the City address highlighting energy-efficient Maplewood affordable housing, Durham Performing Arts Center revenues ($1.2 million to the city and over $24 million in economic impact), the $20 million street-paving bond for 150 miles of roads, Durham's AAA bond rating, green and brownfields workforce training partnerships, Southside and Rolling Hills neighborhood revitalization, real-time bus arrival apps, and a reduced $4 million projected budget gap. Council also proclaimed February 2011 as Black History Month and heard an announcement for a campus sexual assault conference hosted by the Mayor's Task Force on Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault. On business items, Council unanimously approved the Consent Agenda (excluding Items 5 and 6) 7-0, and after public comments from Victoria Peterson and a representative of Triangle Citizens Rebuilding Communities' 'Fiber to the World' program advocating increased workforce training funds and city/county hiring of trainees, passed Items 5 and 6 unanimously by 7-0 votes. There were no split or contested votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m., Council Member Howard Clement III led the Pledge of Allegiance, and roll call confirmed all seven Council members present: Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, and Council Members Farad Ali, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Howard Clement III, and Mike Woodard.

agenda_items.title: Mayor's Ninth Annual State of the City Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented his ninth annual State of the City address covering Maplewood energy-efficient affordable housing, the 2010 Census, DPAC's second-year success ($1.2M net to the city, 10,000 season ticket holders, and $24M+ economic impact), a new interactive city website, the $20M street repaving bond, Durham's first three-year strategic plan, AAA bond rating, job creation and green/brownfields workforce grants, Southside/Rolling Hills revitalization, transit real-time apps and the Bull City Connector, and closing an estimated $4M budget gap while seeking to restore employee merit pay as revenues recover.

agenda_items.title: Black History Month Proclamation and Domestic Violence Task Force Announcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell proclaimed February 2011 as Black History Month in Durham and presented the proclamation to Ms. Donaldson. A campus subcommittee chair subsequently thanked Mayor Bell and co-chairs Council Member Mike Woodard and Human Relations Director Ivan Pena for leading the Mayor's Task Force on Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault and invited the public to an upcoming campus sexual assault conference.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Items 5 and 6)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read consent items including the Hope Valley Green HOA irrigation license agreement (Item 10), ESRI software maintenance agreement (Item 11), and 2010 Residential Water Meter Replacement Project Phase 2 Contract MR-60 (Item 12). Council voted 7-0 to approve the Consent Agenda with the exception of Items 5 and 6.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 5: Workforce Development / Employment and Training Grant
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speaker Victoria Peterson spoke on Item 5, expressing support for the city's roughly $400,000+ workforce development contribution while urging Council to expand future funding to train residents for employment and reduce homelessness and crime. Council approved Item 5 by a 7-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 6: Employment and Training Grant / Fiber to the World Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A representative of Triangle Citizens Rebuilding Communities thanked Council for workforce development funding that helped launch 'Fiber to the World' to train Durham residents in fiber-optic installation, and asked the city, county, and school system to hire program trainees. Council approved Item 6 by a 7-0 vote, welcomed visiting NCCU students, and adjourned at 8:01 p.m.

votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Victoria Peterson urged expanding future workforce training dollars.

votes.item_title: Pulled Consent Item 6: Employment and Training Grant
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Speaker from Triangle Citizens Rebuilding Communities urged local governments to hire 'Fiber to the World' trainees.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 27, 2011 Durham City Council Work Session, Council approved the City Manager's priority presentation items and the City Attorney's request for a closed session on a condemnation settlement (City of Durham v. Evans et al.), while Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden requested a staff report on CDBG-funded housing counseling agencies. Water Management Director Don Greeley presented Phase 2 of the Residential Water Meter Replacement Program (Contract MR-60), detailing the shift to automated radio-read meters, monthly billing transition, and an estimated $23-24 million total program cost within the CIP and rate model. On the Durham Convention Center management contract, Convention Center Authority Chair Patrick Byker reported that the Authority unanimously reaffirmed Global Spectrum over a revised Shaner Corporation proposal, and Council suspended the rules and voted unanimously to advance the recommendation to a February 7 joint City-County meeting. Council also heard a Fiber to the World update on pulled Item 5, set the upcoming meeting agenda, and entered closed session unanimously, with no split votes occurring.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell called the rescheduled work session to order at 1:04 p.m. and Council moved to excuse an absence (transcribed as 'Councilman Allen', matching Farad Ali), while Howard Clement III noted his support for the manager's recommendation despite a scheduling conflict. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority presentations (Items 8 and 12) and the City Attorney's closed-session request for City of Durham v. Evans et al. (10 CVS 7519), and Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden requested a report on agencies providing CDBG housing counseling.

agenda_items.title: Presentation: 2010 Residential Water Meter Replacement Program Phase 2 (Item 12)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management Director Don Greeley presented the automated meter reading (AMR) deployment covering Districts 4, 6, and 10, explaining parallel hand-read/AMR validation, meter box adjustments, and the planned transition from bimonthly to monthly billing with potential ordinance updates for delinquency timelines. He estimated total program costs across residential and commercial meters at $23 million to $24 million through 2012, funded in the CIP and water rate model.

agenda_items.title: Durham Convention Center Management Contract with Global Spectrum (Item 8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap in the transcript, speakers discussed interim booking coordination and separating the Convention Center's identity from the Marriott Hotel, noting the Joint City-County Committee's unanimous recommendation (with Cole-McFadden excused absent and Commissioner Brenda Howerton abstaining). Convention Center Authority Chair Patrick Byker confirmed the Authority unanimously reaffirmed Global Spectrum over a late revised bid from Shaner Corporation (with Commissioner Joe Bowser abstaining), and Council voted unanimously to suspend the rules and forward the recommendation to a February 7 joint meeting.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson updated Council on Triangle Citizens Rebuilding Communities and 'Fiber to the World' securing Cat-6 wiring work at Duke's University Towers for four to five trainees and seeking city/county IT contracts. Council then unanimously set the regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1-7 and 9-12) and voted unanimously to enter closed session.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 18, 2011 Durham City Council regular meeting, with Council Member Howard Clement III excused absent (5-0) and Council Member Farad Ali arriving later after a flight delay, Council presented proclamations for the 'Marry Durham' civic celebration and Hillside High School's undefeated 16-0 4A state championship football team. Council unanimously approved the Consent Agenda, Chalmers Street paving improvements (5-0), and $75,000 downtown/Parrish Street building improvement grants for Parrish Street Venture (5-0) and Empire Alliance LLC (5-0), and conducted a public hearing on a $75,000 grant for TND Capital Management LLC. Following an extended quasi-judicial hearing featuring neighborhood and PAC 1 procedural objections, Council voted 6-0 (with Farad Ali present) to approve both the Major Special Use Permit (with six special conditions, including odor control, spill/emergency plans, PAC 1/NECD outreach, and limiting vegetable oil to virgin oil) and the companion Major Site Plan (D1000128) for the Clean Green Headquarters Recycling Center. Council also formally adopted Ordinance Item 20 (6-0) rescheduling the January 20 work session to January 27 and voiced support for a City Manager memo authorizing a one-time bonus for full-time employees; no split votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Ceremonial Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. with five members present (Bell, Cole-McFadden, Brown, Catotti, Woodard). Council voted 5-0 to excuse Howard Clement III's absence and noted Farad Ali's flight delay; Council Member Woodard then presented a proclamation for the March 'Marry Durham' event, followed by a proclamation honoring Hillside High School's 16-0 4A State Championship football team.

agenda_items.title: Priority Item 20 and Consent Agenda

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 6, 2011 Durham City Council Work Session, with all seven members present, Council unanimously excused upcoming January 20 absences for Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, and Council Member Farad Ali, and suspended the rules to act on a roof and envelope assessment contract for eight city facilities alongside scheduling the second budget retreat for March 10. Following a truncated middle portion, Council received updates on the Durham Convention Center management agreement deal points with Global Spectrum ahead of a joint City-County review. Staff also delivered an extensive briefing on the newly approved Falls Lake Nutrient Management Rules—covering Stage 1 and Stage 2 reduction targets (40% nitrogen and 77% phosphorus by 2025), projected North Durham Water Reclamation Facility upgrade costs ($3 million to $13 million in Stage 1), and Upper Neuse River Basin Association monitoring—before Council unanimously set the next regular meeting agenda, with no split votes taken.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Absence Excusal, Priority Items, and Second Budget Retreat Scheduling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell called the work session to order with all seven members present, and Council voted unanimously to excuse planned January 20 absences for Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden, Council Member Ali, and Mayor Bell. Council suspended the rules for City Manager Priority Item 4 (roof and envelope assessment for eight city facilities), reviewed Consent Items 1-17, noted National League of Cities committee service by Cole-McFadden and Woodard, and discussed dates with Budget Director Bertha Johnson for the second budget retreat (ultimately confirming March 10 from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.).

agenda_items.title: Item 11: Durham Convention Center Management Agreement Deal Points (Global Spectrum)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle transcript gap, presenters discussed customer service measurement and employee training programs for the Durham Convention Center under Global Spectrum. Staff noted an upcoming Joint City-County meeting the next Tuesday would inform a joint management recommendation in late January or early February with ongoing budgetary implications.

agenda_items.title: Item 12: Falls Lake Nutrient Management Rules Summary and Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff briefed Council on the Environmental Management Commission's approval of Falls Lake nutrient management rules, including dropping the fertilizer rule, new development stormwater treatment requirements, Stage 1 and Stage 2 existing development reduction goals (40% nitrogen and 77% phosphorus by 2025), and Stage 1 North Durham Water Reclamation Facility costs ($3M-$13M). Council Members Ali and Woodard questioned how rezoning and new residential wastewater discharges are costed, and Deputy Manager Ted Voorhees outlined the Upper Neuse River Basin Association's 10-year lake monitoring effort ahead of a June 2012 target.

agenda_items.title: Set Next Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After confirming March 10 for the second budget retreat, Council unanimously voted to set the upcoming regular meeting agenda with Consent Items 1-3 and 5-10 and General Business Agenda Public Hearings 13-19, then adjourned.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 3, 2011 Durham City Council regular meeting, with all seven members present, Council unanimously approved (7-0) adding the 2011 Legislative Program (Item 21), the Consent Agenda (excluding Item 21), a 482-square-foot street closing (Item 15), and Zoning Map Change Z0900015 (Item 16). The centerpiece of the meeting was Item 17, a public hearing and contested vote on amending the Southwest Durham Urban Growth Area (UGA) boundary along the N.C. 751 corridor to align with a 2006 Planning Director watershed interpretation after state regulators advised Durham County had lacked authority to alter watershed lines administratively. On Item 17, Council split 5-2 to approve the UGA boundary amendment: Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, and Council Members Howard Clement III, Eugene Brown, and Farad Ali voted Aye, while Council Members Diane Catotti and Mike Woodard voted Nay after urging Council to delay the boundary extension until pending county litigation and utility extension questions were resolved. Council then unanimously adopted the 2011 Legislative Program (Item 21) by a 7-0 vote following questions from Victoria Peterson regarding small business enterprise authority and municipal broadband.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Priority Item 21 (2011 Legislative Program)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m., Council Member Howard Clement III led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven members answered roll call. Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden recognized judgeships, honored a local leader, and voiced disappointment that the NCCU marching band was not broadcast during the January 1 Rose Bowl parade; Council then voted 7-0 to add Supplemental Item 21 (2011 Legislative Program) as a priority item.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 21)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consent items included piggyback vehicle cab-and-chassis purchases (Item 8), sole-source surveillance equipment (Item 9), a residential energy efficiency contract amendment with Clean Energy Durham Inc. (Item 10), an NC DENR Adopt-a-Trail grant (Item 11), an HOA landscaping license agreement (Item 12), and the annual traffic signals maintenance agreement extension (Item 14). Council approved the Consent Agenda minus Item 21 by a 7-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Item 15: Street Closing (482 Square Feet)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported no identified issues and recommended closing 482 square feet of street/alley right-of-way. After brief appearances by Ron Harward and Mary Quinn with no council questions, Council closed the public hearing and approved the street closing 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 16: Zoning Map Change (Case Z0900015)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City-County Planning's Steve Medlin presented Case Z0900015 to revise a development plan, noting the Planning Commission recommended approval 7-5 in November 2010 and that unit counts remain capped. City DOT's Bill Judge confirmed the traffic impact analysis requires developer-funded roadway improvements and up to two traffic signals on Page Road if warranted; Council closed the hearing and approved the rezoning 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 17: Southwest Durham Urban Growth Area (UGA) Boundary Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Keith Luck of City-County Planning presented a resolution amending the Urban Growth Area boundary in Southwest Durham along NC 751 to align with a 2006 Planning Director interpretation regarding Jordan Lake normal pool elevation after NC DWQ faulted the county's administrative boundary change. Howard Clement III argued for extending the UGA to unlock jobs and tax revenue and Mayor Bell supported staff's technical review, while Diane Catotti and Mike Woodard urged delaying the UGA boundary shift due to ongoing county litigation and broader municipal service commitments; Council approved the amendment 5-2 (Catotti and Woodard voting No).

agenda_items.title: Pulled Item 21: 2011 Legislative Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 21 to ask whether the legislative agenda sought funding for small businesses and why broadband language was included. Staff clarified the local bill requests sought statutory authority to establish a small business enterprise program and local preference program (rather than direct funding) and aligned with the NC League of Municipalities in defending existing municipal broadband authority; Council adopted Item 21 by a 7-0 vote and adjourned at 9:11 p.m.

votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Added supplemental 2011 Legislative Program reviewed by the Legislative Committee.

votes.item_title: Item 15: Street Closing (482 Square Feet)
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Closed public hearing with no opposition; staff recommended approval.

votes.item_title: Item 16: Zoning Map Change (Case Z0900015)
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Development plan change with developer-funded Page Road improvements and traffic signals if warranted.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Resolution Amending Southwest Durham Urban Growth Area (UGA) Boundary
votes.notes: Passed 5-2; transcript explicitly states 'councilmember Catati voting no and councilmember would it voting no', with all seven members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Extended the UGA boundary west of NC 751 to include parcels from the 2006 Planning Director interpretation near the proposed 751 Assemblage project.

votes.item_title: Pulled Item 21: 2011 Legislative Program
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Confirmed legislative requests seek authority for small business enterprise and local preference programs and support municipal broadband authority.

disagreements.issue: Southwest Durham Urban Growth Area (UGA) Boundary Amendment Along NC 751
disagreements.summary: Council divided 5-2 over whether to amend the Urban Growth Area boundary in Southwest Durham to incorporate parcels near the proposed 751 Assemblage development.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the staff-recommended UGA boundary amendment now.
side_a_arguments: Planning staff rigorously reviewed the boundary and recommended aligning it with the 2006 watershed/normal-pool interpretation.
Extending the UGA allows consideration of future utility extension, job creation, and increased tax revenue.
Amending the UGA boundary does not obligate Council to extend water and sewer or approve rezoning without further review.
disagreements.side_b_position: Delay extending the UGA boundary pending resolution of the utility extension agreement and county litigation.
side_b_arguments: Extending the UGA is not legally required immediately and implicates all municipal services, not only water and sewer.
Council should wait for the outcome of the pending county lawsuit affecting the 751 project and reconsider the utility extension agreement first.
Expanding the UGA southward sets a long-term precedent encouraging additional development along the NC 751 corridor.
disagreements.resolution: Adopted 5-2, with Mayor Bell, Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden, and Council Members Clement, Brown, and Ali voting Aye, and Council Members Catotti and Woodard voting Nay.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 21, 2010 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council reviewed administrative, consent, and public-hearing items and heard citizen comments on water conservation, street lighting, and City Hall accessibility. Staff presented the $865,000 City Hall Plaza improvement project (Contract ST-243), noting that approximately one-quarter of the budget is ADA-driven while the remainder addresses aging water lines, storm drainage, and streetscaping. The primary policy conflict centered on Item 18, the utility extension agreement with Southern Durham Development Inc. for the 751 Assemblage: after debate over pending litigation, public emails, and developer financing and carrying costs, the Council voted 6-1 by voice/hand vote to refer Item 18 back to the administration until a more appropriate time (individual Aye and Nay member names were not read aloud in the transcript digest). In advisory board balloting, the Clerk reported unanimous 7-0 appointments for Wendy Clark, Ann Woodward, Jeffrey Baylor, and Cheryl Lord, and a 4-3 split vote selecting Scott Harmon (4 votes) over Chris Brazeau (3 votes) for the Design District Review Team (individual ballot votes were not read aloud in the transcript).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:03 p.m. and the Clerk confirmed all seven Council members were present. The City Manager flagged that Item 13 (City Hall Plaza improvements) would include a brief presentation, and the City Attorney requested a brief closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) regarding a supplemental memo on Item 18. Both priority requests were approved unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matters (Water Conservation, Street Lighting, and City Hall Accessibility)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Robin Jenkins of the Eno River Association spoke on water conservation and meter readings ahead of February billing comparisons, and additional citizens raised concerns regarding street lighting and pedestrian safety. Later during facility remarks, a speaker also flagged wheelchair accessibility barriers in the ground-floor women's restroom in City Hall.

agenda_items.title: Review of Consent and Public Hearing Agenda Items (Items 1–17)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent items including Council minutes, the November 2010 bid report, low-entry cab-and-chassis purchases, Police sole-source surveillance equipment, a Clean Energy Durham contract amendment, an Adopt-a-Trail grant, an Ellerbe Creek Preserve HOA traffic-circle landscaping agreement, and City Hall Plaza Contract ST-243. Public hearing items reviewed included a 482-square-foot Olive Street closing (SC100004), zoning map change Z090015, and the Southwest Durham Urban Growth Area (UGA) boundary amendment.

agenda_items.title: Item 13 Presentation: Contract ST-243 City Hall Plaza Improvements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented plans for City Hall Plaza enhancements, detailing safer crosswalk curb geometry tested for firefighting vehicle turning radii, landscaping, and reconfiguration of parking from 21 to 15 spaces with ADA-accessible spots. Responding to Council Member Eugene Brown's inquiry about the $865,000 budget, staff explained roughly one-quarter is strictly ADA-driven while the rest replaces an un-upgraded water line and resolves basement storm drainage flooding.

agenda_items.title: Item 18: Utility Extension Agreement with Southern Durham Development Inc. (751 Assemblage)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Steve Medlin explained that Item 18 depended on prior Council consideration of the Southwest Durham UGA boundary amendment (Item 17) reflecting a 2006 critical watershed determination. Council members debated intense public criticism, pending litigation, developer loan refinancing and carrying costs, and whether the city should wait before acting outside its current jurisdiction. Council voted 6-1 to refer Item 18 back to the administration until a more appropriate time, with staff confirming annexation fiscal analysis would return only as a report rather than a formal action item.

agenda_items.title: Convention Center Authority Update and Advisory Board Ballot Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated Council on Convention Center Authority board action moving toward legislative policy discussions on a new management contract. The Clerk then reported ballot votes for five advisory boards: Wendy Clark (7 votes), Ann Woodward (7 votes), Jeffrey Baylor (7 votes), Cheryl Lord (7 votes), and Scott Harmon (4 votes) over Chris Brazeau (3 votes) on the Design District Review Team.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (7-0 on four boards; 4-3 on Design District Review Team)

agenda_items.title: Setting the Agenda, Staff Introduction, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the next regular meeting agenda with Consent Items 1–14 and General Business Public Hearings 15–17 (excluding Item 18). Following a point of personal privilege introducing new Assistant City Attorney O'Toole (succeeding retiring attorney Ms. Sindelar), Council voted unanimously to enter closed session.

disagreements.issue: 751 Assemblage Utility Extension Agreement (Item 18) Timing and Litigation Hold
disagreements.summary: Council divided 6-1 over whether to refer the 751 Assemblage utility extension agreement back to the administration amid pending litigation and public controversy versus moving forward to mitigate developer economic and financing pressures.
disagreements.side_a_position: Refer Item 18 back to the administration until external litigation and procedural concerns are resolved cleanly.
side_a_arguments: Citizens felt the prior UGA and legal steps were manipulative and bombarded Council with emails questioning why the item was moving forward.
Council had already amended the UDO so similar UGA boundary disputes could not recur, and residents deserved a clean resolution.
disagreements.side_b_position: Avoid holding the project in abeyance due to economic development and bank financing pressures.
side_b_arguments: The property remained outside city jurisdiction pending annexation, and holding the agreement in abeyance played into opponents' hands while awaiting lawsuit resolution.
Delaying action carried economic implications and complicated loan refinancing in a difficult financing environment.
disagreements.resolution: Council voted 6-1 to refer Item 18 back to the administration (individual Aye and Nay member names were not identified in the transcript digest), with staff instructed to prepare an informational annexation fiscal report without scheduling formal public-hearing action.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 20, 2010 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, six members were present and Council Member Diane Catotti was granted an excused absence by a 6-0 vote. Ceremonial items included a Human Rights and Bill of Rights Day proclamation presented to El Centro Hispano referencing Durham's 2003 Bill of Rights Defense Resolution and 287(g) felony focus, as well as recognition of Keep Durham Beautiful America Recycles Day poster contest winners, while Council Member Howard Clement III and Mayor Bell congratulated Hillside High School (4A football) and Jordan High School (4A soccer) on their state championships. On the business agenda, Council voted 6-0 to refer Item 19 (Confirmation of Assessment Roll) back to the administration and voted 6-0 to adopt Consent Agenda Items 1–12 and 14–18 (including the Ethics Policy amendment, police asset forfeiture firearm lab funds, 10 DATA Access vehicles, and 5 hybrid buses). On pulled Consent Item 13 (Harvard Avenue sidewalk request), following citizen remarks about straw/pine needles placed across the road and staff's explanation of temporary erosion control, the Council approved Item 13 by a 5-1 split vote, with Ayes from Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, and Farad Ali and a Nay from Eugene Brown.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Proclamations, and Keep Durham Beautiful Awards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order and the Clerk confirmed six members present, with Council Member Diane Catotti requesting an excused absence. Mayor Bell presented a proclamation declaring December 20, 2010 as Human Rights and Bill of Rights Day to El Centro Hispano, reaffirming non-discrimination policies and the 287(g) focus on felons, and Keep Durham Beautiful awarded a $200 U.S. savings bond to Creekside Elementary student Catherine Aidan Rooney for her winning recycling calendar cover.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 9, 2010 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, Council approved priority items from the City Manager and City Attorney (including a closed session for attorney-client consultation) and heard citizen complaints regarding ADA egress and parking barriers at the Holton Career and Resource Center as well as expansion disputes between the Durham Farmers Market and Durham Central Park. Council reviewed the employee '20 Hours or 20 Bucks' Habitat for Humanity campaign and unanimously accepted the Durham City Council Ethics Policy amendment after questioning a past city purchase of a distressed soft-second-mortgage property. On pulled Item 13 (Harvard Avenue sidewalk request), members debated allocating roughly $650,000 from street-paving bid savings to Harvard Avenue—equivalent to 85% of a typical annual sidewalk budget—while six approved sidewalk petitions waited and the November street bond allocated zero dollars to sidewalks. Council reported unanimous 7-vote ballot selections for the RDU Airport Authority and Workforce Development Board, set the upcoming consent and public-hearing agenda, and entered closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Priority Items, and Advisory Board Term-Limit Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the work session to order and Council unanimously approved the Manager's priority updates (noting MADD would not appear) and the Attorney's request for a brief attorney-client closed session. During ballot distribution for the RDU Airport Authority and Workforce Development Board, Council discussed referring board term-limit rules to the Procedures Committee after noting a nominee's second reappointment beyond term limits.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (unanimous voice votes on priority items)

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matters: ADA Accessibility at Holton Center and City Facilities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Thomas raised ADA compliance and fire-safety concerns at the Holton Career and Resource Center, noting a second-floor gymnasium lacked ramp egress for wheelchair users and seniors, and reported chronic shortages of accessible parking across from City Hall and at a recent Mayor's disability luncheon. Staff committed to returning with an updated report at the first February work session.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matters: Durham Farmers Market Operations and Expansion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Farmers Market board members outlined vendor sourcing rules, food-justice initiatives, and licensing, while highlighting ongoing friction with Durham Central Park over market expansion across the street because the market is at capacity. Council asked City Manager Bonfield and City Attorney Patrick Baker to clarify the city's authority and property/ordinance boundaries.

agenda_items.title: Employee Habitat for Humanity '20 Hours or 20 Bucks' Initiative
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the annual employee volunteer drive aiming to contribute 2,000 volunteer hours and raise $4,500 to sponsor a Habitat for Humanity house across 12 participating city departments.

agenda_items.title: Durham City Council Ethics Policy Amendment and Past Mortgage Purchase Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained revisions reorganizing the ethics ordinance and resolution to align with state legislative updates. Council members questioned a past city acquisition of a property on which the city held a soft second mortgage prior to the real estate downturn, urging staff to avoid speculative property purchases in the future before unanimously approving the ethics item.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Item 13: Harvard Avenue Sidewalk Request and Sidewalk Funding Priorities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering staff explained that favorable street-paving bids left roughly $650,000 within the existing project and contingency budget to add sidewalks on sloped Harvard Avenue. Council members noted that this represented roughly 85% of a typical annual sidewalk budget while six approved petitions waited and the November street-resurfacing bond set aside $0 for sidewalks, urging staff to bring back a sidewalk priority update—especially sidewalks to schools—during budget workshops.

agenda_items.title: Board Ballot Results, Setting the Agenda, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk reported seven votes each for the RDU Airport Authority and Workforce Development Board appointments. Council unanimously set the regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1–6 and 10–18; GBA Public Hearing Item 19), confirmed the December 20–21 schedule, and moved into closed session.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Items
votes.notes: Voice vote approved without opposition; individual attendance count was not called aloud in the work session digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion approving the City Manager's priority items (noting Item 20 MADD absence and potential agenda adjustments).

votes.item_title: City Attorney Priority Item (Closed Session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.notes: Voice vote approved without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion approving the City Attorney's request for a brief attorney-client closed session.

votes.item_title: Durham City Council Ethics Policy Amendment
votes.notes: Voice vote approved without opposition; individual attendance count not called aloud.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to suspend rules/accept the City Council Ethics Policy revision aligning local code and resolution provisions with state law.

votes.item_title: Ballot Appointments to RDU Airport Authority and Workforce Development Board
votes.notes: 7-0 ballot totals announced by the Clerk.
votes.discussion_detail: Clerk reported 7 ballot votes for the RDU Airport Authority reappointment and 7 ballot votes for the Workforce Development Board appointment.

votes.item_title: Set Agenda (Consent Items 1–6 and 10–18; GBA Public Hearing Item 19)
votes.notes: Voice vote approved without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion setting the upcoming December 20 regular meeting agenda.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Voice vote at end of work session.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to move into closed session for attorney-client consultation.

disagreements.issue: Harvard Avenue Sidewalk Addition vs. Petitioned Sidewalk Backlog and School Sidewalk Priorities
disagreements.summary: Council members questioned using ~$650,000 in street-paving savings for a sidewalk on Harvard Avenue—not originally on the petition list—while six approved sidewalk petitions remained unfunded and the November street bond allocated zero dollars to sidewalks.
disagreements.side_a_position: Add the Harvard Avenue sidewalk now using existing paving contract savings and contingency.
side_a_arguments: Favorable construction bids left capacity inside the existing $650,000 project authorization.
Harvard Avenue has steep slopes and adjoining property grades that leave pedestrians with little room off the roadway, making it safer and more efficient to build while crews are already mobilized.
disagreements.side_b_position: Ensure equitable sidewalk funding priorities, address the six waiting approved petitions, and prioritize sidewalks near schools.
side_b_arguments: Harvard Avenue represented roughly 85% of a typical annual sidewalk budget while six approved petitions waited for funding.

The November street bond allocated 0% to sidewalks, and petition sidewalk funding ($100,000/year after a multi-year hiatus, at ~$50/linear foot) only covers about one multi-block project per year, leaving many schools without sidewalks.
disagreements.resolution: Staff agreed to return during the upcoming budget workshops with a comprehensive update on sidewalk funding, school sidewalk priorities, and high-pedestrian areas.

disagreements.issue: Advisory Board Term-Limit Policy on RDU Airport Authority Reappointment
disagreements.summary: Council members noted that the RDU Airport Authority reappointment was a second appointment beyond standard term limits and discussed referring term-limit rules to the Procedures Committee.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support the reappointment given strong performance as authority treasurer and lack of other applicants.
side_a_arguments: There were no competing applications, and the incumbent served effectively as treasurer for the authority.
disagreements.side_b_position: Review recurring term-limit exceptions through the Procedures Committee rather than repeatedly overriding policy ad hoc.
side_b_arguments: Repeatedly granting appointments beyond term limits warrants clarification by the Procedures Committee.
disagreements.resolution: Council cast 7 ballot votes for the appointment while concurring that term-limit procedures should be reviewed by the Procedures Committee.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the brief December 6, 2010 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, there were no ceremonial items and no priority items from the City Manager, City Attorney, or City Clerk. Council unanimously (7-0) approved the entire Consent Agenda (Items 1–11), including board and commission appointments, the October 2010 bid report, the FY 2010–2011 first quarter financial report, the transfer of nine city-owned lots in Northeast Central Durham to Habitat for Humanity of Durham, a passenger vehicle-for-hire ordinance amendment, an NC State University Triangle Regional Model agreement, and a construction contract for Phase 1 of the Raleigh Water Interconnection Project. Following a public hearing with no speakers, Council also voted 7-0 to adopt Item 14, the sixth round of technical text amendments to the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO), before concluding with remarks congratulating the Durham Bulls, Duke Blue Devils, and Hillside High School ahead of its December 11 state football championship game.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Pledge of Allegiance, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m., led a moment of silent meditation, and asked Council Member Howard Clement III to lead the Pledge of Allegiance. The City Clerk confirmed all seven Council members were present, and the Manager, Attorney, and Clerk reported no priority items.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1–11)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved all 11 consent items in a single 7-0 vote without pulling any items for separate discussion. Approved items included appointments to the Tourism Development Authority, Audit Services Oversight Committee, Recreation Advisory Commission, Citizens Advisory Committee, and Durham Housing Authority Board; the October 2010 bid report; the Q1 financial report; transfer of nine city-owned lots in Northeast Central Durham to Habitat for Humanity; a vehicle-for-hire ordinance amendment; a Triangle Regional Model support agreement with NC State University; and the Raleigh Water Interconnection Phase 1 construction contract.

agenda_items.title: Item 14 Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment — Technical Changes 6
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Steve Medlin presented the sixth omnibus technical text amendment since the Unified Development Ordinance took effect in January 2006, noting the changes were suggested by staff or required to conform with state law and received a 13-0 recommendation from the Planning Commission on October 12. With no speakers during the public hearing, Council closed the hearing and unanimously adopted the amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Council Remarks and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Brief closing remarks celebrated Durham's athletic successes—the Durham Bulls, Duke Blue Devils, and Hillside High School advancing to the December 11 state football championship—before the meeting adjourned at 7:06 p.m.

votes.item_title: Item 14: UDO Text Amendment — Technical Changes 6
votes.notes: Public hearing held with no speakers; passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Adoption of the sixth round of minor technical UDO text amendments recommended 13-0 by the Planning Commission.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 18, 2010 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden (with Council Members Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti arriving after the start), Council approved the City Attorney's priority request for three closed-session items covering judicial consultations and a personnel matter. Budget and Finance directors presented the FY 2011 First Quarter Financial Report, projecting a $5 million sales tax shortfall offset by departmental savings (primarily lapsed salaries and closed recreation centers) and a 13.5% FY 2010 ending fund balance. Staff also presented updates on the Durham Brownfields Assessment and Job Training Program and the NC 54 / I-40 Corridor Study, where residents requested sound barriers, cut-through traffic controls, and collector-street realignments ahead of the December 10 comment deadline. In a policy discussion over a proposed resolution supporting recognition of the Matricula Consular as valid identification—endorsed by Durham Police leadership for citation discretion during minor traffic stops—Council Member Howard Clement III requested additional data and moved the matter to the regular session General Business Agenda before Council set the upcoming agenda and entered closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden opened the work session, noting Council Members Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti would arrive shortly. The City Manager flagged that Item 7 (Q1 Financial Report) would have a presentation, and Council unanimously approved the City Attorney's priority request for three closed sessions under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(6).

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matters: 'Marry Durham' Civic Pride Resolution Request and Consent Agenda Preview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizens proposed a March 19 downtown civic-pride ceremony ('Marry Durham') and requested a Council resolution of support. Council then previewed agenda items including transferring Northeast Central Durham lots to Habitat for Humanity (pulled for a speaker), the vehicle-for-hire ordinance amendment, the NC State Triangle Regional Model agreement, the Raleigh Water Interconnection contract, and UDO Technical Changes 6.

agenda_items.title: Item 7 Presentation: FY 2011 First Quarter Financial Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson and Finance Director David Boyd reported that property taxes are not due until January while sales tax revenue is projected $5 million under budget. All departments were projected to finish under budget largely via lapsed salaries and recreation center closure savings (aside from a county tax-collection contract shortfall in Finance and a $270,000 Transportation amendment), with FY 2010 ending fund balance at 13.5% and FY 2011 projected at 12%–12.5% after a $1.6 million carryover amendment.

agenda_items.title: Item 12 Presentation: Durham Brownfields Assessment and Job Training Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported on the Brownfields Job Training partnership combining technical hard-skills training with soft-skills case management and stimulus-subsidized paid internships to connect Durham graduates with employment.

agenda_items.title: NC 54 / I-40 Corridor Study Presentation and Public Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation staff reviewed focus-group and public feedback showing broad support for transit investments, off-road bike/pedestrian paths, and widening NC 54 in Durham County, alongside concerns over land-use density. A resident urged adding sound barriers, cut-through traffic protections for Leigh Village, relocating the Crossland Drive collector street to the George King Road bed, and refining Southwest Durham Drive plans ahead of the December 8 TAC hearing and December 10 comment close.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting Recognition of the Matricula Consular as Valid Identification
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers and Deputy Police Chief explained that Police Chief Lopez supported treating the Mexican Matricula Consular card like other valid IDs (such as an out-of-state ID) to allow officer discretion on citations rather than two-hour jail transports for minor offenses (~100 citations/year), backed by Consulate-provided Lexan fraud-detection tools. After Council Member Howard Clement III asked for additional information on Durham County Sheriff and statewide municipal practices, the item was placed on the regular session General Business Agenda.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Fee Inquiry, Setting the Agenda, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A resident questioned an unexplained $10 fee and requested follow-up, which staff promised to report on in December. Council unanimously set the regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1–11 and GBA Public Hearing Item 14) and voted unanimously to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: City Attorney Priority Items (Closed Sessions under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(6))
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously among members present; Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti arrived after the start of the session.
votes.discussion_detail: Approval of the City Attorney's request for two judicial/attorney-client closed sessions and one personnel closed session.

votes.item_title: Set Agenda (Consent Items 1–11 and GBA Public Hearing Item 14)
votes.notes: Voice vote passed without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion setting Consent Items 1–11 and GBA Public Hearing Item 14 for the upcoming regular Council meeting.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Voice vote passed without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to enter closed session pursuant to the City Attorney's priority items.

disagreements.issue: Placement and Scope of Matricula Consular Identification Resolution
disagreements.summary: While advocates and police leadership supported adopting a resolution recognizing the Matricula Consular as valid ID during minor traffic stops, Council Member Howard Clement III sought additional information and deferred action to the regular session General Business Agenda.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support recognizing the Matricula Consular as valid identification to improve policing efficiency and community trust.
side_a_arguments: Police officers wrote roughly 100 citations/year for minor offenses like driving without a license; accepting valid consular ID lets officers complete a stop in ~10 minutes instead of spending over two hours on jail transport.
Police Chief Lopez reviewed the proposal, officers retain full arrest discretion, and the Consulate provided Lexan tools to detect fraudulent cards.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer final action to the regular session General Business Agenda for additional comparative data.
side_b_arguments: Questions remained about whether the Durham County Sheriff and other major North Carolina cities had adopted similar policies and how officers handle stops involving other non-licensed drivers such as 16-year-olds.
disagreements.resolution: Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden placed the item on the regular session General Business Agenda rather than voting in the work session.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 15, 2010 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council presented proclamations for GIS Day and the Southern Anti-Racism Network (SARN) honoring departing activist Teresa El-Amin, unanimously (7-0) approved the Consent Agenda (excluding pulled Item 12), and heard Police Chief Jose Lopez present the 2010 Third Quarter Crime Report showing a 7% rise in violent crime alongside a 49% violent-crime clearance rate and 2,846 warrants served by the new Warrant Squad. Council divided 5-2 to pass the resolution supporting recognition of the Matricula Consular as a valid form of identification (Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Mike Woodard, Diane Catotti, Farad Ali; Nays: Eugene Brown, Howard Clement III) after the City Attorney clarified it was a non-binding statement of support rather than an ordinance. Following a unanimous 7-0 vote ordering street, water, and sewer improvements on Lane Street and East Cornwallis Road (Item 17), Council divided 6-1 to approve Item 18, a five-year statutory vested rights determination for the 468-acre Bethpage Village and Chin Page Office Park projects exempting them from the November 4 riparian buffer ordinance amendments (Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, Farad Ali; Nay: Diane Catotti). Finally, Council voted 7-0 to approve pulled Consent Item 12 (a City Hall right-of-way fiber license agreement with Durham County) after rejecting claims that the city was excluded from regional fiber planning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Proclamations (GIS Day and Southern Anti-Racism Network)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order, Howard Clement III led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven members were present at roll call. Council presented proclamations for GIS Day and recognized the Southern Anti-Racism Network (SARN) and departing organizer Teresa El-Amin for her work on Durham's living wage and anti-sweatshop ordinances.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1–11, 13–15, 17, 19, Excluding Item 12)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the consent agenda excluding pulled Item 12 in a 7-0 vote, adopting minutes, the September 2010 bid report, the FY 2010–2011 carryover budget amendment and solid waste fund transfer, the Q1 mortgage loan report, CDBG subrecipient contracts for teen initiatives and Teen Court, certification of the November 2 special bond referendum results, the 2011 Council schedule, asset forfeiture funds, and utility extension agreements.

agenda_items.title: Item 16: 2010 Third Quarter Summary Crime Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Jose Lopez reported January–September 2010 crime figures showing a 7% increase in violent crime (driven by homicides and aggravated assaults while robberies decreased) and slightly lower property crime, with clearance rates of 49% for violent crime and 22% for property crime. Sworn staffing stood at 94% with 28 vacancies (plus 16 frozen positions), while the newly created Warrant Squad served 2,846 warrants on 1,019 individuals including 250 backlog warrants.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting Recognition of the Matricula Consular as Valid Identification
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before calling the vote, Mayor Bell asked the City Attorney to clarify for the record that the Matricula Consular resolution is a policy statement of Council support rather than a binding law, ordinance, or statute. Council then approved the resolution by a 5-2 vote.

agenda_items.title: Item 17 Public Hearing: Lane Street and East Cornwallis Road Utility and Paving Improvements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff recommended adopting resolutions ordering petitioned paving and water main improvements on Lane Street and a sewer main on East Cornwallis Road prompted by a Durham County Health Department notice of a failed septic system. With no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and approved the resolutions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 18 Public Hearing: Statutory Vested Rights Determination — Bethpage Village and Chin Page Office Park (VR10-01)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Steve Medlin presented a request by Tri-Properties Inc. and Crosland for a five-year statutory vested rights determination under UDO Section 8.5 (stream buffers) across 468 acres north of Chin Page Road, exempting the mixed-use project (up to 1 million sq ft office, 1,300 homes, and 150,000 sq ft retail) from riparian buffer revisions adopted November 4. Council Member Diane Catotti questioned the applicants about the November buffer rule changes covering underground stream gaps under 300 feet, and Council approved the vested rights determination 6-1.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 12: Durham County Fiber Right-of-Way and City Hall Lease License Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speaker Victoria Peterson objected that Durham County appeared to be leading the fiber agreement without a work-session review. The City Manager clarified that the license merely covers county fiber access into City Hall while the city (under Kerry Goode) leads a separate joint City-County-DPS shared fiber-ring study, after which Council approved Item 12 by a 7-0 vote.

votes.item_title: Resolution Supporting Recognition of the Matricula Consular as Valid Identification
votes.notes: Clerk announced motion passed 5-2 with Eugene Brown and Howard Clement III voting no.
votes.discussion_detail: Adoption of a non-binding policy resolution supporting recognition of the Matricula Consular as valid identification.

votes.item_title: Item 17: Resolutions Ordering Street, Water, and Sewer Improvements (Lane Street and East Cornwallis Road)
votes.notes: No public speakers; passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Public hearing item ordering petitioned paving/water main on Lane Street and sewer main on East Cornwallis Road due to a failed septic system.

votes.item_title: Item 18: Statutory Vested Rights Determination (VR10-01) — Bethpage Village and Chin Page Office Park
votes.notes: Passed 6-1 with Council Member Diane Catotti voting no.
votes.discussion_detail: Five-year statutory vested rights determination under UDO Section 8.5 (stream buffers) for a 468-acre mixed-use development, exempting it from the November 4 riparian buffer ordinance amendments.

votes.item_title: Pulled Item 12: License Agreement with Durham County for Fiber Access in Right-of-Way and City Hall
votes.notes: Passed 7-0 following citizen comment by Victoria Peterson and City Manager clarification.
votes.discussion_detail: Approval of right-of-way and City Hall fiber access license agreement with Durham County.

disagreements.issue: Resolution Supporting Recognition of the Matricula Consular as Valid Identification
disagreements.summary: Council voted 5-2 to adopt a non-binding policy resolution supporting recognition of the Matricula Consular as valid identification, with Eugene Brown and Howard Clement III dissenting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the resolution expressing Council support for accepting the Matricula Consular as valid identification.
side_a_arguments: The City Attorney confirmed the resolution is a non-binding statement of Council policy rather than a law or ordinance.
Police leadership had worked with advocates and indicated no objection to treating the card similarly to other valid forms of ID.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose adopting the Matricula Consular recognition resolution.
side_b_arguments: Eugene Brown and Howard Clement III had previously raised questions at work sessions regarding sheriff alignment, other North Carolina cities' practices, and minor traffic-stop enforcement.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 5-2.

disagreements.issue: Statutory Vested Rights Exemption from November 4 Riparian Buffer Amendments (Bethpage Village & Chin Page Office Park, VR10-01)
disagreements.summary: Council voted 6-1 to grant a five-year vested rights determination shielding a 468-acre mixed-use project from newly adopted riparian buffer rules, with Diane Catotti voting Nay.
disagreements.side_a_position: Grant the five-year statutory vested rights determination under the stream buffer rules contemplated in the 2008 master plan.
side_a_arguments: Staff determined the application met all statutory vested rights standards.
The developers argued the 50-foot buffer framework matched the 2008 master development plan and enabled a major mixed-use competitor to Brier Creek.
disagreements.side_b_position: Do not exempt the project from the recently adopted November 4 riparian buffer ordinance amendments.
side_b_arguments: Diane Catotti questioned the applicants specifically regarding the November riparian buffer text amendments, including buffering underground/interrupted stream gaps of 300 feet or less.
disagreements.resolution: Vested rights determination VR10-01 passed 6-1.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 4, 2010 City Council Work Session—opened by Mayor Bill Bell, who subsequently handed the gavel to Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden—Council unanimously excused Council Member Farad Ali's absence and discussed scheduling Citizens' Matters consistently at 1:00 p.m. while praising voter passage of the November 2 bond referendum. During consent agenda review, Council Member Eugene Brown criticized a five-year ePlus Group computer lease totaling roughly $377,000 compared to a $307,000 outright purchase price, and members inquired about applying the Governor's local-contracting executive order (told state enabling legislation would be required). On Item 20, following work with Monday's public-hearing speakers, Council unanimously suspended the rules and adopted Attachment C of the Unified Development Ordinance riparian buffers text amendment with one minor modification. On Item 19, after Deputy Police Chief remarks supporting recognition of the Matricula Consular as valid identification with Lexan verification tools, Council Member Howard Clement III requested additional data and Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden placed the resolution on the November 15 Regular Session General Business Agenda before Council unanimously set the meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Excused Absence for Farad Ali, and Citizens' Matters Scheduling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order, noted Council Member Eugene Brown was expected shortly, and led a unanimous vote granting an excused absence to Council Member Farad Ali. Council members discussed fixing Citizens' Matters at 1:00 p.m. so residents would not have to rearrange workdays when work sessions ran short, and commended the City Manager's educational role in the November 2 bond referendum passage.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (unanimous voice vote on excused absence)

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item and Transfer of Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager flagged Item 20 (Riparian Buffers text amendment) as a priority item and asked Council to reflect on the recent loss of parents by three department directors (including Kevin Dick and Devon Payne). Council unanimously approved the priority item, after which Mayor Bell asked Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden to chair the remainder of the session.

agenda_items.title: Review of Consent and Public Hearing Items (Local Contracting & Item 14 Computer Lease)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council previewed upcoming budget carryover, CDBG, bond certification, sewer, crime report, and vested rights items, and staff noted that the Governor's executive order on local purchasing applied only to state agencies without enabling legislation. On Item 14, Council Member Eugene Brown questioned paying ~$377,000 over a five-year ePlus Group lease for laptops and workstations worth ~$307,000 outright, urging capital-budget adjustments in future budgets to avoid losing ~$70,000 in leasing costs.

agenda_items.title: Item 20: UDO Text Amendment — Riparian Buffers (Attachment C)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff reviewed Section 8.5.7/8.5.8 riparian buffer language, confirming existing uses remain exempt, Durham's 50-foot buffer exceeds state minimums, and outside certified consultants could handle stream determinations. Reporting that staff had worked with Monday's two public-hearing speakers to resolve their concerns in Attachment C, Council unanimously suspended the rules and adopted Attachment C with one minor change.

agenda_items.title: Item 19: Matricula Consular Identification Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Advocates and a Deputy Police Chief explained that Police Chief Lopez supported recognizing the Matricula Consular as valid identification (like an out-of-state ID) while preserving officer discretion to cite or arrest, using Consulate-provided Lexan security cards to check authenticity. Council Member Eugene Brown asked which other North Carolina cities had adopted it and Council Member Howard Clement III requested additional information and full-session deliberation, leading Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden to place the resolution on the November 15 General Business Agenda.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the November 15 Regular Meeting agenda with Consent Items 1–15, General Business Agenda Items 16 and 19, and General Business Public Hearings 17–18.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Council Member Farad Ali
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously among members present at roll call; Eugene Brown arrived later in the session.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to grant an excused absence to Council Member Farad Ali.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Item (Item 20 Riparian Buffers Text Amendment)
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion approving the City Manager's priority item placing the Riparian Buffers UDO text amendment on the work session agenda for action.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules to Act on Item 20 (Riparian Buffers Text Amendment)
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to suspend Council rules to take final action on the Riparian Buffers UDO text amendment during the work session.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Adopt UDO Text Amendment — Riparian Buffers (Attachment C with One Change)
votes.notes: Voice vote passed without opposition; individual attendance count at 01:14 was not read aloud.
votes.discussion_detail: Adoption of Attachment C of the UDO Riparian Buffers text amendment with one minor modification following staff consultation with Monday's public hearing speakers.

votes.item_title: Set Agenda (Consent 1–15, GBA 16 and 19, GBA Public Hearings 17–18)
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion setting the November 15 Regular City Council Meeting agenda.

disagreements.issue: Leasing vs. Purchasing Computer Equipment (Item 14 — ePlus Group)
disagreements.summary: Council Member Eugene Brown criticized spending roughly $377,000 over five years to lease 25 laptops and two workstations rather than purchasing them outright for ~$307,000.
disagreements.side_a_position: Budget capital purchases or alternative installment structures in future cycles to avoid paying a ~$70,000 leasing premium.
side_a_arguments: Paying $377,000 over five years for equipment priced at $307,000 costs the city roughly $70,000 more than buying outright.
disagreements.side_b_position: Use five-year leasing when upfront capital funds are unavailable in the departmental budget.
side_b_arguments: Leasing spreads payments at one-fifth per year when the department lacks lump-sum purchase funds upfront, and staff has also reduced computer costs by extending equipment lifecycles and renegotiating Dell pricing.
disagreements.resolution: Left for consideration in future Capital Improvements / operating budget deliberations without halting the pending item.

disagreements.issue: Placement of Matricula Consular Resolution on Regular Session GBA
disagreements.summary: Council Member Howard Clement III requested additional background and full-council regular session deliberation on the Matricula Consular resolution rather than taking immediate action at the work session.
disagreements.side_a_position: Advance the Matricula Consular resolution promptly given police chief support and City Attorney revisions.
side_a_arguments: Chief Lopez met with citizens and expressed no objection, the Attorney's office reworked the draft, and advocates hoped for immediate passage.
disagreements.side_b_position: Move the resolution to the November 15 General Business Agenda and gather answers on statewide municipal and sheriff practices.
side_b_arguments: More information was needed on which other North Carolina cities adopted the policy, whether the Durham County Sheriff accepted it, and how minor traffic-stop citation discretion operates.
disagreements.resolution: Placed on the November 15 Regular Session General Business Agenda for debate and vote.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 1, 2010 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council presented a childhood literacy proclamation, recognized the fifth graduating class of the city's Basic Heavy Equipment Operator Training Course, and noted Durham's NC League of Municipalities Green Challenge advanced status. Council voted 7-0 to approve the Consent Agenda (including 800 MHz radio system upgrades, ARRA Third Fork Creek Trail and SW-25 contracts, Convention Center Phase 2 CMAR Amendment #2K, Twin Lakes Park expansion, and board appointments) and unanimously (7-0) approved Item 19, a $75,000 Building Improvement Grant for N. Cole Williams Attorney leveraging $212,500 in private investment in the Parrish Street area (with Items 20–21 in the middle section truncated in the digest). In the meeting's major contested public hearing on closing a street segment for Greystone Baptist Church's daycare and facility expansion, Old West Durham Neighborhood Association representatives opposed the street closure over neighborhood plan precedent and connectivity while church supporters emphasized youth and community services. Council Member Mike Woodard offered a substitute motion to approve the street closing with a committed 10-to-12-foot bike and pedestrian easement, which failed 2-5 (moved by Mike Woodard; individual electronic Aye and Nay member names were not read aloud in the transcript digest), after which Council unanimously (7-0) passed Howard Clement III's original motion to close the street.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Proclamations, and Employee Equipment Training Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order, Howard Clement III led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven members were present at roll call. Council presented a childhood literacy proclamation ('A Seed Day'), recognized seven Street Maintenance and Water & Sewer Maintenance employees completing the fifth Basic Heavy Equipment Operator Training Course, and highlighted Durham's NC League of Municipalities Green Challenge advanced-level status.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1–5, 7–14, 16–17)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no priority items from the Manager, Attorney, or Clerk, Council approved the entire Consent Agenda 7-0. Approved items included advisory board appointments, an 800 MHz radio system interlocal amendment with Durham County, ARRA Third Fork Creek Trail Phase 1B design amendment, Convention Center Phase 2 Amendment #2K with Skanska USA Building, a 2011 HUD grant award, Twin Lakes Park expansion, an NCDOT winter weather reimbursement contract, and ARRA Contract SW-25 amendment.

agenda_items.title: Item 19 Public Hearing: Building Improvement Grant — N. Cole Williams Attorney (Parrish Street Area)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic and Workforce Development Director Kevin Dick presented a $75,000 cost-reimbursement Building Improvement Grant for N. Cole Williams in the Parrish Street project area, requiring $212,500 in private capital investment to activate first-floor law office space under the May 17, 2010 policy, and noted a new application round closing November 12. With no public speakers, Council approved Item 19 by a 7-0 vote (subsequent public hearing items in the middle of the meeting were truncated in the digest).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Street Closing for Greystone Baptist Church Expansion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Greystone Baptist Church representatives and supporters highlighted decades of daycare and youth programming in West Durham, while Old West Durham Neighborhood Association representative Brett Walters supported the church's expansion but opposed closing the street as inconsistent with the Ninth Street / West Durham plan. Council Member Howard Clement III moved the street closing as requested, while Diane Catotti and Mike Woodard raised neighborhood communication, committed design elements, and bike/pedestrian connectivity; Woodard's substitute motion requiring a 10–12 foot connectivity easement failed 2-5 before Clement's original motion passed 7-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Substitute motion failed 2-5; Main motion passed 7-0

votes.item_title: Item 19: Economic Development Building Improvement Grant — N. Cole Williams Attorney
votes.notes: Public hearing closed with no speakers; passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Approval of $75,000 cost-reimbursement Building Improvement Grant leveraging $212,500 in private investment in the Parrish Street project area.

votes.item_title: Substitute Motion: Street Closing for Greystone Baptist Church with Committed 10-to-12-Foot Bike and Pedestrian Easement
votes.notes: Vote reopened after a member mis-pressed their button and failed 2-5. Mike Woodard is confirmed as the mover; the second Aye and five Nay names were not read aloud in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: Substitute motion by Mike Woodard to close the street subject to a committed 10-to-12-foot easement through the property preserving bicycle and pedestrian connectivity between Hillsborough Road and Main Street.

votes.item_title: Main Motion: Street Closing for Greystone Baptist Church Expansion
votes.notes: Passed unanimously 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Original motion by Howard Clement III to approve the street closing without the added easement condition after the substitute motion failed.

disagreements.issue: Greystone Baptist Church Street Closing vs. Neighborhood Plan Precedent and Bike/Pedestrian Easement
disagreements.summary: Neighborhood speakers opposed closing the street segment without connectivity safeguards, and Council rejected Mike Woodard's 2-5 substitute motion requiring a 10–12 foot bike/pedestrian easement before unanimously approving the unconditional street closing 7-0.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the street closing promptly without deferral or an added easement mandate to support Greystone Baptist Church's daycare expansion.
side_a_arguments: Demand for quality daycare exceeds supply in Durham, and neighborhood plans should be flexible rather than 'etched in stone.'

Church representatives warned that deferring action would cost thousands of dollars in pre-construction expenses, and nearby Warner Street/15th Street provided adjacent access between Hillsborough Road and Main Street.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer for neighborhood consultation or require committed design assurances and a 10–12 foot bike/pedestrian connectivity easement.
side_b_arguments: Old West Durham Neighborhood Association argued the street closing chipped away at the Ninth Street / West Durham plan and set a harmful precedent.
Retaining a 10–12 foot easement or committed site-plan elements would preserve bicycle and pedestrian connectivity between Hillsborough Road and Main Street.
disagreements.resolution: Mike Woodard's substitute motion for a committed 10–12 foot easement failed 2-5, and Council then approved Howard Clement III's main motion for the street closing 7-0.
