meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 21, 2010 City Council Work Session opened by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden (with Mayor Bill Bell and Council Member Mike Woodard arriving later in the session), Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority agenda flagging presentations on Items 12, 15, and 18. General Services presented Amendment #2K to the Skanska USA Building CMAR contract for the $6.5 million Convention Center Phase 2 renovation (split 50/50 with Durham County), detailing HVAC, lighting/sound, ballroom subdivisions, and a DOJ-mandated ADA lobby restroom while Council requested brighter interior renderings. On Item 15, the Revised Master Plan for Old North Durham Park, residents and Council debated perceived lack of public input and park access alongside staff explanations of a shallow diagonal storm drain and lack of capital funds, leading Council to refer the plan back to the City Manager's Office for broader community engagement. After hearing Southwest Central Durham residents urge continued HUD affordable housing funding—prompting Mayor Bell to caution against pitting neighborhoods against each other—Council unanimously suspended the rules to approve an Audit Services Oversight Committee appointment and set the November 1 meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Priority Items, and Consent Agenda Preview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the work session to order with five members present and noted Mayor Bell was on his way. Council unanimously approved the Manager's priority agenda (flagging presentations on Items 12, 15, and 18) and previewed advisory board appointments, the 800 MHz radio upgrade amendment, ARRA Third Fork Creek Trail and SW-25 amendments, Twin Lakes Park expansion, Building Improvement Grants, and Elementary School E initial zoning.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (unanimous voice vote on priority items)

agenda_items.title: Item 12 Presentation: Convention Center Phase 2 Renovation (Skanska USA Pre-GMP Amendment #2K)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the $6.5 million Convention Center Phase 2 renovation (split evenly at roughly $3.25 million each between the city and county), covering pre-function corridor upgrades, a DOJ-settlement ADA lobby restroom, pre-purchased chillers/HVAC, lighting and sound controls, and subdivisible meeting spaces. Council members criticized dark finish renderings on handout pages 10–11, and staff committed to providing brighter renderings while finalizing textured-wall pricing with Skanska USA.

agenda_items.title: Item 15: Revised Master Plan for Old North Durham Park
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle section omitted from the transcript digest, Council and residents debated public engagement and access for the Old North Durham Park Revised Master Plan. Parks staff noted there was no capital project funding and that a shallow diagonal storm drain prevented heavy field grading, after which Council moved to refer the plan back to the City Manager's Office to ensure neighborhood, PAC, and InterNeighborhood Council input.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Referred back to City Manager's Office

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matters: Southwest Central Durham HUD Affordable Housing Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A representative of Southwest Central Durham residents urged Council to maintain HUD-funded affordable housing and social services in the neighborhood. Mayor Bill Bell commented that he hoped funding deliberations would not appear to pit neighborhoods against one another.

agenda_items.title: Suspension of Rules, Audit Services Oversight Committee Appointment, and Setting the Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously suspended the rules and unanimously appointed a member to the Audit Services Oversight Committee so she could attend the committee's Monday meeting. Council then unanimously set the November 1 regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1–5, 7–14, 16–17 and GBA Public Hearings 19–25) before adjourning.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Items (Items 12, 15, and 18 Presentations)
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously among members present at start of work session.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion approving the City Manager's priority schedule for presentations on Items 12, 15, and 18.

votes.item_title: Suspend Rules for Immediate Appointment to Audit Services Oversight Committee
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to suspend Council rules so the Audit Services Oversight Committee appointee could serve at Monday's committee meeting.

votes.item_title: Audit Services Oversight Committee Appointment
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Approval of the Audit Services Oversight Committee appointment following rule suspension.

votes.item_title: Set November 1 Regular Meeting Agenda (Consent 1–5, 7–14, 16–17; GBA Public Hearings 19–25)
votes.notes: Voice vote passed unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion setting the upcoming November 1 Regular City Council Meeting agenda.

disagreements.issue: Old North Durham Park Revised Master Plan — Public Input, Park Access, and Field Conditions
disagreements.summary: Residents and Council members criticized inadequate community input on the Old North Durham Park Revised Master Plan and questioned future access and control, leading Council to pull it from the upcoming agenda and send it back to the City Manager's Office.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the revised master plan featuring a walking path, picnic shelter, and rainwater features while addressing drainage constraints.
side_a_arguments: Adopting the plan would not transfer ownership or public access away from the city, and a shallow diagonal storm drain limits heavy athletic-field grading without major capital funding.
disagreements.side_b_position: Refer the plan back to the City Manager's Office for inclusive PAC, InterNeighborhood Council, and neighborhood input.
side_b_arguments: Multiple residents testified they had no input into the proposed plan, indicating a flaw in the public outreach process.
Affirmative outreach through PACs and the InterNeighborhood Council is needed before Council acts on any master plan.
disagreements.resolution: Removed from the November 1 agenda and referred back to the City Manager's Office for further public engagement.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the October 18, 2010 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council Member Mike Woodard recognized Boy Scout Troop 405 and encouraged support for the November 2 bond referendum, while Council Member Howard Clement III thanked the Campaign for Decent Housing. Council unanimously (7-0) approved the City Manager's priority items—referring Item 13 (Strategic Plan adoption) back to administration and adding supplemental Item 17 (HTC America Innovation Inc. economic incentives)—and voted 7-0 to adopt Consent Agenda Items 1–8 and 10–12 (including the HUD VASH veteran housing voucher program, Friendly Rest Home project amendment, West Point at 751 LLC water/sewer extension agreement, UGA/utility extension ordinance amendment, and ePlus Group mobile data computer lease). Following public hearings, Council voted 7-0 to approve Item 14 (closing 4,253/42,053 square feet of Harmony Road for a Standard Pacific Carolinas subdivision realignment) and voted 7-0 to approve supplemental Item 17, an economic development incentive agreement with HTC America Innovation Inc. for high-wage mobile technology jobs in downtown Durham. Council concluded by unanimously (7-0) approving pulled Consent Item 9 (the 2010 Justice and Mental Health Collaboration Program planning grant) and reminding residents of early voting locations before adjourning at 7:35 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Council Member Comments (Boy Scout Troop 405 & Housing Tour)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order, Howard Clement III led the Pledge of Allegiance, and all seven members were confirmed present. Council Member Mike Woodard recognized Boy Scout Troop 405 from St. Matthew's Church and urged support for the November 2 street bond referendum, while Howard Clement III thanked the Campaign for Decent Housing for its annual meeting and tour.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Item 13 Referral & Supplemental Item 17)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to approve the City Manager's priority items: referring Item 13 (Adoption of Strategic Plan) back to the administration and adding supplemental Item 17 (public hearing on economic incentives with HTC America Innovation Inc.). Mayor Bell also asked the Clerk to post clear sign-up instructions for General Business Agenda speakers prior to 7:00 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1–8 and 10–12, Excluding Item 9)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to approve the consent agenda excluding pulled Item 9 and referred Item 13, covering minutes, a Human Relations Commission appointment, workers' compensation TPA contracts, a Fire Department donation, the HUD VASH veteran housing voucher program, Friendly Rest Home funding, asset forfeiture funds, the West Point at 751 LLC water/sewer extension agreement, a UGA utility extension ordinance amendment, and the ePlus Group mobile data computer lease.

agenda_items.title: Item 14 Public Hearing: Street Closing of Harmony Road (Standard Pacific Carolinas)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Steve Medlin presented a request by Standard Pacific Carolinas to close a portion of Harmony Road near Cook Road and Julia Drive to realign right-of-way for a single-family subdivision. With no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and approved the street closing 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Item 17 Public Hearing: Economic Development Incentive Agreement with HTC America Innovation Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic and Workforce Development Director Kevin Dick presented a proposed incentive contract with smartphone designer HTC America Innovation Inc. to bring high-wage jobs (reported at roughly $125,000 average salary with benefits) to downtown Durham. Following questions from Howard Clement III on local degree/training access and comments from four speakers (Bill Kalkhof, Keith Burns, Adam Klein, and Victoria Peterson), Council approved the agreement 7-0 and heard remarks from HTC Chief Strategy Officer Ron Loughson.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 9: 2010 Justice and Mental Health Collaboration Program Grant & Early Voting Reminder
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a speaker's inquiry regarding ex-offenders programming, staff clarified that this multi-agency DOJ planning grant prepares an implementation proposal competing to make Durham one of eight national pilot sites. Council unanimously approved Item 9 (7-0) and reminded residents of early voting sites before adjourning at 7:35 p.m.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden with six Council members answering roll call (Bill Bell absent), the Durham City Council Work Session focused on the City's draft Strategic Plan, routine departmental consent items, and a citizen environmental resolution. Budget and Management Services Director Bertha Johnson presented the three-tier Strategic Plan organized around five core goal areas, prompting extensive Council feedback on explicitly prioritizing poverty reduction, refining economic development language, using positive workforce input metrics, and addressing the City's deferred maintenance backlog identified in the Carter-Burgess study. Council also voted unanimously (6-0) by voice vote to support a resolution brought by the Blue Ridge Environmental Defense League pending confirmation by the Environmental Affairs Board prior to October 15, remanded a separate citizen matter to the City Manager, approved two closed sessions, and set the upcoming regular meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Manager's and City Attorney's Closed Session Requests
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the start of the work session, the City Manager requested a closed session to discuss the location or expansion of industries or other businesses in Durham. The City Attorney also requested a brief closed session for attorney-client consultation pursuant to NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3). Both priority requests were approved by unopposed voice votes.

agenda_items.title: Consent and Departmental Agenda Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden read through administrative consent and departmental items, including Council minutes (Item 1), Human Relations Commission appointment (Item 2), Community Development contract amendment with Circa (Item 3), workers' compensation TPA contract extension (Item 4), HUD Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing vouchers (Item 6), Friendly Rest Home capital project ordinance amendment (Item 7), Police asset forfeiture funds and Justice & Mental Health Collaboration grant (Items 8-9), Westpoint at 751 LLC water/sewer and Urban Growth Area ordinance items (Items 10-11), mobile data computer lease (Item 12), Strategic Plan (Item 13), and Harmony Road street closing public hearing (Item 14).

agenda_items.title: City of Durham Strategic Plan Presentation and Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget and Management Services Director Bertha Johnson presented the draft Strategic Plan structured across five goal areas (strong and diverse economy, safe and secure community, thriving livable neighborhoods, well-managed city, and stewardship of physical assets) and three accountability levels. Council members urged stronger, explicit prioritization of poverty reduction rather than burying it among bullets, suggested emphasizing businesses and arts/tourism alongside industry, and recommended positive employee training/diversity metrics. Council Member Eugene Brown pressed staff on how the deferred maintenance backlog from the Carter-Burgess study is prioritized when budget constraints act as a 'millstone,' and staff agreed to incorporate feedback and return in a couple of weeks.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Blue Ridge Environmental Defense League Resolution & Remanded Item
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following discussion on Item 15, Council voted to support a resolution presented by the Blue Ridge Environmental Defense League pending similar formal support from the Environmental Affairs Board (EAB) prior to the October 15 deadline, directing the City Clerk to certify Council's vote upon EAB concurrence. Council also noted that Item 16 (John Hunter) had been remanded to the City Manager, affecting four signed-up speakers.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda and Closed Session Entry
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council set the regular meeting agenda to include Consent Items 1 through 12 and General Business Agenda Public Hearing Item 14 (with no non-hearing GBA items). Following the agenda vote and noting ballot results for the Human Relations Commission, Council cleared the room to enter closed session with General Services and the City Attorney.

votes.item_title: City Manager's Priority Items (Closed Session for Business Location/Expansion)
votes.notes: Voice vote carried unopposed. Bill Bell did not answer the initial roll call (and had requested an excused absence at the October 4 meeting).
votes.discussion_detail: City Manager requested a closed session to discuss location or expansion of industries or other businesses in the city.

votes.item_title: City Attorney's Priority Item (Closed Session - Attorney-Client Consultation)
votes.notes: Voice vote carried unopposed with Bill Bell absent at roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: City Attorney requested a 2-to-5-minute closed session for attorney-client consultation pursuant to NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3).

votes.item_title: Item 15: Support for Blue Ridge Environmental Defense League Resolution Pending EAB Concurrence
votes.notes: Voice vote carried unopposed.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to support the resolution pending confirmation of similar support by the Environmental Affairs Board prior to October 15, with the Clerk authorized to certify Council's vote upon EAB concurrence.

votes.item_title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda (Consent Items 1-12 and GBA Public Hearing Item 14)
votes.notes: Voice vote carried unopposed.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to set the upcoming regular Council agenda with Consent Items 1 through 12 and GBA Public Hearing Item 14.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven Council members present, the October 4 Regular City Council Meeting opened with a series of community proclamations and recognitions, including Disability Awareness Month, 2010 Piedmont Laureate Zelda Lockhart, International Walk to School Day, and Durham's recognition among America's 100 Best Communities for Young People. In its legislative business, Council unanimously approved (7-0) a rezoning and subdivision plan for Carolina Outreach supported by the Tuscaloosa-Lakewood Neighborhood Association, adopted the Annual Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) of the Comprehensive Plan (7-0), and continued the Bethpage Village and Chin Page Office Park vested rights public hearing to November 15, 2010 (7-0). Council also addressed pulled consent items following questions from speaker Victoria Peterson on workforce training funding (Item 4) and General Obligation Bonds Series 2010A and 2010B (Item 6), advancing both without opposition.

agenda_items.title: Community Proclamations and Awards Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell and Council presented proclamations recognizing Disability Awareness Month (highlighting the October 16 Community Day at NCCU), welcoming 2010 Piedmont Laureate Zelda Lockhart who read an original story, International Walk to School Day with Safe Kids Durham County, Prayer and Fast Month, health insurance literacy ahead of an Affordable Care Act seminar, and veterans homelessness awareness. Council also recognized local students and celebrated Durham's second win as one of America's 100 Best Communities for Young People.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Carolina Outreach Rezoning and Subdivision
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council held a public hearing on Carolina Outreach's request to rezone rear gravel parking on its property to accommodate modern parking requirements while subdividing the parcel so lots fronting Bedford Street remain residential on both sides. Representatives of Carolina Outreach and Susan Sewall of the Tuscaloosa-Lakewood Neighborhood Association spoke in support, praising the collaborative 'backyard-to-backyard' buffer solution. Council approved the item unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Annual Evaluation and Assessment Report of the Durham Comprehensive Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Department staff Aaron King presented the Annual Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) tracking Comprehensive Plan implementation and proposed text changes, noting no county ratification was requested this year due to pending legal matters on one county case. No members of the public spoke during the public hearing, and Council approved the item unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Statutory Vested Rights Determination — Bethpage Village and Chin Page Office Park
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Per the City Manager's recommendation, Council opened the statutory vested rights public hearing for Bethpage Village and Chin Page Office Park and voted to continue it to the November 15, 2010 City Council meeting without receiving staff reports or public comment.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Employment and Training 2009-2011 Grant Project Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson spoke on Item 4, thanking the City on behalf of grant recipient Triangle Citizens and urging local government in the future to match 25-30% of federal and state workforce training funds to expand short-term training programs. Council approved the superseding grant project ordinance (Ordinance No. 14044) unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Sale of General Obligation Bonds Series 2010A and 2010B
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson spoke on Item 6, asking whether any unobligated bond funds for streets and sidewalks could be directed toward laying municipal fiber-optic broadband to spur jobs and revenue. Mayor Bell acknowledged the broader need for community broadband while Finance Director David Boyd confirmed all proceeds from the planned bond issuance are already obligated to existing projects and contracts. Council moved, seconded, and closed the vote before adjourning at 8:33 p.m.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Carolina Outreach Zoning Map Change / Parking & Subdivision
votes.notes: All seven seated members recorded present at initial roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved following public hearing with neighborhood association support for the revised parking and Bedford Street residential buffer boundary.

votes.item_title: Item 21: Annual Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) of the Durham Comprehensive Plan
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted Comprehensive Plan EAR and proposed text changes after public hearing with no speakers.

votes.item_title: Item 22: Open and Continue Public Hearing on Statutory Vested Rights (Bethpage Village / Chin Page Office Park) to Nov 15, 2010
votes.discussion_detail: Opened and continued the public hearing to November 15, 2010 per City Manager recommendation.

votes.item_title: Item 4: City of Durham Employment and Training 2009-2011 Grant Project Ordinance (Superseding No. 14044)
votes.discussion_detail: Pulled consent item approved following public remarks by Victoria Peterson advocating future city matching funds for short-term workforce training.

votes.item_title: Item 6: Sale of General Obligation Bonds Series 2010A and 2010B
votes.notes: Motion was moved, seconded, and vote opened and closed without opposition prior to immediate adjournment at 8:33 p.m. (ASR cut off before verbal tally readout).
votes.discussion_detail: Approved after Finance Director David Boyd confirmed all bond proceeds are already obligated to existing projects and contracts.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden (with Mayor Bill Bell excused), the September 23 City Council Work Session opened with a Water Management drought briefing reporting that all North Carolina counties were under drought classification and Durham's combined reservoir capacity stood at 75.3% (Lake Michie 3 feet below full and Little River 8 feet below full). Council reviewed upcoming consent and public hearing items—including the 2010A/B General Obligation Bonds, Parrish Street Common Room lease, Fire Station No. 9 design contract, UDO buffer rules, and street paving updates on Revere Road—and approved the Manager's priority items and the regular meeting agenda by unopposed voice votes. The session closed with an in-depth discussion of neighborhood revitalization strategy comparing Northeast Central Durham and Southcentral Durham models against past struggles in Rolling Hills, followed by Walltown Community Association comments supporting continued housing renovation funding.

agenda_items.title: Water Supply Drought Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management staff Don Greeley and Vicki Westbrook reported that every North Carolina county was in drought status, with Lake Michie 3 feet below full, Little River Reservoir 8 feet below full, combined reservoir capacity at 75.3%, and 30-day average demand at 31 MGD. Staff noted a draft regional water supply plan was under review and addressed Council questions on public communication and customer water bill inquiries.

agenda_items.title: Consent, Departmental, and Public Hearing Agenda Review & Street Paving Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent and public hearing items, including the 2010/2010B GO Bonds, 112 West Parrish Street lease, Fire Station No. 9 architects contract, Planning interlocal renewal (questioning at-large appointment wording when applicant categories are unfilled), Central Carolina Holding solid waste amendment, and upcoming zoning/plan amendments (Durham Place, Calvin Street, Carolina Outreach, Comprehensive Plan EAR, and Bethpage Village). Staff also provided an update on UDO steering committee buffer recommendations and Engineering reported on severe pavement deterioration on Revere Road and NCDOT punch-list work.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted by unopposed voice vote to set the regular meeting agenda with Consent Items 1 through 4 and 6 through 14, General Business Agenda Item 5 (privilege license issuance), and General Business Agenda Public Hearings Items 15 through 22.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Revitalization Strategy (Rolling Hills) & Walltown Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff outlined three options for allocating housing funds—including a hybrid approach combining ongoing housing production with Rolling Hills infrastructure and tax-credit readiness—and reviewed why previous Rolling Hills efforts fell short compared to HOPE VI/Golden Belt in Northeast Central Durham and organic market gains in Southcentral Durham. Council members emphasized a 'both-and' strategy and requested research on Charlotte's housing trust fund model. A Walltown Community Association representative spoke on behalf of Mrs. Seibel urging continued housing renovation funding and pool investment.

votes.item_title: City Manager's Priority Items (Water Supply Presentation and Citizens Matters Schedule)
votes.notes: Voice vote carried unopposed; Bill Bell had an excused absence.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved adding the Water Supply Update presentation and scheduling Citizens Matters at 2:30 p.m.

votes.item_title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda (Consent 1-4, 6-14; GBA 5; GBA Public Hearings 15-22)
votes.notes: Voice vote carried unopposed; Bill Bell excused.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved moving Item 5 to GBA and setting the remaining consent and public hearing items.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: With Mayor Bill Bell presiding and all seven Council members present, the September 20 Regular City Council Meeting approved a 7-0 consent agenda spanning workforce training contracts (including WIA youth and dislocated worker awards and Builders of Hope green jobs), law enforcement grants, and Contract Amendment 1 with the Triangle Transit Authority (Item 32). Following a 7-0 vote to annex tax-exempt Elementary School E (Item 31), Council held an extensive public hearing on the Greenfire Economic Development Incentive Contract for the 165-room Spark Hotel revitalization of the historic Hill Building in downtown Durham (Item 26). After hearing supportive testimony from downtown business owners alongside public questions on living wages and MWBE subcontracting, and questioning staff on life-safety renovation costs, net new tax revenues, foreclosure transferability, and the 15-year schedule, Council approved the Greenfire incentive unanimously (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Childhood Obesity Prevention Proclamation & Manager's Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council opened with proclamations promoting Parks and Recreation's 'Play More' initiative and childhood obesity prevention. Council then approved the City Manager's priority request (7-0) to reorder the evening's two public hearings so Item 31 (Voluntary Annexation) preceded Item 26 (Greenfire Incentive).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda: Workforce Grants, Public Safety, IT Lease, and Transit Operations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council passed the consent agenda in a single 7-0 vote, approving minutes, board attendance reports, SPARO ordinance amendments, Center for Documentary Studies and Workforce Investment Act contracts ($225,000 youth and $825,000 adult/dislocated worker services), a USCM/Walmart Foundation grant, Builders of Hope green job training, surplus property sale at 14 Melbourne Street, Justice Assistance/Target/HIDTA grants, asset forfeiture funds, E+ Group computer lease, and Contract Amendment 1 with the Triangle Transit Authority for Durham transit operations.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Voluntary Annexation Petitions (Elementary School E)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson presented the voluntary annexation petition received by January 1, 2010 for Elementary School E, noting the parcel is tax-exempt property. No public speakers came forward during the hearing, and Council approved the annexation unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Greenfire Economic Development Incentive Contract (Hill Building / Spark Hotel)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD Director Kevin Dick and Finance Director David Boyd presented the proposed 15-year economic development incentive for Greenfire's revitalization of the vacant downtown Hill Building into a 165-room Spark Hotel (requiring construction start by July 31, 2011 and completion by July 31, 2013). Public speakers praised the project's boost to downtown restaurants and convention viability while pressing for living-wage jobs and local MWBE subcontracting. Council members examined feasibility, net new tax generation, printout year spans (FY2031 vs FY2033), and transferability rules upon foreclosure before approving the contract 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Remarks on Transit Governance & Excused Absence Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the formal agenda, a speaker (Carol Allen) voiced disappointment that the Triangle Transit Authority contract (Item 32) passed on consent without a public hearing and criticized eliminating the transit board of trustees' oversight. Council then unanimously approved (7-0) an excused absence request for the September 23 Thursday work session before adjourning at 9:01 p.m.

votes.discussion_detail: Reversed the order of the evening's two public hearings so Voluntary Annexation (Item 31) was heard before Greenfire (Item 26).

votes.discussion_detail: Approved voluntary annexation of tax-exempt Elementary School E after public hearing with no speakers.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved 15-year incentive contract with Greenfire for the 165-room downtown hotel following public hearing and Council scrutiny of tax cash flows, livable wages, and foreclosure transferability.

votes.discussion_detail: Granted excused absence for the upcoming Thursday work session.

Council also appointed voting delegates for the North Carolina League of Municipalities and National League of Cities annual meetings, reviewed the Culture of Service and 2010 Street Bond communications, and heard sobering FY2010 Q4 financial and Durham County tax settlement reports highlighting flat tax base growth despite a 98.76% property tax collection rate. The Durham County Tax Administrator reported a strong 98.76% collection rate on the 2009 city levy ($120M of $122M) and 91.93% on motor vehicles, but warned of zero tax base growth—including $40-50M in motor vehicle value declines and a $160M utility drop—urging caution for the upcoming budget season.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Following an executive session evaluating the City Manager, Mayor Bill Bell called the September 7 Regular City Council Meeting to order at 7:05 p.m. with all seven Council members present. Council referred four Durham Place and Calvin Street planning items (Items 25-28) back to administration for advertising clarification (7-0) and adopted the bulk of the consent agenda (7-0), including DPAC, street resurfacing, paratransit, and public safety grants. Following a contested public hearing on petition paving for Leonard Drive and Turner Street (Item 24)—where one resident raised concerns over undeveloped lots and senior costs while other residents urged paving to eliminate red clay dust after sewer blasting—Council members clarified that the 9% assessment interest rate would be set after construction and voted 7-0 to order the improvements. Council also approved three pulled ARRA/fiber consent items (Items 16, 18, and 22) unanimously (7-0) after addressing Victoria Peterson's questions on local jobs and residency.

agenda_items.title: Recovery, Sickle Cell Disease, and Life Insurance Awareness Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council presented three proclamations recognizing Alcohol and Drug Addiction Recovery Month (with Partnership for a Healthy Durham), Sickle Cell Disease awareness (with the National Organization of Top Ladies of Distinction), and Life Insurance Awareness Month.

agenda_items.title: Referral of Durham Place & Calvin Street Cases and Street Bond Update Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved (7-0) the City Manager's request to refer Items 25-28 (Durham Place and Calvin Street plan amendments and zoning map changes) back to administration to clarify an advertising issue. The Manager also announced that upcoming Thursday work sessions would feature regular updates on city and state street resurfacing and the November 2 street paving bond referendum communications plan.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda: Boards, DPAC Amendment, CIP, Grants, and Street Resurfacing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Excluding pulled Items 16, 18, and 22, Council passed the consent agenda 7-0, approving board appointments, the Fifth Amendment to the DPAC operating agreement, Camden Avenue radio building CIP funding, City Hall annex patio roof contract, Capitol Broadcasting and Carolina Panthers grants, Northern Durham Parkway state road resolution, Contract ST-234 street resurfacing amendment, Lincoln Community Health Center paratransit lease, transit trip planner, and Hillandale utility easement condemnation.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Petition Paving Improvements on Leonard Drive and Turner Street
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater staff presented a valid petition to pave Leonard Drive and Turner Street together. Speaker Elizabeth Dana expressed opposition citing undeveloped property, notification timing, and senior affordability, while residents Ron Meadows and Miguel (1450 Turner Road) testified that heavy red clay dust since prior sewer dynamiting harms elderly and ill neighbors and urged paving both roads. Council members questioned the 30-day notice and 9% assessment interest rate, confirmed the final rate is set post-construction, and approved the improvements 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items: ARRA JAG District Attorney Grant, NCCU Fiber Conduit, and ARRA Passenger Information System
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen Victoria Peterson questioned whether the assistant district attorney funded under Item 16 lives in Durham, which contractor performed the NCCU fiber conduit installation under Item 18, and how many local jobs Durham-based Digital Recorders Inc. (DRI Inc.) would create under the Item 22 ARRA transit passenger information system project. Staff clarified the ADA position has existed for three years and committed to sharing vendor contact information; Council passed each item 7-0. Mayor Bell closed by affirming that violent crimes raised by Ms. Peterson are a top priority for Police and the City Manager.

votes.item_title: City Manager's Priority Items (Refer Items 25-28 Durham Place and Calvin Street Back to Administration)
votes.discussion_detail: Referred Items 25, 26, 27, and 28 back to administration to resolve a public advertising issue.

votes.item_title: Item 24: Resolutions Ordering Petition Paving Improvements on Leonard Drive and Turner Street
votes.discussion_detail: Ordered paving improvements following public hearing and confirmation that assessment interest rates are finalized post-construction.

votes.item_title: Item 16: ARRA FY2009 Stimulus JAG Contract Amendment No. 1 (District Attorney 14th Prosecutorial District / AOC)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved two-month supplemental stimulus funding for an existing assistant district attorney position.

votes.item_title: Item 18: License Agreement with NCCU for Fiber Optic Conduit Installation in Public Right-of-Way
votes.discussion_detail: Approved right-of-way fiber optic conduit license agreement for North Carolina Central University.

votes.item_title: Item 22: ARRA Passenger Information System Project (Digital Recorders Inc.)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved ARRA transit passenger information project with Durham-based Digital Recorders Inc.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden with all seven Council members present, the August 19 City Council Work Session referred the SPARO ordinance amendment (Item 10) back to administration, moved up recognition of a Capitol Broadcasting Company donation (Item 14), and continued a personnel closed session. Council devoted substantial scrutiny to Item 11, the Fifth Amendment to the Durham Performing Arts Center (DPAC) operating agreement, examining the $2 ticket facility fee split, operator repair caps, HVAC completion and construction closeout status, and whether blanket advance language on future local or state ticket/sales taxes should be narrowed. Council also discussed ways to support Durham Public Schools student achievement, set the upcoming regular meeting agenda (7-0), heard citizen complaints from Creekside Townhomes residents regarding nighttime industrial warehouse noise near T.W. Alexander Drive, and adjourned to closed session.

agenda_items.title: Manager's Priority Items & Personnel Closed Session Continuation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved (7-0) the City Manager's priority items referring Item 10 (Streets, Parks and Recreation Open Space ordinance amendment) back to administration and advancing Item 14 (Capitol Broadcasting Company donation) because a CBC representative was present. Council also voted 7-0 to continue its closed session on personnel matters.

agenda_items.title: Departmental Agenda Review & Setting the Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed board appointments (Items 1-9), public safety and infrastructure items (Items 12-23, including Camden Avenue radio building, Carolina Panthers grant, Northern Durham Parkway, NCCU fiber, ST-234 resurfacing, and Hillandale easement condemnation), and public hearing items (Items 24-28). Council then voted 7-0 to set the regular meeting agenda with Consent Items 1-9 and 11-23 and GBA Public Hearings Items 24-28.

agenda_items.title: Fifth Amendment to the Durham Performing Arts Center (DPAC) Operating Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed the Fifth Amendment to the DPAC operating agreement with Nederlander, clarifying that $1 of the $2 per-ticket facility fee goes to the operator and $1 to a city capital reserve fund, and confirming HVAC repairs were operating smoothly while final construction closeout wrapped up. A Council member expressed concern that provisions addressing taxes assessed by 'any local government' on tickets granted overly broad advance authority without fiscal projections if county or transit sales taxes were enacted. Members also discussed DPAC show profitability, riding the Bull City Connector, and partnering with Superintendent Dr. Becoats on DPS academic mentoring.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Matters: Homeless Reentry Program & T.W. Alexander Drive Industrial Noise
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speaker Mr. Garrett presented his work assisting formerly homeless men, and Council directed City Manager Tom Bonfield to follow up on potential city support. Creekside Townhomes resident Lila Stockton (1725 T.W. Alexander Drive) and a Skybrook neighbor then complained of loud nighttime metallic/warehouse noise from an adjacent light-industry-zoned building, requesting better decibel noise-ordinance enforcement or rezoning; Planning and staff reviewed transitional zoning history and committed to follow-up inspection and enforcement, before Council voted 7-0 to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: City Manager's Priority Items (Refer Item 10 Back to Administration; Advance Item 14)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved referring Item 10 back to staff and moving Item 14 earlier on the work session agenda.

votes.item_title: Continue Closed Session for Personnel Matters
votes.discussion_detail: Continued personnel closed session without a time certain.

votes.item_title: Setting the Regular Council Meeting Agenda (Consent Items 1-9, 11-23; GBA Public Hearings 24-28)
votes.discussion_detail: Set the regular Council meeting agenda excluding Item 10.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: Approved adjourning to closed session following Citizens Matters.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven Council members present, the August 16 Regular City Council Meeting honored Special Olympics USA National Games gold-medal powerlifter Charles Quick and marked the 100th episode of 'City Hall This Week,' alongside Council reflections comparing Durham Public Schools test performance and poverty indicators with Wake County. Council unanimously approved (7-0) the Manager's priority adjustments and Consent Agenda Items 1-12, and received the Police Department's 2010 Second Quarter Summary Crime Report noting a 4% rise in violent crime, a 7% rise in property crime, a 6-minute-6-second average Priority 1 response time, and 25 new rookie officers entering BLET. In public hearings, Council voted 7-0 to refer Thompson Road sewer improvements back to staff while ordering East Geer Street sewer and Harwick Drive sidewalk petition improvements (Item 14), and voted 7-0 to adopt UDO Text Amendment TC1000001 updating bicycle parking and alternative pedestrian plan standards (Item 15).

agenda_items.title: Charles Quick Special Olympics Proclamation, DPS Reflections, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented a proclamation honoring Durham powerlifter Charles Quick for winning gold at the Special Olympics USA National Games with a 270.1-pound deadlift. Council approved (7-0) the Manager's priority items correcting Item 13's title to the Second Quarter Crime Report and referring the Thompson Road motion in Item 14 back to staff, and members later discussed news coverage comparing Durham and Wake County school proficiency and free-and-reduced-lunch rates.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda: ARRA Paving, Nonpoint Source Grant, IT Storage, and NCDOT Agreements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved Consent Items 1 through 12 in a single 7-0 vote, including ARRA 2009 Contract ST-247 for 2010 street improvements, a Section 319 nonpoint source control grant, an EMC unified storage lease, municipal software licensing, and NCDOT municipal and utility agreements.

agenda_items.title: 2010 Second Quarter Summary Crime Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Department leadership presented Q2 2010 performance metrics: violent crime rose 4% in the first six months (18 homicides vs. 16 the prior year, with 9 arrests and 1 suspect death clearance; 354 incidents and 438 victims) and property crime increased 7% (driven by metal and appliance thefts). Priority 1 response times beat targets at 6 minutes, 6 seconds (53% under 5 minutes), sworn staffing stood at 96% with 25 new Durham officers starting BLET, and the department highlighted automated vehicle locators, the third-year Bullseye report, 1,300+ donated school book bags, and 140+ youth in the Police Athletic League.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Petition Improvements on Thompson Road, East Geer Street, and Harwick Drive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater staff recommended declaring the Thompson Road sewer petition null and void and referring it back to staff while moving forward with East Geer Street sewer service and Harwick Drive sidewalk improvements. With no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and approved the recommended actions 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC1000001 (Bicycle Parking & Alternative Pedestrian Plans)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Department staff Steve Medlin presented UDO Text Amendment TC1000001 implementing recommendations from the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission (BPAC), noting prior 12-0 Planning Commission and 5-0 County Commissioner approvals. BPAC Development Review Subcommittee Chair Dan Clever spoke in favor, and Council adopted the text amendment unanimously (7-0) before adjourning at 7:58 p.m.

votes.item_title: City Manager's Priority Items (Item 13 Title Correction; Refer First Motion of Item 14 Back to Administration)
votes.discussion_detail: Corrected Item 13 from First Quarter to Second Quarter Crime Report and referred the Thompson Road portion of Item 14 back to staff.

votes.item_title: Item 14: Resolutions Ordering East Geer Street Sewer and Harwick Drive Sidewalk Improvements (Thompson Road Referred Back)
votes.discussion_detail: Ordered East Geer sewer and Harwick Drive sidewalk improvements and referred Thompson Road sewer petition back to staff as null and void.

votes.item_title: Item 15: UDO Text Amendment TC1000001 (Bicycle Parking Requirements and Alternative Pedestrian Plans)
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted BPAC-recommended UDO amendments for bicycle parking and alternative pedestrian plans.

meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden with five Council members present at the dais (Farad Ali excused; Mayor Bill Bell noted as in his office), the August 5 City Council Work Session excused Farad Ali's absence (5-0) and acted immediately under suspended rules on three items: rescinding a board appointment and re-advertising for a landlord seat for 15 days (5-0), approving Convention Center Phase 2 CM-at-Risk Amendment No. 2J with Skanska USA Building (5-0), and receiving the Environmental Affairs Board's Falls Lake Nutrient Strategy recommendations for transmittal to the state Division of Water Quality (5-0). Council also pulled Duke University's fiber-optic license agreement (Item 5) pending confirmation that resident Victoria Peterson's inquiries were answered, reviewed billboard maintenance enforcement under state and UDO 50% replacement thresholds, and pressed housing staff on vacant boarded houses, Rolling Hills CDBG/HOME tradeoffs, and the 100 worst commercial buildings before setting the regular meeting agenda (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence for Farad Ali, Manager's Priority Items, and Clerk's Board Rescission
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 5-0 to grant Council Member Farad Ali an excused absence and approved the City Manager's priority items (5-0). Under suspended rules (5-0), Council also approved the City Clerk's request (5-0) to rescind Mr. Case's appointment and re-advertise for 15 days to fill a landlord seat, and voted (5-0) to add Environmental Affairs Board Falls Lake comments to the end of the agenda.

agenda_items.title: Billboard Ordinance Deferral and Maintenance Enforcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff reported that the county's billboard consideration was deferred for up to two cycles and noted the city carries no enforcement duty for county areas. Within the city, staff explained that UDO technical changes were underway to align the city's older 25% destruction threshold with state law's 50% threshold while actively inspecting deteriorated billboards for notices of violation or removal.

agenda_items.title: Convention Center Phase 2 Skanska Amendment & Duke Fiber Optic License Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council suspended the rules (5-0) and approved Amendment No. 2J to the Skanska USA Building CM-at-Risk contract for Convention Center Phase 2 (5-0). On Item 5 (Duke University fiber-optic cable license agreement), Council declined to suspend the rules and pulled the item to confirm whether resident Victoria Peterson had received and responded to staff answers regarding her questions.

agenda_items.title: Vacant Housing, Rolling Hills Financing, and Commercial Code Enforcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Housing staff discussed developing a phased short- and long-term strategy for over 700 vacant houses, Rolling Hills tax-credit and CDBG/HOME reallocation impacts, and annual repair capacity (~30 city-funded repairs/year). Council Member Clement urged frank reporting on boarded-up neighborhood homes, members pressed for category-by-category budget allocations ahead of the November first work session, and staff committed to re-sending the list of the 100 worst commercial buildings.

agenda_items.title: Falls Lake Nutrient Strategy Recommendations & Setting the Regular Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After discussing potential city cost exposure if the state Division of Water Quality (DWQ) lacks funding for Use Attainability Analyses, Council voted 5-0 to receive and accept the Environmental Affairs Board's Falls Lake Nutrient Strategy report for transmittal to DWQ. Council then set the regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1, 3, 4, and 6-11; GBA Item 13; GBA Public Hearings 14-15) by a 5-0 voice vote; a closing motion to enter closed session was made without a second recorded in the digest.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven Council members present, the August 2 Regular City Council Meeting opened with a National Night Out proclamation ('Safety in Numbers' across 94 Durham neighborhoods) and a tribute by Council Member Howard Clement III recognizing Coach Willie Bradshaw's induction into the National Federation of State High School Associations Hall of Fame. Council approved (7-0) referring back a cultural arts contract (Item 17) and a 1106 Hillandale Road utility easement condemnation (Item 32), added an NCDOT downtown street resurfacing update, approved the Clerk's Durham Housing Authority ballot item (7-0), and passed the consent agenda unanimously (7-0). Following an extensive late-night debate over a proposed billboard/sign ordinance text amendment—examining legal precedent upheld by the U.S. Supreme Court, existing sign-maintenance rules, staffing costs, and whether Council could force removal of an offensive billboard—Council unanimously defeated the proposed billboard ordinance change by a 0-7 vote (Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Farad Ali all voting Nay) before adjourning at 11:13 p.m.

agenda_items.title: National Night Out Proclamation & Recognition of Coach Willie Bradshaw
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell presented the National Night Out proclamation to Project Safe Neighborhoods Coordinator Jennifer Snyder, noting 94 registered Durham neighborhoods under the 'Safety in Numbers' gun-crime prevention campaign and a kickoff rally at the Holton Career and Resource Center. Later, Council Member Howard Clement III led applause recognizing Coach Willie Bradshaw's induction into the National Federation of State High School Associations Hall of Fame.

agenda_items.title: Manager's and Clerk's Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to refer Item 17 (FY11 cultural arts contract) and Item 32 (1106 Hillandale Road easement condemnation, under active negotiation) back to administration and added an NCDOT resurfacing presentation by Wally Bowen. Council also approved 7-0 the City Clerk's priority ballot item for a Durham Housing Authority Board of Commissioners appointment.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda: Boards, Audits, Grants, DPAC Naming Rights, and Infrastructure
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council passed the consent agenda unanimously (7-0), approving minutes, advisory board appointments, May and June 2010 bid reports, Personnel Action Form and non-city agency audits, CIP amendments, Employment & Training and HUD grants, domestic violence court contracts, DPAC minor naming rights (F.M. Kirby Foundation), backyard hen permits report, Planning work program, SharePoint 2010 web upgrade, and sanitary sewer monitoring improvements.

agenda_items.title: Proposed Billboard / Sign Ordinance Text Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In an extended late-night discussion continuing past 11 p.m., Council questioned Planning staff and the City Attorney on Durham's existing non-conforming billboard ordinance—which had survived seven years of litigation to the U.S. Supreme Court—and Section 11.2.5 maintenance standards. Staff confirmed the existing 20-year-old ordinance works well and causes no harm to the city if left unchanged, while Council Member Clement questioned whether anything could be done about a controversial privately owned billboard at the north end of a bridge, which the Mayor and City Attorney confirmed could not be forced down. A motion to adopt the proposed ordinance change (moved with intent to vote no) failed unanimously 0-7.

votes.item_title: City Manager's Priority Items (Refer Items 17 & 32 Back to Administration; Add NCDOT Presentation)
votes.discussion_detail: Referred Item 17 and Item 32 back to administration and added NCDOT resurfacing presentation by Wally Bowen.

votes.item_title: City Clerk's Priority Item (Durham Housing Authority Board of Commissioners Appointment Ballot)
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the Clerk's priority ballot item for a DHA Board of Commissioners appointment on the General Business Agenda.

votes.item_title: Proposed Billboard / Sign Ordinance Text Amendment

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - 2010 Bond Referendum and City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Bill Bell (who stepped away briefly around 01:08:55 for a conference call while Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden presided), the July 22, 2010 Special Meeting and City Council Work Session opened with a required public hearing on the proposed $20 million General Obligation Street Bond order ahead of the November 2 ballot. Staff reported filing the sworn statement of debt showing net city indebtedness at 1.36% of assessed property valuation, while six public speakers addressed the proposal—including Citizens Capital Improvement Panel (CCIP) Vice Chair Jack Steer conveying CCIP's 9-3 endorsement conditioned on establishing a $5 million annual street maintenance fund by FY 2012-13, alongside five speakers opposing a bond tax increase during an economic downturn. After an omitted middle segment in the transcript digest, Council discussed property acquisition timing for a construction contract ahead of the August 2 meeting, received the CPAC Fourth Quarter Report showing 96.9% of capital projects on time and on budget, heard citizen comments on a Hyde Park alley easement and bus driver customer service, and unanimously approved by voice vote two closed sessions, an alternate appointment to the Housing Appeals Board, and the upcoming regular meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on $20 Million General Obligation Street Bond Order and Referendum
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained the final statutory steps to place the proposed $20 million general obligation street bond referendum on the November 2, 2010 ballot, reporting that the bond order introduced July 8 was published July 11 and a sworn statement of debt was filed showing net city indebtedness at 1.36% of assessed property valuation. During the public hearing, CCIP Vice Chair Jack Steer reported a 9-3 committee endorsement contingent on a Council policy establishing a $5 million or greater annual street maintenance fund starting in FY 2012-2013, while speakers Larry Hester, Virginia Williams, E.L. Allison, Don Leppkes, and Anita Keef raised concerns about rushing the referendum onto the ballot and increasing property taxes during high unemployment and economic uncertainty, urging line-item budget funding instead.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Public hearing held; final vote occurred in omitted digest segment

agenda_items.title: Property Acquisition and Construction Contract Notice-to-Proceed
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council questioned General Services staff regarding an unresolved property-owner issue tied to a construction project and emphasized that, barring rare exceptions, the City should not issue construction contracts or notices to proceed without full control of necessary properties. Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden kept the item on the General Business Agenda in hopes the dispute would be resolved before the August 2 Council meeting.

agenda_items.title: Capital Program Advisory Committee (CPAC) Fourth Quarter Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson introduced CPAC Vice Chair Jack Steer to present the fourth-quarter report for the period ending June 30, 2010. Steer highlighted a pool feasibility study ($1 million allocated for design only, with no construction funding in the CIP), praised a roughly 70% management improvement in General Services, and reported that 96.9% of capital projects by dollar value were on time and on budget, with 2% facing potential issues and 2.9% behind schedule or over budget (only two projects in red); staff also noted Walltown Park lighting and gates were handled under a separate parks contract.

agenda_items.title: Motion to Enter Closed Sessions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the conclusion of presentations, Council moved and seconded entering two consecutive closed sessions, beginning with the City Attorney's Office. The motion carried without opposition by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments on Hyde Park Alley Easement and Transit Service
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizens addressed Council regarding the process for purchasing an undeveloped World War I-era alley easement behind Hyde Park properties and transit customer service feedback. A transit rider commended helpful bus drivers while reporting that some drivers pass waiting passengers without stopping when behind schedule.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments (Housing Appeals Board)

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council set the agenda for the upcoming regular meeting comprising Consent Items 1-7, 9-25, 30, and 31, General Business Agenda Item 32, and GBA Public Hearings 33-38. The motion carried by voice vote prior to adjournment at 01:43:11.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - 2010 General Obligation Bond Referendum
meetings.executive_summary: Called into brief special session during Council's July recess with Mayor Bill Bell presiding and Council Member Eugene Brown holding an excused absence, the Durham City Council completed the second of three required steps to place a $20 million General Obligation street resurfacing bond referendum on the November 2010 ballot. meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden with six members present (Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Howard Clement III, and Mike Woodard; Farad Ali excused), the June 10 City Council Work Session reviewed the upcoming regular agenda and concluded Council's FY 2010-2011 budget balancing deliberations. Council unanimously (6-0) accepted the City Manager's priority items, suspended the rules to adopt an amended resolution supporting the North Carolina Mobility Fund (Item 42) incorporating Powell Bill and interstate maintenance language for the Raleigh conference committee, and suspended the rules to approve priority consent items (Items 15/24) without opposition. Staff also reviewed commercial/neighborhood revitalization target areas (comparing Little Five Points, East Main Street, Angier/Driver, and Fayetteville Street) and walked through the final budget balancing spreadsheet, clarifying ~$206,696 in general-fund special needs housing alongside $113,000 in FY10 carryover, ~$460,000-$485,000 including code enforcement/demolition, and $800,000 in Continuum of Care funds in response to 'Penny for Housing' advocacy, as well as reducing the General Fund transfer to the Parrish Street reserve given its ~$800,000 fund balance.

agenda_items.title: City Manager's Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager presented priority items including suspending rules to vote immediately on Item 15 (HR 4812 Local Jobs for America Act) and Item 24, referring Item 30 (city code revisions on extension agreements) back to the administration, scheduling Item 35 (DPAC Oversight Committee annual report), and adding supplemental Items 39 (Downtown Durham Inc. board reappointments), 40 (TTA/DATA transit contract), 41 (Human Relations Commission), and 42 (NC Mobility Fund support). Council approved the priority items by a 6-0 voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Support for North Carolina Mobility Fund Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Due to the upcoming legislative conference committee meeting in Raleigh, Council voted 6-0 to suspend the rules and take immediate action on Item 42. Members amended the resolution to include a Transportation Advisory Committee clause stating it is essential for the Mobility Fund to provide additional funding to Powell Bill and interstate maintenance programs, and adopted the amended resolution 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent and General Business Agenda Review & Rule-Suspension Action
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cole-McFadden read through the agenda, including Workforce Development Board appointments, water chemical contracts, FY10/FY11 budget ordinances (Items 9-10), Chamber of Commerce and Downtown Durham contracts, T-Mobile antenna license, Civic Center amendment, police sidewalk bicycle exemption, Casner sewer easement (Item 27), Duke University fiber-optic license (Item 28, pulled for Victoria Peterson), tank maintenance (Item 34), DPAC report (Item 35), and Planning items (37-38). Council suspended the rules and approved the time-sensitive priority consent items without opposition.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood / Corridor Infrastructure Target Area Selection
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed five candidate areas (including Little Five Points, East Main Street, Angier/Driver, and Fayetteville Street) to determine where public infrastructure investment would address the greatest need and yield the strongest return. Staff explained that East Main Street was ruled out due to recent roadwork while focusing on areas in worst physical condition.

agenda_items.title: FY 2010-2011 Budget Balancing, 'Penny for Housing,' and Parrish Street Reserve
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed how to respond to 'Penny for Housing' advocacy (including an INC resolution) for permanent supportive housing, with staff detailing $206,696 in General Fund special needs housing, $113,000 in FY10 carryover, roughly $460,000-$485,000 total when counting code enforcement and demolition, and $800,000 in Continuum of Care funding ahead of a Monday joint city-county meeting on 10-Year Plan governance. Members then reviewed the preliminary budget balancing spreadsheet, including reducing the General Fund transfer to the Parrish Street reserve (noting an ~$800,000 fund balance and ~$165,000 budgeted expenditure) and next year's public arts allocation before adjourning around 11:00 p.m.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Draft Strategic Plan
meetings.executive_summary: Called to order by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden while Mayor Bill Bell was en route, the June 10 Special City Council Meeting reviewed the City's draft Strategic Plan and mapped out the statutory schedule for a proposed November 2010 General Obligation street bond referendum. Budget and Management Services staff Jay Reinstein and Bertha Johnson outlined nine months of internal team and stakeholder work, presenting a proposed mission statement and a streamlined structure reducing eight original goals to five—including Safe and Secure Community, Thriving Livable Neighborhoods, and Well-Managed City—paired with internal intermediate metrics and Council-facing outcome measures. In the second half of the meeting, staff detailed the mandatory Local Government Commission (LGC) and public-notice timeline requiring three resolutions on June 21, a brief special meeting during Council's July vacation week (July 8-14) to introduce the bond order, and a July 22 public hearing and adoption ahead of the July 23 Board of Elections deadline. Council debated sizing the street bond at $15 million versus $20 million, directed staff to prepare the three LGC resolutions for June 21, and unanimously voted by voice vote to excuse Council Member Eugene Brown from the July special meeting before adjourning to the work session.

agenda_items.title: Draft City of Durham Strategic Plan Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Tom Bonfield, Jay Reinstein, and Budget Director Bertha Johnson presented the draft Strategic Plan developed over nine months by internal teams (Direction Setting Team and 10-director Plan Development Team) using citizen/employee surveys and February budget retreat feedback. Staff proposed a new mission statement ('to provide quality services to make Durham a great place to live, work, and play'), consolidated eight original goals into five, and outlined outcome measures (such as crime clearance, neighborhood health index, bond rating, and tax burden) linked to internal departmental metrics.

agenda_items.title: 2010 General Obligation Street Bond Referendum Timeline and Sizing ($15M vs. $20M)

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Proposed Fiscal Year 2010-2011 Budget
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden on Day 3 of FY 2010-2011 budget deliberations, the May 27 Special City Council Meeting reviewed the Durham Performing Arts Center (DPAC) Enterprise Fund, the Non-City Agency (NCA) grant program, and flagged budget balancing items without taking formal votes. Senior Assistant to the City Manager Reginald Johnson and naming-rights consultant Hill Carrow detailed DPAC revenues, naming-rights prospects ($1.4 million projected by FY15), and the $1,000-per-seat naming campaign (with Council Member Howard Clement III pledging two seats), while Budget Director Bertha Johnson and Melinda Squires-Nelson reviewed the NCA transition policy reducing FY11 funding to $178,423 ($297,000 below FY10) as multi-year capacity-building grantees like the Durham Symphony reached zero. In closing budget-balancing discussions covering an estimated $400,000-$425,000 delta (0.1 to 0.25 cents on the tax rate), members debated adding $17,000 for Crest Street youth programming, funding Warrant Control (with Clement pressing why the Clerk of Court was not funding statutory warrant duties), and preserving roughly $138,000 for the Domestic Violence Court judge and legal assistant—where one member questioned city funding of a state judge while Clement called it vital to public safety and another urged caution against tax increases given county tax pressures.

agenda_items.title: Durham Performing Arts Center (DPAC) Enterprise Fund Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reginald Johnson and budget analyst J.J. Scott presented the DPAC Enterprise Fund for the first time as a full budget briefing, explaining naming-rights commissions paid to Front Row Sports / Hill Carrow and revenue projections reaching $1.4 million by FY15. agenda_items.title: Non-City Agency (NCA) Grant Program Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson and NCA Coordinator Melinda Squires-Nelson reviewed the 2008-09 policy replacing perpetual grants with two-year transitional grants and three-year diminishing capacity-building grants (100%, 66%, and 33%, capped at $25,000). They reported FY11 proposed NCA funding of $178,423—down $297,000 from FY10—and noted that long-time grantees like the Durham Symphony were now reaching zero funding under the phase-out schedule.

agenda_items.title: Budget Balancing Delta and Flagged Items (Crest Street, Warrant Control, Domestic Violence Court)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed an estimated $400,000-$425,000 budget delta (0.1 to 0.25 cents on the property tax rate) and flagged items ahead of the June 10 wrap-up session: $17,000 for the Crest Street youth program; Warrant Control funding, which Council Member Clement endorsed as crucial to public safety while questioning why the Clerk of Court was not paying statutory costs; and ~$138,000 for the Domestic Violence Court judge and legal assistant, where one member doubted cities should fund a judge while Clement emphasized its importance and another member cited reluctance toward additional tax or fee increases alongside expected county tax hikes. Members also confirmed a street paving bond referendum would not impact the FY11 operating budget and requested resolutions honoring local soccer standouts Molly Patman and Jordan High's Gatorade Player of the Year before adjourning.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Proposed Fiscal Year 2010-2011 Budget
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Bill Bell on Day 2 of the FY 2010-2011 budget work sessions, the May 26 Special City Council Meeting reviewed emergency services, operational departments, and community-building budgets without taking formal votes. In the Police Department briefing, officials highlighted a 7.8% budget increase alongside a reduction of three civilian positions, a new Firearms Analyst position in forensics (11 months grant-funded and one month city-funded) to accelerate in-house shell-casing analysis, asset forfeiture priorities, and facility planning for a future police headquarters. Council and City Manager Tom Bonfield extensively debated Warrant Control—clarifying it had been stimulus-funded rather than part of the City budget and should be a state responsibility pending talks with judicial and county officials—and later heard Human Relations staff warn that omitting $84,476 for a Domestic Violence District Court judge and $49,634 for a victim-witness legal assistant would create dangerous case backlogs, prompting two Council members to urge preserving the ~$134,000 allocation. At the close of the 7.5-hour session, Bonfield recapped flagged items for follow-up—including Warrant Control, Domestic Violence Court, General Services/City Attorney legal coordination, cemetery maintenance, deferred maintenance, Crest Street, Neighborhood College ($2,000-$2,500), and a $40,000 matching city share for a Gang Coordinator—ahead of a June 10 budget-balancing session.

agenda_items.title: Police Department Budget, Firearms Forensics Analyst, and Facility Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Department leadership presented a 7.8% overall budget increase while cutting three civilian FTEs, prioritizing a new Firearms Analyst FTE in the forensics unit (11 months grant-funded, one month city-funded) requested by the Crime Cabinet and Gang Oversight Committee to analyze bullet casings locally within months despite a three-year certification track. Staff also discussed federal asset forfeiture needs lists, CIP funding for future police headquarters planning, and an annual citizen perception-of-safety survey.

agenda_items.title: Warrant Control Funding and County/State Coordination
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Addressing questions from Council Member Howard Clement III, City Manager Tom Bonfield clarified that Warrant Control had never been funded in the City's budget—having relied on federal stimulus dollars—and argued it should be state-funded while noting ongoing Friday discussions with Elaine Bushfan, Tracy Cline, Archie Smith, the Sheriff's Office, and Durham County. Chief Jose Lopez detailed magistrate warrant intake, Sheriff's Office warrant service coordination, and beat-officer warrant enforcement.

agenda_items.title: Domestic Violence District Court Funding Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reviewing the Human Relations Department budget, staff reported that salaries for the Domestic Violence District Court judge ($84,476) and victim-witness legal assistant ($49,634) were omitted from the proposed FY 2011 appropriation, warning of severe backlogs and heightened danger to victims. Two Council members strongly advocated restoring the ~$134,000 allocation in the $300 million city budget to protect women and children victims even while pressing state legislators to assume responsibility.

agenda_items.title: Day 2 Flagged Items Recap: Neighborhood College, Gang Coordinator, and June 10 Wrap-Up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Bonfield recapped Day 2 flagged items—Warrant Control, General Services/City Attorney coordination, cemetery maintenance, deferred maintenance, Crest Street, and Domestic Violence Court—and Council debated funding a spring session of Neighborhood College ($2,000-$2,500 from Council contingency or joint City-County talks) and a $40,000 City share (potentially from health insurance savings) matched by $40,000 from the County for a Gang Coordinator. Due to Friday quorum absences, Council planned a final budget-balancing session around June 10 alongside the strategic planning session.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Proposed Fiscal Year 2010-2011 Budget
meetings.executive_summary: Opened by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden for Day 1 of Council's FY 2010-2011 budget review, the May 25 Special City Council Meeting examined citywide revenue projections, transit funding, and Transportation Department programs without taking formal votes. Budget Director Bertha Johnson and City Manager Tom Bonfield reported that declining development fees, a two-thirds state cut to beer and wine tax distributions, sluggish sales tax, and a 75% ($1.6 million) drop in investment income had increased the General Fund's reliance on property taxes to 62% (up from 58%) within a $206 million General Fund budget reduced by $10 million over two years, requiring a proposed property tax increase adding $7.3 million. In afternoon transportation presentations, staff explained a proposed 0.7-cent tax increase (bringing transit's total General Fund support to 3.26 cents) to replace expiring two-year federal stimulus funds, cover livable wage adjustments under new TTA-negotiated paratransit and fixed-route management contracts, and launch the Duke-partnered Bull City Connector linking Duke South, Main Street, Durham Station, and Golden Belt every 15 minutes. Staff also outlined regional half-cent sales tax transit planning for as early as Fall 2011, reinstatement of $130,000 for street lighting, and challenges regulating shuttle operators competing with licensed taxicabs.

agenda_items.title: FY 2010-2011 Revenue Overview and Property Tax Dependence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson presented the revenue picture for the $206 million General Fund (down $10 million over two years), noting sharp drops in development revenues, a two-thirds General Assembly cut in beer and wine tax sharing, flat sales taxes below pre-recession peaks, and a $1.6 million (75%) decline in investment income due to near-zero federal funds rates and prior-year overestimates. With property taxes now accounting for 62% of General Fund revenue (including a $7.3 million increase from growth and the proposed tax rate hike), Council Member Diane Catotti asked staff to clarify transfer offsets on budget comparison slides.

agenda_items.title: Transit Budget, Livable Wage Contracts, Bull City Connector, and Regional Sales Tax Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation staff detailed a 0.7-cent tax rate increase (for 3.26 cents total General Fund support) to offset the expiration of one-time federal stimulus funds and incorporate livable wage increases into new Triangle Transit-negotiated management contracts for fixed-route and paratransit services. Staff highlighted the proposed Bull City Connector route running every 15 minutes Monday-Friday from Duke South through downtown to Golden Belt with Duke financial support, ongoing regional transit planning with Wake and Durham counties for a potential Fall 2011 half-cent sales tax referendum, and annexation paratransit cost modeling.

agenda_items.title: Transportation Department: Street Lighting, Parking, MPO Planning, and Shuttle Regulation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed department-wide operations, including $130,000 reinstated in the proposed budget for the Street Lighting program (following ~400 lights installed from prior carryover), parking citation collections, $865,000 in NCDOT traffic maintenance reimbursements, MPO 2040 Long Range Transportation Plan and NC 54 corridor study work, and ongoing taxicab subcommittee concerns over shuttle vehicles operating like unregulated taxis despite limited enforcement staffing. Council concluded Day 1 shortly after 4:00 p.m.
