meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 17, 2010 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with six members present and Council Member Howard Clement III absent, the Council presented proclamations for National Public Works Week (May 16–22, 2010), North Carolina School of Science and Mathematics students' Guinness World Record 320,000-pound food drive, and a resolution memorializing former Mayor Charles Buchanan Markham. After a gap in the transcript digest, Council held public hearings and approved 6-0 the Major Special Use Permit (M100001 / D0900196) and companion 1.89-mile Major Site Plan (D0900196) for American Tobacco Trail Phase E, including Major Thoroughfare Corridor buffer reductions to improve vegetative opacity and safe pedestrian and bicycle traffic. Following public comment, Council also approved 6-0 an ordinance revising stormwater rates upward by 9.3% effective July 1, 2010 to fund 4.5 FTEs for regulatory compliance and illegal-discharge enforcement, deferred Item 30 to the June 7 meeting, and passed pulled Consent Items 5 (petitioned improvements) and 21 (parking fee changes) by 6-0 votes.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Silent Meditation, Pledge, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m., noted the absence of Council Member Howard Clement III, and asked Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden to lead the Pledge of Allegiance. The City Clerk called the roll with six members present: Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, Farad Ali, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Mike Woodard.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: National Public Works Week (May 16–22, 2010)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell proclaimed May 16–22, 2010 as National Public Works Week in Durham and presented the proclamation to the Public Works Director. Staff thanked street, inspection, survey, sidewalk, resurfacing, pothole, and watershed personnel and screened a short engineering video focused on bridges.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of NCSSM Students for World-Record Food Drive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council recognized students from the North Carolina School of Science and Mathematics, alongside Dr. Julian Barber and former teacher Dr. Doyle, for collecting nearly 320,000 pounds of food on March 20, 2010 to break the Guinness World Record for the largest 24-hour food drive benefiting the Food Bank of Central and Eastern North Carolina.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Memorializing Former Mayor Charles Buchanan Markham
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented a memorial resolution honoring former Durham Mayor Charles Buchanan Markham (1981–1985) to his nephew Bruce Buschoo, recounting Mayor Markham's journalism, legal, EEOC, HUD, NCCU Law, and civic career as well as his family's long history of public service in Durham.

agenda_items.title: Major Special Use Permit: American Tobacco Trail Phase E (M100001 / D0900196)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff reviewed required findings of fact under UDO Sections 3.9 and 4.9.3.D.2 for the American Tobacco Trail Phase E Major Thoroughfare Corridor buffer reduction, and the applicant explained that removing overlapping buffer restrictions on greenway easement areas would improve vegetative opacity and safe trail traffic. Council Member Mike Woodard moved approval, clarifying with staff that the written order was already prepared for adoption, and Council passed the motion 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Major Site Plan: American Tobacco Trail Phase E (D0900196)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Planning Director presented the companion Major Site Plan covering the entire 1.89-mile American Tobacco Trail Phase E section, noting Development Review Board recommendation for approval on March 19, 2010. Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden and seconded by Council Member Farad Ali, Council approved the site plan.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Ordinance to Revise Stormwater Rates (9.3% Increase)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a 9.3% stormwater rate increase effective July 1, 2010, explaining the program is wholly fee-funded and the increase supports 4.5 FTEs for illegal discharge enforcement, public education, staff training, and stormwater compliance. Citizens Allen Lang and E.L. Allison spoke during the public hearing, after which Council voted 6-0 to approve the ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Deferred Item (Continued to June 7 Meeting)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell opened the public hearing on Item 30, which had been flagged for deferral, and with no public comments offered, continued the matter to the June 7 City Council meeting.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 5: Setting Public Hearing for Petitioned Improvements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Item 5 had been pulled because citizen Allen Lang signed up on it mistakenly instead of Item 29. After confirming Mr. Lang had already spoken on Item 29, Council voted 6-0 to approve Item 5.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 21: Parking Fees Change
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen Allen Lang spoke on downtown parking fees, arguing that over $200,000 in fines owed by out-of-county drivers remained uncollected and urging the City to consider parking meters and wheel boots for delinquent out-of-county vehicles. Council then voted 6-0 to approve Item 21 and adjourned at 9:27 p.m.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 6, 2010 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden in the excused absence of Mayor Bill Bell, four members answered initial roll call (Cole-McFadden, Farad Ali, Eugene Brown, and Diane Catotti) before Council Members Mike Woodard and Howard Clement III arrived shortly thereafter; Catotti was later excused during the session. Council approved the City Manager's and City Attorney's priority items by voice vote, voted to suspend the rules to take action on Item 19 (East End Connector U-0071) ahead of the May 14 comment deadline, and reviewed the upcoming May 17 regular agenda including the proposed FY 2010–11 budget, water/sewer and stormwater rates, Stewart Heights low-income housing loan amendment, and the American Tobacco Trail Phase E applications. During discussions, Council members examined parking fee hours (6 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday–Friday) to reduce a general fund subsidy exceeding $700,000 for parking deck debt, debated cost-recovery fees charged to Partners Against Crime (PAC) groups for Parks and Recreation meetings, and heard citizen complaints regarding Durham Police Department conduct that prompted a request for an appointment with the City Manager and Police Chief Lopez. All recorded procedural and agenda-setting votes passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Excused Absence of Mayor Bell, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden called the work session to order at 1:16 p.m. with Farad Ali, Eugene Brown, and Diane Catotti present, and Council approved an excused absence for Mayor Bill Bell while noting Mike Woodard and Howard Clement III would arrive shortly. Council approved the City Manager's four priority items—a presentation on Item 17 (Harvard Ave Street Improvement Project), a rule-suspension request on Item 19 (East End Connector U-0071) before the May 14 comment deadline, and citizen no-shows on Items 31 and 32—and the City Attorney's two closed-session items.

agenda_items.title: Review of Upcoming May 17 Regular Meeting Agenda (Items 5–35)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk and Council reviewed agenda items including petitioned improvements, the Charles Buchanan Markham memorial resolution, Stewart Circle LP's loan amendment for 20 low-income tax credit units at Stewart Heights, CAD maintenance, Albright Community Association lease at 1017 Juniper Street, City-County interlocal agreements, ATT Phase E, Dell server lease, proposed FY 2010–11 budget and FY 2011–16 CIP, water/sewer and stormwater rates, economic development incentives (pulled), housing code demolition liens (Item 26, pulled by Catotti), and private utilities fees (Item 30, pulled). Council suspended the rules to take up Item 19 (East End Connector U-0071) as Council Members Mike Woodard and Howard Clement III joined the meeting.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously to suspend rules on Item 19 (voice vote)

agenda_items.title: Item 17 Presentation: ST-248 Harvard Avenue Street Improvement Project
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented on the Harvard Avenue Street Improvement Project, reporting that major condemnation concerns had passed and only minor clearance work remained before moving forward with construction.

agenda_items.title: Item 21 Discussion: Parking Fee Rates, Hours, and General Fund Subsidy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council members and staff discussed parking rate changes and revenue needed to cover parking deck debt service, noting the City transferred over $700,000 annually from the general fund to break even. Staff clarified that proposed parking charges would apply from 6:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. Monday through Friday rather than evenings and weekends.

agenda_items.title: Parks and Recreation Cost-Recovery Policy for PAC Meeting Fees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed Parks and Recreation's cost-recovery fee policy for Partners Against Crime (PAC) meetings, noting the Police Department sets aside $12,500 ($2,500 per PAC across five PACs) to pay valid PAC expenses. Some members questioned whether charging Parks and Recreation facility fees out of Police-allocated PAC funds was circular accounting, while staff emphasized departmental cost recovery.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Setting, Excused Absence of Catotti, and Citizens' Matters
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council excused Council Member Diane Catotti from the remainder of the session, approved the agenda assigning Items 25–30 as General Business public hearings, and heard citizen testimony (including Dr. Allison) regarding Durham Police Department conduct and property access following a tenant death at 119 property in November 2009 and a recent incident. Council directed setting an appointment with the City Manager and Police Chief Lopez to resolve the complaint.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Legislative Breakfast
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 4, 2010 Special City Council Meeting (Legislative Breakfast) presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, Diane Catotti, Howard Clement III, and Farad Ali (arriving) in attendance and Mike Woodard excused, Durham officials briefed the Durham delegation to the North Carolina General Assembly on the City's 2010 short-session legislative agenda. City staff presented one local charter amendment to authorize special stormwater assessments on benefited private properties—addressing legislator questions from Representative Michaux regarding appeal safeguards and assessment acceleration on undeveloped land—alongside resolutions supporting the Falls Lake consensus water management principles and Durham County's witness-intimidation and victim-protection bill. Mayor Bill Bell and Deputy City Manager Wanda Page also urged legislators to oppose Revenue Laws Study Committee restrictions on municipal broadband authority, while staff briefed the delegation on regional Jordan Lake water allocation efforts and state prisoner re-entry transition issues. No formal Council votes were taken during this informational legislative breakfast.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Overview of 2010 Short Session Legislative Package
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order and the Clerk called roll, noting Mike Woodard's excused absence and Farad Ali en route. Assistant to the City Manager Carmisha Wallace introduced the City's non-controversial short-session package: a charter amendment on stormwater assessments and two resolutions supporting Falls Lake consensus principles (adopted by Wake County and Raleigh) and victim/witness protection.

agenda_items.title: Charter Amendment Proposal: Stormwater Assessments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City legal staff Karen Sindelar explained the proposed charter amendment enabling Durham to construct or repair stormwater facilities and assess benefited private properties as a last resort when HOAs or private agreements fail, citing an increase in stormwater lawsuits over the past five years. Legislators including Representative Michaux questioned appeal safeguards and Section G acceleration on undeveloped parcels prior to building permits, and staff agreed to refine draft language to maintain unanimous delegation support.

agenda_items.title: Municipal Broadband Authority and Witness Protection Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell and Deputy City Manager Wanda Page urged the delegation to oppose a Revenue Laws Study Commission proposal restricting North Carolina municipalities from operating broadband as a local utility, noting Durham's universities and healthcare institutions could benefit from municipal broadband options in the future. Council Member Howard Clement III also highlighted ongoing coordination with Stormy Ellis and Senator McKissick on the victim and witness protection bill.

agenda_items.title: Prisoner Re-entry Study and Jordan Lake / Falls Lake Water Allocations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Officials discussed state prisoner release practices and homelessness/poverty study commission efforts, followed by a water resources update urging legislators not to place a moratorium on regional Jordan Lake water allocation recommendations pending before the Environmental Management Commission while state Water Resources Act legislation remained under review.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 3, 2010 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven Council members present, the Council presented proclamations for Older Americans Month, Drinking Water Week (honoring local and statewide student poster winners), Police Officers Memorial Day, and Public Service Week, and commended Neighborhood Improvement Services on 2010 Census outreach. Council unanimously (7-0) approved the City Manager's priority items (referring Item 9 back to staff and adding supplemental Item 25 on Rolling Hills/Southside financing) and unanimously (7-0) adopted the Consent Agenda. The centerpiece of the evening was supplemental Item 25—authorizing conditional subordinate financing ($5,486,468) and infrastructure commitments (up to $3,887,410) to MBA Development Corporation for 119 mixed-income rental units and 13 live-work units in Rolling Hills/Southside—which drew sharp criticism from nonprofit housing advocates and Council members worried about diverting future CDBG/HOME entitlements amid tight city budgets, while Mayor Bell argued Council could explore a half-cent property tax equivalent (~$1.3 million) to sustain nonprofit programs; Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved Item 25 (with the vote occurring during a brief omitted gap in the transcript digest), followed by a 7-0 vote excusing an absence for the May 4 legislative breakfast.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Proclamations, and Public Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. and Council Member Howard Clement III led the Pledge of Allegiance. Council presented proclamations for Older Americans Month (May 2010, noting 200+ participants in the Durham Senior Games), Drinking Water Week (May 2–8, honoring six local and state-level NC AWWA-WEA poster contest winners), Police Officers Memorial Day, and Public Service Week recognizing Durham's ~2,200 city employees.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items and Census Outreach Commendation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to approve the City Manager's priority items: referring Item 9 (FY 2010–11 Planning Department fee resolution) back to the administration and adding supplemental Item 25 (local funding commitment for Rolling Hills submission to the NC Housing Finance Agency). Council Member Howard Clement III then commended Department of Neighborhood Improvement Services Director Constance Stancil and staff for expanded 2010 Census outreach.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved 7-0 the Consent Agenda covering board/committee appointments (Board of Adjustment, Capital Program Advisory Committee, Equal Business Opportunity Program Advisory Committee, Durham Convention Center Authority), VOA Durham Maple Court loan documents, Item 10 (federal asset forfeiture funds), and Item 11 (NCDOT utility agreement U-4763B), excluding referred Item 9 and General Business items.

agenda_items.title: Item 7: Neighborhood Stabilization Program Grant Ordinance (Housing for New Hope)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Larry Jarvis presented Item 7, adopting a Neighborhood Stabilization Program grant project ordinance (superseding Ordinance 13814) to receive additional funds and award funding to Housing for New Hope. Further discussion and voting on this item occurred within the truncated middle portion of the digest.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote recorded in digest

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Item 25: Rolling Hills / Southside Redevelopment Conditional Financing Commitment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Southside residents and nonprofit housing providers (including Builders of Hope) objected to committing future federal CDBG/HOME entitlements to Rolling Hills/Southside at the expense of existing nonprofit programs and homeowner rehabilitation. Staff (Larry Jarvis) explained project timelines through August and noted new-unit purchase assistance was sometimes more cost-effective than rehabbing severely deteriorated homes; Council members voiced fiscal alarm given city budget constraints (such as being unable to fund a 15-officer police academy), while Mayor Bill Bell emphasized Council's prior support for nonprofits and noted a half-cent property tax could replace the ~$1.3M peak nonprofit allocation before Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved the conditional commitments of $5,486,468 (subordinate financing) and up to $3,887,410 (site/infrastructure).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Motion made (vote occurred in omitted transcript gap)

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence Request and Council Member Closing Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to approve an excused absence request for the May 4 morning legislative breakfast due to a work conflict. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden commended Pastor McCarter and Greater Joy International Ministries for ex-offender outreach following a fatal Dupree Street shooting, Council Member Eugene Brown noted he would be late to the breakfast due to a Habitat for Humanity event, and the meeting adjourned at 11:12 p.m.

disagreements.issue: Using Future Federal CDBG/HOME Entitlements for Rolling Hills / Southside Redevelopment (Item 25)
disagreements.summary: Public speakers, nonprofit housing providers, and Council members debated whether committing millions in future federal CDBG/HOME entitlements to MBA Development Corporation for Rolling Hills/Southside ($5.49M subordinate financing and up to $3.89M site/infrastructure) unfairly diverted funds from community nonprofits and existing Southside homeowners amid severe municipal budget constraints.
disagreements.side_a_position: Advance the Rolling Hills/Southside conditional financing commitment to catalyze neighborhood revitalization while exploring alternative funding for nonprofits.
side_a_arguments: The Rolling Hills project offered the best hope to address safety and disinvestment in a challenged neighborhood.

Council had already unanimously asked the administration to identify alternative financing plans, and Mayor Bell noted roughly half a cent on the property tax could replace the peak $1.3 million in prior annual nonprofit funding.
disagreements.side_b_position: Question committing future federal entitlements and reducing support for nonprofit housing and service providers or existing Southside residents.
side_b_arguments: Nonprofit developers such as Builders of Hope and Southside advocates warned that diverting funds left existing Southside homeowners without rehab support and threatened nonprofit housing/job-training capacity.
Critics on Council expressed shock at pledging future entitlements during a tight budget cycle when the City could not even afford a new 15-officer police academy.
disagreements.resolution: Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden moved the conditional commitments for MBA Development Corporation at [04:08:03]–[04:09:09]; the vote occurred in an omitted 8-second gap in the transcript digest before [04:09:17].

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting - Rolling Hills/Southside Redevelopment Initiative
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 29, 2010 Special City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with six members present and Council Member Farad Ali excused, the Council first approved by unanimous voice vote (6-0) the revised Use and Possession Agreement with Calvary Ministries for the Community Family Life and Recreation Center at Lyon Park, after discussing default reversion to the 1998 development agreement, shared-space cost escalators, and appointing a Council liaison rather than a voting board seat. Community Development Director Larry Jarvis then presented the ~$19.8 million city financial participation plan for the Rolling Hills/Southside Redevelopment 'tipping point' phase, relying heavily on a $7.053 million CDBG Section 108 loan, HOME funds, and pay-as-you-go homeownership write-downs alongside Self-Help acquisitions. Council members engaged in extensive policy debate with staff and developers over whether heavy multi-year CDBG/HOME commitments would drain momentum from Southwest Central Durham, whether past development losses ($6–7 million) posed undue financial risk, and whether the ratio of rental units to homeownership units was skewed too heavily toward rentals, though no formal vote on the Southside financing package was taken at the special meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Use and Possession Agreement for Lyon Park (Calvary Ministries)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the special meeting to order with six members present and Farad Ali excused. The City Attorney explained revisions to the Lyon Park Use and Possession Agreement reverting operations to the 1998 joint agreement in the event of default; Council discussed the Section 3 cost escalator covering 8,766 square feet of shared space and whether to place a voting member or a non-voting liaison on Calvary Ministries' 15-member board before passing the contract unanimously by voice vote (6-0).

agenda_items.title: Rolling Hills / Southside Redevelopment 'Tipping Point' Financing Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Larry Jarvis presented the ~$19.8 million city financial participation plan for the Rolling Hills/Southside tipping-point phase, detailing a $7,053,000 CDBG Section 108 loan (20-year repayment from annual entitlements), HOME funds for mixed-income rental phases (including 115 units at ~$4.6M), and $2.5M over five years for homeownership write-downs alongside Self-Help's ~15 South Street lots. Council members questioned impacts on Southwest Central Durham, security planning, past $6–7M project losses, CDBG spending accountability, and the rental-to-ownership ratio, while presenters argued rental phases were essential to overcome stigma and leverage $70M in private investment with $14M public dollars.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Remarks on Education / Budget Rally (People's Durham)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A speaker addressed Council regarding six months of organizing with students, teachers, and parents through the group People's Durham around budget pressures and an upcoming permitted march and rally.

votes.item_title: Adopt Revised Use and Possession Agreement for Community Family Life and Recreation Center at Lyon Park (Calvary Ministries)
votes.notes: Council Member Farad Ali had an excused absence; mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest; passed by voice vote without opposition.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to adopt the revised Use and Possession Agreement with Calvary Ministries for the Lyon Park facility.

disagreements.meeting_title: Special City Council Meeting - Rolling Hills/Southside Redevelopment Initiative
disagreements.issue: Rolling Hills / Southside Redevelopment Financing Risk, Entitlement Concentration, and Rental-vs-Ownership Mix
disagreements.summary: During the nearly three-hour presentation and work session on the ~$19.8 million Southside tipping-point financing plan, Council members questioned staff and developers over financial risk, multi-year entitlement commitments, security planning, and the heavy proportion of rental units relative to homeownership.
disagreements.side_a_position: Concentrate public Section 108/HOME commitments and start with mixed-income rental phases to overcome neighborhood stigma and attract major private capital.
side_a_arguments: Investing ~$14 million in public funds could leverage ~$70 million in private investment into Southside.
Given disinvestment and stigma in the area, rental development was a necessary initial step to establish stability before broader ownership sales.
disagreements.side_b_position: Scrutinize financial exposure, protect momentum in other target neighborhoods, and prioritize higher homeownership shares and clear security planning.
side_b_arguments: Members worried heavy commitments to Southside could stall progress in Southwest Central Durham and recalled a prior failed venture costing the City $6–7 million.
Speakers argued the ratio of rental to ownership units was 'definitely off' and should be reversed, and requested clear security/policing plans and historical CDBG accountability.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken at the April 29 special meeting; the financing commitment returned for formal action as supplemental Item 25 at the May 3, 2010 regular meeting.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 19, 2010 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council proclaimed April 24, 2010 as Day of Service recognizing Durham Latter-day Saints congregations, recognized Urban Farming and Kraft's garden behind Union Baptist Independent School, and commended Deputy City Manager Wanda Page on earning ICMA credentialed manager status. Council unanimously (7-0) referred Item 16 (roll-off container rates) and pulled Consent Item 26 (Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission) back to the administration, and passed the remaining Consent Agenda 7-0, along with unanimous 7-0 approvals for Item 28 (2010 Legislative Program proposals), Item 24 (a $15,000 Parrish Street retail incentive grant for Uno Restaurant and Market LLC at 102 City Hall Plaza), and Supplemental Item 29 (corrective water/sewer extension and assessment rate resolution). On General Business Item 7 (Beer and Wine Privilege License Issuance), Council split 6-1: Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Farad Ali voted Aye, while Howard Clement III voted Nay, objecting that 51 renewal and new applications had not come before Partners Against Crime (PAC) District 4 as he understood the checklist required.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Day of Service Proclamation, and Council Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order with all seven members present and proclaimed April 24, 2010 as Day of Service for six Durham congregations of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Council members also recognized an urban farm established on Corporation Street behind Union Baptist Independent School with Urban Farming and Kraft, and Council Member Howard Clement III commended Deputy City Manager Wanda Page on receiving ICMA voluntary credentialing.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the City Manager's request, Council voted 7-0 to refer Item 16 (roll-off container rental rates and disposal fees) back to the administration.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 26: Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission (Refer Back to Administration)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Howard Clement III pulled Item 26 (Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission) to refer it back to the administration for additional consideration, and Council approved his motion 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 7: Beer and Wine Privilege License Issuance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a motion to approve beer and wine privilege licenses, Council Member Howard Clement III questioned whether all 51 new and renewal applications had been reviewed by the respective Partners Against Crime (PAC) districts, noting that as chair of PAC 4 he did not recall receiving them. Although staff stated PAC contact via meetings or listserv was part of the checklist, Clement voted no while the remaining six Council members voted aye, passing 6-1.

agenda_items.title: Item 28: Proposals for 2010 Legislative Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no additional comments or questions, Council voted 7-0 to approve the proposed 2010 Legislative Program.

agenda_items.title: Item 24 Public Hearing: $15,000 Retail Incentive Grant for Uno Restaurant and Market LLC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Peter Coyle of the Office of Economic and Workforce Development presented a $15,000 Parrish Street merchandise-based retail incentive grant for Uno Restaurant and Market LLC to occupy vacant space at 102 City Hall Plaza, projecting 20 full-time and 21 part-time jobs and $1.8 million in first-year gross revenues, with endorsements from the Parrish Street Advocacy Group, Downtown Durham Inc., and PAC 5. After opening and closing the public hearing with no speakers, Council approved the grant 7-0.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering Stormwater Manager Ed Venable presented a corrective resolution replacing an incorrect resolution attached at the prior meeting regarding petitions for water/sewer extensions outside city limits and inside/outside assessment rates. meetings.executive_summary: At the April 8, 2010 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with five members at roll call (Mike Woodard excused and Farad Ali arriving shortly thereafter), Council heard remarks requesting a memorial resolution and portrait for former Mayor Charles Markham, highlighted the NC Dental Society's Missions of Mercy free clinic in Durham, and received Mayor Priscilla Everette-Oates of Princeville thanking Durham for donating a fire vehicle. meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 5, 2010 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with five members present and Council Members Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti excused, Council presented proclamations for Fair Housing Month, National Public Safety 911 Communications Officer Week, and a resolution memorializing former Council Member Alton Carroll Pleasants (1971–1983). All actions passed unanimously by 5-0 votes: referring the Lyon Park use-and-possession agreement portion of Item 12 back to administration while keeping its budget motion on the agenda; adopting the Consent Agenda; approving a 1.24-acre rezoning for a Bojangles at the South Durham Lowe's development; accepting a Parks and Recreation supplemental grant/donation; and approving pulled Consent Item 33, a memorandum of agreement authorizing the City Manager to begin negotiations with Triangle Transit to manage Durham's bus and paratransit services (DATA) after citizens raised concerns about potential Route 10, evening, and Sunday service cuts. Council also approved an excused absence for Mike Woodard for the April 8 work session in case a Greensboro DOT meeting ran late.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m., noting excused absences for Eugene Brown and Diane Catotti. meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 18, 2010 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present at roll call, Council approved priority items from the City Manager, City Attorney (adding a closed session and revised 2010 Legislative Program), and City Clerk (referring minutes back and flagging Passenger Vehicle for Hire appointments), and granted upcoming excused absences for Diane Catotti and Eugene Brown. Following a clarification from the City Attorney confirming that delaying a quasi-judicial hearing solely for additional testimony was unprecedented, Council suspended the rules and unanimously approved the sale of 517B Eastway Avenue (Item 9). Later in the session, Council reviewed stormwater redevelopment compliance, heard Walltown Community Association remarks and flagged hazardous buckled park stairs for Public Works inspection, suspended the rules to resolve board appointments—including appointing Maria Singleton and Pernell Kennedy to the Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission, Edwin Vignet to break a 4-4 DPAC Oversight Committee tie, and Rebecca Winders to the Planning Commission—set the upcoming regular meeting agenda, and granted Eugene Brown an excused absence ahead of surgery.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Priority Items, Excused Absences, and Quasi-Judicial Guidance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:15 p.m. with all seven members present. Council unanimously approved priority items for the City Manager (including budget guidelines, Walltown Aquatics Center, City Center market study, BPAC report, Triangle Transit MOA, Census update, NC 147 pedestrian bridge video, and NCDOT pothole repair), City Attorney (closed session and legislative program), and City Clerk, approved April excused absences for Diane Catotti and Eugene Brown (plus a 2:15 p.m. excuse), and heard the City Attorney confirm that deferring an open quasi-judicial hearing merely for extra testimony was unprecedented.

agenda_items.title: Item 9: Rule Suspension and Approval of Sale of 517B Eastway Avenue
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During the agenda walkthrough—where Items 6 and 12 were pulled for discussion—Council voted unanimously by voice vote to suspend the rules and approve the proposed sale of property at 517B Eastway Avenue (PIN 0831-10-45-4470).

agenda_items.title: Stormwater Redevelopment Compliance and Walltown Park Safety Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the session, Council discussed enforcing the 40% stormwater redevelopment threshold and heard Walltown Community Association remarks from Ms. Hooker praising neighborhood improvements. A Council member also asked Public Works staff to inspect tree-root damage that had buckled concrete steps at the northwest corner of Walltown Park.

agenda_items.title: Advisory Board Ballot Results and Rule Suspensions for Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk reported ballot results: Marty Berlin (6 votes) and a 4-4 tie between Edwin Vignet and Sherrim Lamee Lord on the DPAC Oversight Committee; Jarvis Martin (7 votes) on the Planning Commission; Susan Stroll and Kevin Turner (7 votes each) on the Appearance Commission; and Maria Singleton and Pernell Kennedy (7 votes each) on the Passenger Vehicle for Hire Commission. Council suspended the rules to immediately appoint Singleton and Kennedy, broke the DPAC tie by unanimously appointing Edwin Vignet, and unanimously appointed Rebecca Winders to the Planning Commission.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Agenda and Excused Absence for Eugene Brown
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously set the next regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 5, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13–21, and 33; GBA Items 6 and 12; and GBA public hearings Items 27–29), held a closed session, and unanimously approved an excused absence for Council Member Eugene Brown ahead of scheduled surgery.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 15, 2010 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with six members present and Council Member Mike Woodard absent with an excused absence, the Council approved the Consent Agenda (excluding pulled Items 12, 13, and 14) 6-0, expedited review of the Riparian Buffers UDO Text Amendment (TC0900008) 6-0, and later approved pulled workforce training grants (Items 12 and 13) and the Equal Business Opportunity ordinance extension (Item 14) 6-0. After public hearings on mini assessment rolls for Roland Street (Item 22) and Belvin Road (Item 23), the Council held a quasi-judicial hearing on the McDonald's Parking Lot Major Special Use Permit (Item 27, M0700002/D07-548) and its companion Major Site Plan and Floodplain Development Permit (Item 28). On Item 27, the Council voted 5-1 to grant the permit with staff-recommended conditions, with Ayes from Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Eugene Brown, and Farad Ali, and a Nay from Diane Catotti (Mike Woodard absent). On Item 28, the Council initially voted 6-0 to approve the site plan, then voted 6-0 to reconsider Item 28 so Diane Catotti could register her opposition on the companion item, and passed Item 28 by a final 5-1 vote with Ayes from Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Eugene Brown, and Farad Ali, and a Nay from Diane Catotti (Mike Woodard absent).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Proclamation, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m., Council Member Howard Clement III led the pledge, and the Clerk confirmed six members present with Council Member Mike Woodard having an excused absence. A proclamation was presented to Jamie Vellbano, and the City Manager reported no priority items while noting a non-substantive formatting update to Item 19 and supplemental information requested by Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden on Item 20. Council approved the priority items 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Items 12, 13, and 14)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the consent items, including minutes approval, appointments to the Durham Area Transit Authority Board of Trustees, Durham Cultural Advisory Board, and Workforce Development Board, financial audits, a HOME/Builders of Hope agreement for ten properties in Southwest Central Durham, an EPA Climate Showcase Communities grant ordinance, 1510 East Main Street rehabilitation, the 2010-2011 annual assurance plan, a Nation Avenue sewer extension, street improvements, and Contract SR-51 sanitary sewer repairs. Items 12, 13, and 14 were pulled for separate discussion, and the remaining consent agenda passed 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 21: Amendment to Unified Development Ordinance — Riparian Buffers (TC0900008)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Medlin of the Durham City-County Planning Department requested expedited review for the riparian buffer text amendment (TC0900008) once the state Division of Water Quality (DWQ) returns comments on the draft submitted by the March 10 deadline under Jordan Reservoir nutrient management rules. Because local jurisdictions have two months after DWQ's six-month review to adopt the ordinance, expedited review is needed to meet state timelines. Council approved the item 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Items 22 & 23: Public Hearings on Mini Assessment Rolls (Roland Street and Belvin Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater staff presented Item 22, a continued mini assessment roll for street opening, curb, gutter, paving, and water main improvements benefiting the Webb property on Roland Street, and recommended confirmation. With no public speakers, Council closed the public hearing and confirmed Item 22 by a 6-0 vote before opening the public hearing on Item 23 for Belvin Road curb, gutter, paving, water, and sewer improvements.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 6-0 (Item 22); Item 23 outcome omitted in truncated transcript

agenda_items.title: Item 27: Quasi-Judicial Hearing — Major Special Use Permit, McDonald's Parking Lot (M0700002 / D07-548)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During a quasi-judicial hearing on the McDonald's parking lot expansion, counsel cautioned Council members about ex parte lobbying and special-knowledge disqualification risks compared to standard public hearings. Staff presented three options and recommended granting the Major Special Use Permit with conditions requiring substantial consistency with submitted plans (D07-548) and completion of site improvements prior to compliance. Council approved Option 1 by a 5-1 vote, with Diane Catotti voting against.

agenda_items.title: Item 28: Major Site Plan and Floodplain Development Permit — McDonald's Parking Lot (D07-00548)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Steve Medlin presented the companion Major Site Plan and Floodplain Development Permit (D07-00548) for the McDonald's parking lot expansion, confirming compliance with all UDO standards. Council initially approved Item 28 by a 6-0 vote (Mayor Bell briefly misstated 7-0 before correcting to 6-0), then later voted 6-0 to reconsider Item 28 so Diane Catotti could record her Nay vote consistent with Item 27, resulting in a final 5-1 approval.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items 12, 13, and 14: Employment Training Grants and Equal Business Opportunity Extension
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speaker Mr. Peterson addressed pulled Items 12 and 13 (City of Durham Employment Training 2008-2010 and 2009-2011 grant ordinances, including a $425,000 youth demonstration grant), urging incentives for companies to hire locally trained residents and youth; staff clarified the Item 12 funds support networking and leadership development for laid-off and underemployed professionals. On Item 14 (extension of the Equal Business Opportunities ordinance and advisory committee), Equal Opportunity/Equity Assurance Director Deborah Giles confirmed the EBO program applies to all city contracting opportunities. Council approved Items 12, 13, and 14 each by 6-0 votes.

disagreements.summary: Council voted 5-1 on both the Major Special Use Permit (Item 27) and, upon reconsideration, the companion Major Site Plan and Floodplain Development Permit (Item 28) for the McDonald's parking lot expansion, with Diane Catotti dissenting.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 4, 2010 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, the Council approved City Manager and City Clerk priority items (including two supplemental items and notice of a valid protest petition on Item 25, West Point on the Eno) unanimously, reviewed upcoming consent and public-hearing items, and set the next regular meeting agenda unanimously. The Council heard a presentation on establishing a sister city relationship with Zhuzhou in Hunan Province, China (Item 29), received a quarterly report on youth, Durham Tech, and Lincoln Community Health Center programs at the Holton Career and Resource Center (Item 20), and reviewed the state-mandated Riparian Buffers UDO text amendment (Item 21, TC0900008) ahead of the March 10 Division of Water Quality submission deadline. In written ballot appointments reported by the City Clerk, Stephen Williams was appointed to the Workforce Development Board with 6 votes and Catherine McLean was appointed to the Durham Area Transit Authority Board (4 votes in ASR) alongside three appointments to the Durham Cultural Advisory Board; individual member ballot votes were not read aloud in the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Priority Items, and Valid Protest Petition Notice
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:05 p.m. and Council members congratulated him on being elected President of the North Carolina Metropolitan Mayors Coalition. The City Manager introduced two supplemental priority items—Item 29 (Zhuzhou, China sister city relationship) and Item 30 (a carried-over zoning map change)—which passed unanimously. The City Clerk reported a valid protest petition on Item 25 (Zoning Map Change on Jennifer Eno Drive at West Point on the Eno), which Council accepted unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Consent and Public Hearing Agenda Walkthrough
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk read through administrative, consent, presentation, and public hearing items for the upcoming cycle, including Builders of Hope's 1510 East Main Street ARRA rehabilitation, employment and training grant ordinances, the Equal Business Opportunities ordinance extension, sidewalk and paving contracts, sanitary sewer repairs, mini assessment rolls on Roland Street and Belvin Road, and the McDonald's parking lot special use permit and site plan.

agenda_items.title: Item 29: Proposed Sister City Relationship with Zhuzhou, Hunan Province, China
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Representatives from Sister Cities and an NC State University professor serving as President of the Carolina China Council and trade representative for Hunan Province presented a proposal linking Durham with Zhuzhou (population ~4 million, $12 billion GDP, precision manufacturing) as part of a regional triangle cluster under North Carolina's state-to-province letter of intent. The delegation invited Durham to participate in a June 21–22 sister city forum in Hunan with in-country lodging, meals, and transportation funded by Hunan Province.

agenda_items.title: Item 20: Holton Career and Resource Center Quarterly Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Parks and Recreation staff (including Andrea White) and Lincoln Community Health Center representatives reported on operations at the Holton Career and Resource Center, noting $18,367 in sliding-scale fee waivers for after-school care (ages 6–12), Claymation programming, Durham Tech classes, and Lincoln clinic patients averaging 1.2 chronic conditions led by hypertension and diabetes. Council Member Mike Woodard asked staff to track clinic utilization by zip code and return during the May budget process with utilization data for the Burton Heights facility.

agenda_items.title: Item 21: Riparian Buffers UDO Text Amendments (TC0900008)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the draft Riparian Buffers UDO text amendment (TC0900008) due to the state Division of Water Quality (DWQ) by March 10 under Jordan Lake nutrient rules, combining state mandates, EEUDO steering committee recommendations (expanding suburban/rural stream buffers from 50 to 100 feet and wetland buffers from 25 to 50 feet), and Neuse/Jordan rule alignment. Staff noted Council did not need to adopt the ordinance immediately, only provide comments before submission and consider an expedited hearing resolution ahead of the April 13 Planning Commission hearing.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Agenda and Advisory Board Ballot Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted unanimously to set the March 15 regular meeting agenda with Consent Items 1–4, 6–16, 18, and 19, General Business Items 21 and 28, and General Business Public Hearings 22–27. The Clerk announced ballot appointments for the Durham Area Transit Authority Board (Catherine McLean), three Durham Cultural Advisory Board seats, and the Workforce Development Board (Stephen Williams with 6 votes) before adjournment at 3:00 p.m.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (agenda); Ballot appointments (6 votes for Stephen Williams)

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 1, 2010 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members voting, the Council presented ceremonial resolutions for Multiple Sclerosis Awareness Week, American Red Cross Month, and the late Patricia Diane Elliott Riley Amey, and heard a presentation on pursuing 1,000-megabit high-speed broadband service in Durham. Following priority reports—including the City Clerk's finding that protest petitions on three zoning map changes (Items 15, 16, and 20) were invalid—Council unanimously approved priority items 7-0 and heard remarks honoring the Durham Affordable Housing Coalition's 20th anniversary. On General Business Public Hearings, the Council unanimously approved 7-0 the transportation special use permit (Item 17), major special use permit M090005 (Item 18), and major site plan D080029 (Item 19) for the new middle school and city park, as well as the West Point at 751 commercial rezoning (Item 20, Z0803031) with 18 committed elements. Council also voted 7-0 to grant Mike Woodard an excused absence for the March 15 meeting before adjourning at 9:27 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Ceremonial Resolutions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m., Council Member Howard Clement III led the pledge, and the Clerk called the roll (noting one member arriving in about 15 minutes). Mayor Bell presented three resolutions: Multiple Sclerosis Awareness Week, American Red Cross Month (recognizing Council Member Howard Clement III's service on the Red Cross board), and a memorial resolution honoring Patricia Diane Elliott Riley Amey of Healing with CAARE.

agenda_items.title: High-Speed Broadband (1,000 Mbps) Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A presentation highlighted efforts with the Durham Convention and Visitors Bureau and partner organizations to pursue 1,000-megabit-per-second broadband service in Durham. Speakers illustrated the potential benefits by comparing download speeds and citing real-time emergency MRI consultations between Duke University Medical Center and Durham Regional Hospital.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items, Protest Petition Rulings, and Council Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager had no priority items, the City Attorney noted he would make a personal disclosure on Item 16 regarding the new middle school items, and the City Clerk reported that protest petitions filed on zoning Items 15, 16, and 20 were all ruled invalid. Council approved the priority items 7-0, and Council Member Howard Clement III commended Mark Trustin and the Durham Affordable Housing Coalition on its 20th anniversary.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1–5, 9, and Related Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell introduced the consent agenda, including approval of Council minutes, the January 2010 bid report, a memorial resolution for former Council Member Alton Carroll Pleasants, an ARRA subrecipient contract with the Center for Community Self-Help for three Walltown properties, the comprehensive annual financial report, and Section 5317 New Freedom transit funding with Durham's Coordinating Council for Senior Citizens. The consent vote fell within the middle gap omitted in the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Items 17, 18, and 19: New Middle School and City Park Permits and Site Plan (M090005 / D080029)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council acted on three companion approvals for the new middle school and city park: Item 17 (Transportation Special Use Permit) and Item 18 (Major Special Use Permit M090005), each approved under Option 1 with staff-recommended conditions by 7-0 votes. Planning staff then confirmed that Item 19 (Major Site Plan and Preliminary Plan D080029) met all UDO setback, height, buffer, and tree-coverage requirements, and Council approved it 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 20: Zoning Map Change — West Point at 751 (Z0803031)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Zoning Map Change Z0803031 for 17.43 acres at NC 751 and I-40 (West Point at 751), noting an 11-0 Planning Commission recommendation and comprehensive plan consistency for commercial uses. Applicant representatives Kenneth Spaulding and George Stanfield highlighted seven neighborhood meetings resulting in 18 non-transportation committed elements covering lighting, buffers, setbacks, height limits, bike lanes, and stormwater. With no opposition speakers, Council closed the hearing and approved the rezoning 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence Request and Free Dental Clinic Announcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Mike Woodard requested and received a 7-0 excused absence for the March 15 meeting to attend a National League of Cities Transportation Infrastructure Committee meeting in Washington, D.C. Council Member Howard Clement III announced the North Carolina Dental Society's free Missions of Mercy adult dental clinic on March 12–13 at the National Guard Armory with no income requirements before adjournment at 9:27 p.m.

votes.item_title: Priority Items (City Attorney and City Clerk Reports)
votes.notes: Mayor Bell announced 'seven to zero' (ASR transcribed 'Senate zero').
votes.discussion_detail: Motion approving the priority items reported by the City Attorney and City Clerk (including invalidation rulings on three zoning protest petitions).

votes.item_title: Item 17: Transportation Special Use Permit — New Middle School
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion approving Option 1 (grant permit with staff-recommended conditions) for the new middle school transportation special use permit.

votes.item_title: Item 18: Major Special Use Permit — New Middle School (M090005)
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion approving Option 1 (grant permit with staff-recommended conditions) for Major Special Use Permit M090005.

votes.item_title: Item 19: Major Site Plan and Preliminary Plan — New Middle School and City Park (D080029)
votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion approving the companion major site plan and preliminary plan D080029 upon staff confirmation of full UDO compliance.

votes.item_title: Item 20: Zoning Map Change — West Point at 751 (Z0803031)
votes.notes: Passed 7-0 following public hearing with no opposition speakers.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion approving the 17.43-acre West Point at 751 commercial rezoning (hotel, restaurant, retail, office) with 18 non-transportation committed elements.

votes.notes: Passed 7-0.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion granting Mike Woodard an excused absence for the March 15, 2010 Council meeting to attend a National League of Cities Transportation Infrastructure Committee meeting in Washington, D.C.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 18, 2010 City Council Work Session opened by Mayor Bill Bell (who noted he would depart around 1:50 p.m. to meet with the Governor, leaving Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden to chair the remainder), the Council addressed Falls Lake nutrient regulations, yard-waste contracting, affordable housing grants, and bridge closures. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items (requesting rule suspensions for Item 8 on Falls Lake legal services and Item 22 on the yard-waste/compost contract, and adding supplemental Item 23 on Falls Lake Consensus Principles), while the City Clerk reported invalid protest petitions on the Treyburn middle school and West Point at 751 rezonings. After questioning the use of stormwater and water/sewer funds on Item 8 and reviewing worst-case $1 billion 10-to-20-year exposure estimates for Falls Lake nutrient compliance, Council unanimously approved the Falls Lake Consensus Principles resolution (Item 23). Council also heard an urgent bridge-inspector road closure report, discussed HUB/SDB contracting participation, unanimously set the next meeting agenda, and voted to enter closed session; no split votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Mayor's Remarks on Princeville, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:01 p.m. (noting Mike Woodard and Diane Catotti were arriving shortly) and stated he had no issue with how individual members voted on the recent Princeville surplus equipment item, only seeking clear staff communication. The City Manager presented three priority items: suspending the rules to vote on Item 8 (Falls Lake legal services) and Item 22 (yard waste/compost contract), and adding supplemental Item 23 (Falls Lake Consensus Principles). Council approved the priority items unanimously, and the City Clerk reported invalid protest petitions on the new middle school and West Point at 751 rezonings.

agenda_items.title: Mandatory Ethics Training Legislation and Local Ordinance Subcommittees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed newly enacted state legislation (effective January 1) requiring ethics workshops for elected officials and reviewed plans for ad hoc subcommittees working with the police attorney and staff to update local ordinances.

agenda_items.title: Item 8: Falls Lake Legal Services Funding Inquiry
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Responding to a citizen complaint relayed by Council Member Eugene Brown questioning whether stormwater funds could legally pay for Falls Lake legal services, staff and the City Attorney confirmed the work directly concerns stormwater facilities as well as water and sewer treatment requirements at the North Durham plant, making both enterprise funds appropriate sources. The final vote on Item 8 fell within the omitted middle portion of the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Item 23: Falls Lake Nutrient Management Strategy Consensus Principles
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained Stage 1 nutrient compliance, the 2019–2021 Stage 2 reexamination milestone, and the worst-case $1 billion stormwater and wastewater exposure over 10–20 years if regulatory modifications are not achieved, noting Durham faces the largest reduction obligation due to its wastewater plant size. Following discussion with Diane Catotti and Eugene Brown, Council unanimously adopted Item 23 supporting the TJCOG Chairs and Mayors Consensus Principles.

agenda_items.title: Item 4 (Center for Community Self-Help) and HUB/SDB Contracting Participation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On pulled Item 4 (an ARRA subrecipient contract with the Center for Community Self-Help), Council Member Farad Ali asked about the remaining two NOFA proposals, and staff explained Builders of Hope and Preservation Durham would come forward in subsequent cycles. Council and presenters also discussed HUB, MBE, and SDB contractor participation, bid competitiveness, pre-qualification, and Governor's Executive Order No. 50 providing preference for North Carolina companies.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence, Culvert Road Closure, Agenda Setting, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council unanimously approved a member's excused absence request for a Saturday PAC1 meeting due to coaching Little League, and staff (Mr. Voorhees) announced an immediate culvert/bridge road closure ordered by the bridge inspector while Kimley-Horn designs the replacement. Council then unanimously set the upcoming meeting agenda and voted to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: City Manager Priority Items (Items 8, 22, and Supplemental Item 23)
votes.notes: At [00:00:30], Diane Catotti and Mike Woodard had not yet arrived; it is unclear from the truncated digest whether they arrived before this vote. Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion approving the City Manager's priority items requesting rule suspension on Items 8 and 22 and adding supplemental Item 23.

votes.item_title: Item 23: Resolution Supporting Consensus Principles for Falls Lake Nutrient Management Strategy
votes.notes: Mayor Bill Bell had noted at [00:01:02] he planned to leave around 1:50 p.m.; passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion approving the resolution endorsing the TJCOG Chairs and Mayors Consensus Principles to guide the Falls Lake Nutrient Management Strategy.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence Request for Saturday PAC1 Meeting
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion granting an excused absence for a council member coaching a 10:00 a.m. Little League game conflicting with a PAC1 meeting.

votes.item_title: Set Agenda for Next Regular Meeting
votes.notes: Passed unanimously by voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion setting the upcoming regular council meeting agenda.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 15, 2010 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council presented proclamations for Black History Month, Human Relations Month, the Year of the Young Child, and Keep Durham Beautiful's fifth consecutive national award, and referred Item 11 (yard waste and compost facility contract) back to the February 18 work session. On the Consent Agenda, Council approved Items 1, 2, 4–8, and 10 unanimously 7-0, but split 5-2 on Item 3 (Donation of Surplus Equipment to the Town of Princeville), with Ayes from Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Diane Catotti, and Farad Ali, and Nays from Mike Woodard and Eugene Brown. On the General Business Agenda, Council voted 6-1 to approve Item 14 (Full Frame Documentary Film Festival), with Ayes from Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Farad Ali, and a Nay from Howard Clement III. The meeting adjourned at 7:27 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Ceremonial Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. and the Clerk confirmed all seven Council members present. Proclamations were presented for Black History Month, Human Relations Month (accepted by Human Relations Director Bonnie Pena), and 2010 as the Year of the Young Child, followed by remarks from Keep Durham Beautiful leaders celebrating five consecutive national awards, improved litter index scores, a $2.59–$4.00 return per city/county dollar, and a 500-tarp giveaway.

agenda_items.title: Priority Item (Referral of Item 11) and Council Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested that Item 11 (contract to operate the yard waste and compost facility) be referred back to the February 18, 2010 Work Session, which Council moved and seconded. Council Member Howard Clement III also commended the Hayti Heritage organization and Director Diane Pleasants for the Spirits of Hayti program honoring former Mayor Chester Jenkins posthumously.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Including Item 3: Donation of Surplus Equipment to Town of Princeville)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted on the Consent Agenda covering minutes, the December 2009 bid report, the Princeville surplus equipment donation (Item 3), Durham Affordable Housing Coalition home repair, Operation Breakthrough weatherization, Criminal Justice Resource Center, police vehicles, employment medical services, and Adopt-a-Trail grant. While all remaining consent items passed 7-0, Mike Woodard and Eugene Brown both recorded Nay votes on Item 3, resulting in a 5-2 passage for the Princeville donation.

agenda_items.title: Item 14: Full Frame Documentary Film Festival
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On General Business Agenda Item 14 regarding the Full Frame Documentary Film Festival, Council Member Howard Clement III stated that he opposed the organization's request and voted No. After clarifying that General Business Agenda dissent requires an electronic/recorded No vote, Mayor Bell announced the item passed 6-1 with Howard Clement III voting Nay before adjourning at 7:27 p.m.

votes.item_title: Item 14: Full Frame Documentary Film Festival
votes.notes: Mayor Bell initially said 6-0 and corrected to '6 to 1 with Mr. Clement voting no'.
votes.discussion_detail: General Business Agenda request regarding the Full Frame Documentary Film Festival; Howard Clement III stated his opposition and voted Nay.

disagreements.issue: Donation of Surplus City Equipment to the Town of Princeville (Item 3)
disagreements.summary: Council approved donating surplus city vehicles and equipment to the Town of Princeville by a 5-2 vote, with Mike Woodard and Eugene Brown dissenting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the donation of surplus city equipment to support the Town of Princeville.
side_a_arguments: Supporting Princeville's request helps the town bring municipal services in-house and save money (as presented at the Feb 4 work session).
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose donating auctionable surplus equipment to another municipality.
side_b_arguments: Mike Woodard and Eugene Brown recorded No votes on Item 3 (consistent with Eugene Brown's Feb 4 work session concern over giving away $25,000+ in auctionable equipment amid Durham's own budget cuts and layoffs).
disagreements.resolution: Item 3 passed 5-2 (Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Diane Catotti, Farad Ali; Nays: Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown).

disagreements.summary: Council voted 6-1 to approve Item 14 for the Full Frame Documentary Film Festival, with Howard Clement III dissenting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the Full Frame Documentary Film Festival request.
side_a_arguments: Majority supported advancing the General Business Agenda item as presented.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the organization's request on Item 14.
side_b_arguments: Howard Clement III stated he opposed the request by the organization and cast the lone Nay vote.
disagreements.resolution: Item 14 passed 6-1 (Ayes: Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Farad Ali; Nay: Howard Clement III).

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 4, 2010 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden with Mayor Bill Bell and all Council members participating, the Council approved City Manager and City Attorney priority items (including a closed session on Hunter et al. v. City of Durham) unanimously, suspended the rules to approve a Third Fork Creek Phase 1B design contract amendment unanimously, and set the February 15 meeting agenda unanimously before entering closed session. Under a point of personal privilege, Mayor Bell introduced Town of Princeville Mayor Priscilla Everette-Oates, who requested surplus dump trucks, trash trucks, and police cars, prompting Council Member Eugene Brown to object to giving away over $25,000 in auctionable assets while Durham faces layoffs, foreclosures, and budget cuts. Council also heard status presentations on the Durham Walks Pedestrian Plan (noting $1.9 million in remaining 2005/2006 bond funds and 27% citizen satisfaction in 2007), the Capital Program Advisory Committee's second-quarter report (~90% of projects on schedule and budget), and Item 8 on employment-related medical services (affecting two current city positions). No formal split votes occurred during this work session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Priority Items, and Third Fork Creek Phase 1B Design Contract Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the work session to order at 1:01 p.m. on behalf of Mayor Bill Bell. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority schedule and the City Attorney's request for a closed session in Hunter et al. v. City of Durham (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)). Council then suspended the rules and unanimously approved a Third Fork Creek Phase 1B design contract amendment after asking General Services Director Joel to check whether the engineering firm offers internships for underrepresented groups.

agenda_items.title: Point of Personal Privilege: Town of Princeville Surplus Equipment Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell introduced Princeville Mayor Priscilla Everette-Oates, who requested a donation of surplus dump trucks, trash trucks, and three police cars to help Princeville bring contracted services in-house amid tight municipal budgets. Council Member Eugene Brown objected, questioning why Durham should give away over $25,000 in auctionable surplus equipment to another municipality when Durham has laid off staff, faces another difficult budget retreat, and averaged seven foreclosures per day in January.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (scheduled for Feb 15 consent)

agenda_items.title: Durham Walks Pedestrian Plan Status Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation and engineering staff reviewed implementation of the 2006 Durham Walks Pedestrian Plan, reporting roughly $1.9 million remaining from the 2005/2006 bond for sidewalk repairs, curb ramp installations, a 27% satisfaction rating in the 2007 citizen survey, and a UNC pedestrian safety grant. Council members discussed texting-while-driving safety concerns, sidewalk needs along NC 55 and North Roxboro, and re-scoring modified project endpoints without convening a new citizen committee.

agenda_items.title: Item 13: Capital Program Advisory Committee (CPAC) Second Quarter Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Bertha Johnson and CPAC Chair Charles Watts presented the second-quarter capital program report, noting approximately 90% of capital projects were on schedule and within budget and expressing satisfaction with Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) delivery.

agenda_items.title: Item 8: Employment-Related Medical Services Consolidation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated Council on two November 1, 2009 contracts (with Health Screening Inc. for drug testing and Research Triangle Occupational Health Services for firefighter wellness) and reviewed the third recommendation covering 1,287 patient visits in 2009 (mostly pre-employment physicals and on-the-job injury evaluations, with >1,300 projected in 2010). Staff noted the proposal would eliminate two current employee positions (after one employee found work elsewhere) and said those two employees were being referred to compete for open city positions.

agenda_items.title: ARRA Update, Durham Affordable Housing Coalition Audit Inquiry, Agenda Setting, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff noted no changes on the ARRA update, and a Council member asked the City Manager for the status of the Durham Affordable Housing Coalition audit and the impact of a 20% penalty on its city contract. Council then unanimously set the February 15 regular meeting agenda (Consent Items 1–8, 10, 11; General Business Item 14) and voted to enter closed session.

votes.notes: Passed by unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion approving the City Manager's priority item presentation times and ARRA update schedule.

votes.notes: Passed by unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion accepting the City Attorney's request for a brief closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) regarding Hunter et al. v. City of Durham.

votes.notes: Passed by unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to suspend Council rules to vote immediately on the non-ARRA Third Fork Creek Phase 1B design contract amendment.

votes.item_title: Third Fork Creek Phase 1B Design Contract Amendment
votes.notes: Passed by unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approval of the Third Fork Creek Phase 1B design contract amendment, with a request for staff to follow up on whether the firm offers internships for underrepresented groups.

votes.item_title: Set Agenda (Consent Items 1–8, 10, 11; GBA Item 14)
votes.notes: Passed by unanimous voice vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion setting the February 15, 2010 Regular City Council meeting agenda with Consent Items 1–8, 10, 11 and General Business Agenda Item 14.

disagreements.summary: Following Princeville Mayor Priscilla Everette-Oates's request for surplus trucks and police cars, Council Member Eugene Brown questioned donating over $25,000 in auctionable equipment to another municipality while Durham faced staff layoffs, foreclosures, and budget shortfalls.
disagreements.side_a_position: Prepare a resolution to donate surplus city vehicles to assist the Town of Princeville.
side_a_arguments: Mayor Bill Bell invited the Princeville Mayor and noted staff compiled available surplus vehicles for Council consideration on February 15.
Princeville sought dump trucks, trash trucks, and three police cars to perform services in-house, save funds, and create local jobs.

Durham County averaged seven foreclosures per day in January, and auctioning the surplus equipment could yield over $25,000.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken at the work session; the item remained on the February 15 Consent Agenda, where it later passed 5-2 with Eugene Brown and Mike Woodard voting Nay.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 1, 2010 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Mayor Bell delivered his eighth State of the City Address, citing declining violent and property crime rates, 284 jobs saved or created with stimulus funds, a projected $15 million budget gap for the upcoming fiscal year, upcoming Coffee with Council budget sessions, and the city's first long-term strategic plan. The Council unanimously approved the Consent Agenda 7-0, adopted the Reality Check regional smart-growth resolution (Item 11) 7-0, and unanimously passed the Downtown Zoning Update package—the UDO Text Amendment (Item 17 area), Comprehensive Plan Amendment (Item 18), and Zoning Map Change replacing downtown overlays with form-based Downtown Design Districts (Item 19)—each by 7-0 votes. In written balloting for a Durham Planning Commission appointment (Item 5), the City Clerk reported an appointee received 4 votes (a 4-vote majority; individual member ballot votes and the appointee's name were not clearly captured in the transcript digest). The meeting adjourned at 9:13 p.m. after a winter-weather solid waste collection update.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Mayor's Eighth State of the City Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with all seven Council members present and delivered his eighth State of the City Address. He reported downtown revitalization exceeding revenue projections, 21 homicides in 2009 (second lowest in eight years, with violent crime down ~26% and property crime down >30% since 2000), 284 jobs saved or created via stimulus dollars, Jordan/Falls Lake water challenges, a projected $15 million budget gap due to depressed sales, occupancy, and development revenues, upcoming Coffee with Council sessions, and the city's first long-term strategic plan.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 1–4 and Related Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no priority items from the City Manager, City Attorney, or City Clerk, Council approved the Consent Agenda—including Council minutes, a Triangle Transit Authority Board of Trustees reappointment, a Cultural Advisory Committee appointment, and a Durham Historic Preservation Commission appointment—by a 7-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Item 5: Durham Planning Commission Ballot Appointment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council cast written ballots for an appointment to the Durham Planning Commission (held over from January 19). At the close of the meeting, the City Clerk reported that the selected appointee received four votes.

agenda_items.title: Item 11: Reality Check Project Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a point of order, Council took up Item 11 (the Triangle region Reality Check smart-growth resolution supporting transit, vibrant downtown centers, and compact development) and adopted the resolution 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Zoning Update: UDO Text Amendment (Form-Based Downtown Design Districts)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a public hearing touching on proposed Elliott Square development, historic designation concerns, and density vs. form-based envelope regulation (allowing 12–24 units per acre), Council members noted the hearing was about the 2.5-year planning update rather than a site plan. Council Member Mike Woodard spoke in support of form-based zoning as the future for Ninth Street and downtown, and Council approved the UDO text amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 18: Comprehensive Plan Amendment — Downtown Zoning Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the Comprehensive Plan Amendment adjusting downtown tier boundaries (three expansions and one retraction), designating the downtown tier for design districts on the future land use map, and aligning policy language with the downtown master plan. With no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and approved Item 18 by a 7-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Item 19: Zoning Map Change — Downtown Zoning Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented the Downtown Zoning Update map change removing prior base zoning districts and Downtown Design Overlays 1, 2, and 3 and replacing them with Downtown Design Districts while keeping the existing Historic District Overlay in place. With no public speakers, Council approved Item 19 by a 7-0 vote, heard a winter-weather solid waste collection delay announcement, and adjourned at 9:13 p.m.
