meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 21, 2010 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden with six Council members present (Mayor Bill Bell absent), the Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority presentation schedule, granted Eugene Brown an excused 3:00 p.m. early departure, and granted Farad Ali an excused absence for the prior Monday night's meeting. Board of Elections Director Michael Ash reported that the 2009 municipal primary and general elections cost $243,782 against a $350,000 budget—roughly $107,000 under estimate—due to a $40,000 state maintenance grant and operational savings on precinct phones, poll workers, and in-house printing. Council also heard concerns during infrastructure presentations about an eastern alignment shift affecting the Durham Rescue Mission's expansion, received a proposed Homeless Bill of Rights resolution from the Durham Youth Community Action and Advocacy Network (which Mayor Pro Tem Cole-McFadden agreed to place on the February 3 agenda of the 10-Year Plan to End Homelessness Executive Committee), and unanimously set the February 1 meeting agenda. In a written ballot appointment, a candidate (transcribed as 'Eric Linde's track') received 5 votes for the Capital Program Advisory Committee; individual ballot choices were not read aloud in the transcript digest.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Priority Items, and Excused Absence Motions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the work session to order with Farad Ali, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, Howard Clement III, and Mike Woodard present (Mayor Bill Bell absent). Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority schedule (CPAC report, Reality Check, Durham Housing Authority, East End Connector, Alston Avenue widening, and Downtown Zoning Update), granted Eugene Brown an excused early departure at 3:00 p.m., and unanimously granted Farad Ali a retroactive excused absence for the January 19 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Item 6: 2009 Municipal Election Cost Report (Durham County Board of Elections)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Ash of the Durham County Board of Elections reported that the 2009 municipal primary and general elections came in at $243,782 compared to the $350,000 budget estimate (~$107,000 savings). He attributed the variance to an unexpected $40,000 state maintenance grant, $27,000 saved by using cell phones instead of turning on all precinct landlines, $15,000 from reduced poll worker staffing, in-house manual printing, and the absence of recounts.

agenda_items.title: Transportation Alignment Comment (East End Connector / Alston Avenue)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During the afternoon infrastructure portion of the session, a speaker raised concerns that shifting the proposed roadway design eastward would adversely affect the Durham Rescue Mission's ongoing capital campaign and future expansion as well as neighboring properties to the east.

agenda_items.title: Citizens' Matters: Proposed Homeless Bill of Rights Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Representatives of the Durham Youth Community Action and Advocacy Network and a supporting speaker presented a draft Homeless Bill of Rights resolution citing point-in-time survey counts (746) and alleged mistreatment on transit and by police, seeking eventual statewide protections. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden declined immediate Council action out of respect for the city's advisory structure but committed to placing the resolution on the February 3 agenda of the 10-Year Plan to End Homelessness Executive Committee for a recommendation.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Setting, CPAC Ballot Appointment, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council moved Item 11 (Reality Check) to General Business for February 1 pending a drafted resolution and unanimously set the February 1 agenda (Consent Items 1, 3, 4, 6–9; GBA Items 5 and 11; GBA Public Hearings 15–19). The Clerk reported five ballot votes for a Capital Program Advisory Committee appointee (transcribed as 'Eric Linde's track'), and Howard Clement III shared updates on Mental Health Durham and outreach to homeless residents for the March 11–13 free dental clinic before adjournment.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 19, 2010 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with six members present and Council Member Farad Ali absent (later excused on January 21), all formal actions passed unanimously 6-0. Council granted Howard Clement III an excused absence for the January 21 work session, welcomed new Finance Director David Boyd, approved the Consent Agenda (including Lake Michie advance land acquisition, Durham Affordable Housing Coalition funding, and a Twin Lakes Park PARTF grant), and requested a memorial resolution for late former Council Member Alton Carroll Pleasants. Following public hearings, Council confirmed assessment rolls on Bellgreen Road and O.V. Drive while continuing objected properties and Connie Daniels's parcel (Item 10) 6-0, continued the Webb property Roland Street assessment hearing to the March 4 work session (Item 11) 6-0, and approved an economic development incentive contract with UK-based microelectronics firm ACW Technology (Item 12) 6-0 with an amended $11.40/hour minimum wage requirement alongside a $50,000 state match.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Priority Items, and Excused Absence Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. with six members present and Farad Ali expected late/absent. Council voted 6-0 to excuse Howard Clement III from the January 21 work session and held the Planning Commission appointment until February 1. The City Manager provided supplemental details on Items 10 and 12 (confirming a $50,000 North Carolina state incentive match) and introduced new Finance Director David Boyd; Council approved priority items 6-0, and Howard Clement III requested a memorial resolution for former Council Member Alton Carroll Pleasants.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 2–5, 7–8)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the Consent Agenda 6-0, covering the November 2009 bid report, the Durham Affordable Housing Coalition FY 2009–2010 subrecipient contract, appointments of the Finance Officer and Tax Collector/Revenue Collector, advance property acquisition from Gerald A. and Sue Poole for future Lake Michie expansion, a Twin Lakes Park PARTF grant application, and a service contract for water/sewer lines.

agenda_items.title: Item 10: Public Hearing — Confirmation of Assessment Rolls (Bellgreen Road and O.V. Drive)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Engineering and Stormwater staff recommended confirming assessment rolls for Bellgreen Road and O.V. Drive improvements while continuing and referring objected properties (Lockside Master HOA, Durham Habitat for Humanity, 526 United Drive LLC, Guillermo and Dulce Ramirez, and Woodlake HOA) to a future work session. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden asked to also pull and refer Connie Daniels's parcel at 508 Bellgreen Road because she was in a nursing home facility; staff agreed, and Council approved the motion 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 11: Public Hearing — Mini Assessment Roll for Roland Street (Webb Property)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On the continued Roland Street assessment for the Webb property, the City Attorney advised that Council had already granted an eight-month delay since May 18, 2009 for the Webbs' private dispute with the prior seller, and noted another continuance to March would not impair the city's legal ability to enforce the assessment. Council amended the staff recommendation to continue the public hearing and refer the item to the March 4, 2010 work session, passing 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 12: Public Hearing — ACW Technology Economic Development Incentive Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: OEWD Director Kevin Dick presented a performance-based incentive contract (paired with a $50,000 state match) for Southampton, England-based microelectronics manufacturer ACW Technology Limited to create jobs in the urban growth area. Five speakers, including Durham Chamber of Commerce VP Ted Connor and a Durham Tech representative, supported the deal and praised ACW's openness to hiring ex-offenders, while Council Member Eugene Brown urged preference for returning military veterans. Council approved the contract 6-0 as amended by Howard Clement III to specify a minimum wage of $11.40 per hour before adjourning at 7:47 p.m.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 7, 2010 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council opened with remarks clarifying that the August yard-waste facility construction contract awarded 7-0 to C.T. Wilson ($452,036) followed disqualification of a non-responsible $300,000 bid and was only $6,000 below the next responsible bid ($458,500) rather than $152,000 higher as reported in the press. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's, City Attorney's (two closed-session claims items under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)), and City Clerk's (referring Item 1 minutes back) priority items, suspended the rules to vote on Item 6 (Rock Quarry Park/Edison Johnson Recreation Center construction agreement) and suspended the rules to approve Item 15 (Second Amendment to the West Village II Agreement) unanimously. Council also heard presentations on the North Carolina Dental Society's Missions of Mercy free adult dental clinic (Item 14) and Jordan Lake regional water supply cost-sharing with Chatham County and OWASA, heard from Ms. Webb regarding her Roland Street assessment dispute ahead of the January 19 public hearing, and voted unanimously to enter closed session. No split votes occurred.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order at 1:05 p.m. with all seven Council members present. A Council member clarified press coverage of the $452,036 C.T. Wilson yard-waste facility contract, noting a $300,000 Thompson Contracting bid was deemed non-responsible and the next responsible bid was $458,500. Council unanimously approved the City Manager's priority items, two City Attorney closed-session items under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), and the City Clerk's referral of Item 1 minutes back to the Clerk's office.

agenda_items.title: Item 6 (Rock Quarry Park / Edison Johnson) and Item 15 (West Village II Second Amendment)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During the agenda walkthrough, Council unanimously suspended the rules on Item 6 (Rock Quarry Park and Aquatics Center / Edison Johnson Recreation Center Construction Agreement). Council also unanimously suspended the rules and unanimously approved Item 15 (Second Amendment to the West Village II Agreement), which had been carried forward across several prior meetings.

agenda_items.title: Item 14: North Carolina Dental Society Missions of Mercy Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Alec Parker of the North Carolina Dental Society presented plans for the Missions of Mercy (MOM) free dental clinic program in Durham, describing a gymnasium-scale clinic model.

agenda_items.title: Jordan Lake Regional Water Supply Partnership Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated Council on Durham's regional water partnership and 10% (10 million gallons per day) Jordan Lake water allocation, noting the state would evaluate demand for any future allocation requests. Responding to budget and cost inquiries, staff highlighted ongoing cost-sharing discussions with Chatham County and OWASA regarding a potential western Jordan Lake intake.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ms. Webb addressed Council regarding the ~$22,000 assessment on her Roland Street property, stating her purchase contract disclosed no pending assessments and asking for time until March (the three-year purchase mark) to pursue legal/title remedies. Mayor Bell kept the item on the January 19 public hearing agenda while asking the City Attorney to review any legal implications of further delay, after which a Council member questioned City Hall visibility and newspaper outreach for a water/sewer discount program and Council voted to enter closed session.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the January 4, 2010 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, six members were present and Council Member Eugene Brown was granted an excused absence by a 5-0 vote due to illness. Ceremonial and administrative business included a proclamation recognizing Earned Income Tax Credit Awareness Day with Community Development Senior Project Manager Juanita Massenburg and a moment of sympathy from the City Manager for deceased city employee Eugene Odom. Council unanimously approved (6-0) the Consent Agenda excluding pulled Items 5, 9, 11, and 20, approved the creation and bylaws of the City Cultural Advisory Board (Item 7, 6-0), and continued Item 24 (Second Amendment to West Village II Agreement) to Thursday's work session at Council Member Brown's request. Following a public hearing on the FY 2010–2015 Consolidated Plan (Item 21, covering approximately $1.9 million in CDBG, $1.2 million in HOME, and $80,000 in Emergency Shelter Grant planning allocations), Council approved Item 21 and all four pulled consent items—the Rolling Hills option contract with MBA Development Corp. (Item 5), the Triangle Citizens Rebuilding Communities contract (Item 9), Hillside Park/W.D. Hill Recreation Center upgrades (Item 11), and North/South Durham Water Reclamation Facility renovations (Item 20)—by unanimous 6-0 votes among all members present.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Excusal of Council Member Eugene Brown
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the January 4, 2010 Regular City Council Meeting to order at 7:00 p.m., followed by a moment of silent meditation and the Pledge of Allegiance. The Clerk called the roll, confirming Mayor Bill Bell, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, and Council Members Farad Ali, Diane Catotti, Howard Clement III, and Mike Woodard present, while Council Member Eugene Brown had notified staff he would be absent due to illness and was excused on a 5-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation (Earned Income Tax Credit Awareness Day) and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell presented an Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) Awareness Day proclamation to Juanita Massenburg of the Department of Community Development, highlighting free tax filing assistance offered with more than 25 partners including Duke Law School to help working families avoid high-cost refund anticipation loans. During priority items, the City Manager reported no formal items but expressed condolences on the passing of General Services landscape laborer Eugene Odom, the City Attorney and Clerk had no priority items, and Council Member Howard Clement III recognized guests from Cumberland County.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Items 5, 9, 11, and 20)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read the consent agenda titles, including Firefighters' Relief Fund trustee appointment, bid report, assessment roll public hearings, a memorial resolution for Lewis Edward Hargis, Jr., General Services bundle phase three amendments, ARRA COBRA grant ordinance, IBM and Blue Cross/Blue Shield grants, 2010 Fugitive Apprehension Task Force grant, Durham County school water/sewer extension, West Markham Avenue culvert design amendment, and residential meter replacement. Items 5, 9, 11, and 20 were pulled for separate discussion, and the remaining consent items passed unanimously 6-0.

agenda_items.title: General Business Agenda Item 7: City Cultural Advisory Board
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff from the Office of Economic and Workforce Development presented Item 7 establishing a City Cultural Advisory Board to replace the former City-County Cultural Master Plan advisory body. The item included revised provisions clarifying eligibility for secondary school students to serve as student members and updating the quorum rule, and passed 6-0.

agenda_items.title: General Business Agenda Item 24: Second Amendment to West Village II Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell announced that absent Council Member Eugene Brown had requested continuing Item 24 (Second Amendment to West Village II Agreement) to the upcoming Thursday work session. Council confirmed the deferral to Thursday's work session without a formal roll-call vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (continued to work session)

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Item 21: FY 2010–2015 Consolidated Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Community Development Director Mike Burris and Federal Programs Coordinator Wilma Conners held the initial HUD-mandated needs public hearing for the five-year Consolidated Plan (due May 15, 2010), noting planning estimates of approximately $1.9 million in CDBG, $1.2 million in HOME, and $80,000 in Emergency Shelter Grant funds. A Council member flagged concerns about integrating the Ten-Year Plan to End Homelessness, while public speakers including Denise Hester urged neighborhood streetscape parity outside downtown, youth home-repair engagement, and expanded homeownership; staff noted 22 families had been assisted into homeownership in the first six months of the fiscal year before Council approved the item 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 5: Option Contract with MBA Development Corp. (Rolling Hills)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council heard public comment from Larry Hester, Denise Hester, Edward I. Woods, and Betty Woods regarding the Rolling Hills option contract with MBA Development Corp. Speakers criticized downtown streetscape prioritization over neighborhood corridors, urged a resolution barring eminent domain for private economic gain, and questioned the lack of HOA meeting notice or resolution regarding a $1 common-area transfer while five homeowners remained in Rolling Hills; Council approved Item 5 on a 6-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 9: Contract with Triangle Citizens Rebuilding Communities, Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A resident who pulled Item 9 criticized 'good faith' workforce provisions as lacking enforcement teeth and asked how the City tracks where contract jobs go and who receives them. Following the comment, Council approved Item 9 on a 6-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 11: Hillside Park / W.D. Hill Recreation Center Upgrades

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 20: North & South Durham Water Reclamation Facility Renovations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Item 20, pulled by Dr. Allison, covered construction contracting for renovations at the North Durham and South Durham Water Reclamation Facilities. Council approved the item 6-0, and Mayor Bell asked the City Manager to follow up directly on Dr. Allison's questions.

agenda_items.title: Council Inquiries (Toilet Rebate Program, Amplification Equipment) and Adjournment

Council members also discussed microphone audio and telecommunications amplification devices for hearing-impaired attendees and wished Mayor Bell a happy birthday before adjourning at 7:59 p.m.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 22, 2009 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, the Council excused Council Member Eugene Brown (6-0) and opened with a remembrance of longtime General Services employee Bobby Malone. Council suspended the rules to unanimously approve (6-0) Item 8, accepting a North Carolina 911 Board orthophotography grant and technical services contract, while carrying over the West Village II Second Amendment (Item 24) to January 4, 2010. General Services staff reported roughly $700,000 in cost savings from switching five recreation center bundle projects from Construction Manager at Risk (CMR) to direct single-prime bidding, and Water Management updated Council on the single-family high-efficiency toilet rebate pilot and potential expansion to multifamily and institutional users. All votes taken during the session were unanimous (6-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Excusal of Council Member Brown, and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order, confirmed six members present, and Council voted 6-0 to excuse Council Member Eugene Brown. City Manager noted the passing of 21-year city laborer Bobby Malone and flagged priority items including Rolling Hills (Item 5), Southside CDBG acquisition (Item 6), an NC 911 grant needing immediate action (Item 8), carrying over West Village II (Item 24) to January 4, a recreation center bundle update, and two citizen matters.

agenda_items.title: Consent and Departmental Agenda Review (Items 1-24) and Item 8 Suspension Vote
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council reviewed consent items including the October 2009 bid report (with Purchasing Manager Joe Clark clarifying low-bid rules on non-federal contracts awarded to a Canadian firm), a memorial resolution for Louis H. Hodges Jr., Cultural Advisory Board student membership bylaws, a typo correction on Triangle Citizens Rebuilding Communities (Item 9), ARRA COBRA grant funds (Item 12), and a Barbee Chapel Road sewer/water extension with Montclair LLC (Item 17). Council voted 6-0 to suspend the rules and 6-0 to approve Item 8, the NC 911 Board orthophotography grant and technical services contract.

agenda_items.title: Recreation Center Bundle Direct-Bidding Cost Savings Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services staff reported receiving 11 bids from primarily local contractors after shifting recreation center bundle projects from Construction Manager at Risk (CMR) to direct single-prime bidding, yielding approximately $700,000 to $750,000 in savings. Council requested future comparisons showing general-conditions and contingency deltas, and staff noted Parks and Recreation would return with recommendations in January to fund deferred 2005 bond list items.

agenda_items.title: High-Efficiency Toilet Rebate Pilot Program Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Water Management staff briefed Council on the single-family owner-occupied toilet rebate pilot, noting customers replacing multiple toilets could apply for a second rebate. Council members discussed expanding eligibility to multifamily landlords, small churches and nonprofits, and large employers while tracking utility bill impacts and budget capacity.

agenda_items.title: Setting the Agenda and Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 6-0 to set the upcoming regular meeting agenda with Consent Items 1-6, 9-16, and 18-20, General Business Items 7 and 24, and Public Hearing Item 21. Council then voted 6-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) regarding business location or expansion matters.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 21, 2009 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, Council excused Council Member Eugene Brown (recovering from surgery) by a 6-0 vote, issued proclamations for the Talk It Up Lock It Up underage-drinking campaign and Durham's 2003 Bill of Rights Defense and immigration-status policies, and approved the consent agenda (6-0, excluding Item 6), a $73.5 million ARRA Recovery Zone Economic Development Bond allocation application (Item 8, 6-0), stormwater utility code amendments (Item 25, 6-0), and the Toll Brothers Page Road rezoning with a stormwater reuse commitment (Item 30, 6-0). The session's major conflict occurred on Item 6, the Second Amendment to the West Village II Agreement: a motion to approve failed on a 3-3 tie, with Ayes from Bill Bell, Howard Clement III, and Farad Ali and Nays from Cora Cole-McFadden, Diane Catotti, and Mike Woodard (Eugene Brown excused). Following the 3-3 tie, Mike Woodard moved to reconsider Item 6 (passed 6-0) and then moved to postpone consideration to the January 4, 2010 cycle (passed 6-0) so Cora Cole-McFadden could obtain requested youth-space follow-up information and Eugene Brown could participate.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excusal of Council Member Brown, and Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order and Council voted 6-0 to excuse Council Member Eugene Brown as he recuperated from surgery. Mayor Bell presented a proclamation launching the Talk It Up, Lock It Up campaign against underage alcohol access and read a proclamation reaffirming Durham's 2003 Bill of Rights Defense Resolution and Resolution 9046 regarding civil immigration status and traffic stops.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items and Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 6 and Moving Item 8 to GBA)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On the City Attorney's recommendation, Council voted 6-0 to move Item 8 to the General Business Agenda so the bond resolution could be read into the record. Council then approved the Consent Agenda (Items 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 13, 14, 18, 19, and 21, excluding Item 6) by a 6-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Item 8: ARRA Recovery Zone Economic Development Bond Allocation ($73.5M)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council read into the record and considered a resolution authorizing the Interim Finance Director to apply to the North Carolina Department of Commerce for $73,500,000 in Recovery Zone Economic Development Bond allocation under the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act, designating the entire city as a recovery zone due to significant unemployment and economic distress.

agenda_items.title: Item 25: Public Hearing on Chapter 70, Article VIII Stormwater Utility Funds Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant Stormwater Manager Paul Wiebke presented ordinance revisions prioritizing stormwater utility funds for city rights-of-way and Priority 1 and 2 private-property drainage problems threatening structural integrity or access, while excluding stable private drainage systems. With no public speakers, Council closed the hearing and adopted the ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Item 30: Zoning Map Change Z0800032 (Simcoe / Toll Brothers, 2613 Page Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented Toll Brothers Incorporated's PDR 6.79 development plan revision at 2613 Page Road, returning from a November 2 public hearing with a new Committed Element #17 requiring stormwater reuse conditioned on NC Division of Water Quality nitrogen-reduction credit. Council Member Diane Catotti requested sentence clarification on Committed Element #17 and Council Member Mike Woodard praised staff and the applicant.

agenda_items.title: Item 6: Second Amendment to West Village II Agreement (Tie Failure, Reconsideration, Postponement)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Members Mike Woodard and Diane Catotti opposed the West Village II second amendment because they remained opposed to using Economic Development Administration (EDA) funds to underground Main Street power lines, while staff noted the amendment restored $1 million in EDA funds for alternate streetscape projects. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden also voted no due to unanswered questions about youth/community space commitments, resulting in a 3-3 tie failure before Council voted 6-0 to reconsider and 6-0 to postpone the item to the January 4, 2010 cycle.

votes.notes: Eugene Brown was absent/excused.

votes.notes: Eugene Brown was excused.
votes.discussion_detail: Motion approving the City Attorney's request to handle Item 8 separately on GBA and read the resolution into the record.

votes.discussion_detail: Adoption of resolution authorizing application for $73,500,000 in ARRA Recovery Zone Economic Development Bond allocation and designating the city as a recovery zone.

votes.discussion_detail: Adoption of stormwater utility ordinance revisions prioritizing right-of-way and Priority 1-2 structural/access drainage projects.

votes.item_title: Reconsider Item 6 (Second Amendment to West Village II Agreement)
votes.notes: Eugene Brown was excused.

votes.discussion_detail: Motion by Mike Woodard to postpone Item 6 to the agenda cycle beginning at the next day's work session for action on January 4, 2010.

disagreements.issue: West Village II Second Amendment (Use of EDA Funds for Underground Power Lines and Youth Space)
disagreements.summary: Council split 3-3 on approving the Second Amendment to the West Village II Agreement, leading to an initial tie failure before Council unanimously voted to reconsider and postpone the item to January 4, 2010.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the Second Amendment to restore $1 million in EDA funds for alternate streetscape projects while advancing West Village II.
side_a_arguments: The amendment restores $1 million of EDA money (against $4 million general money) previously tied up, making it available for alternate streetscape projects.
Delaying risks time-constraint complications on project administration.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose or withhold approval due to continued opposition to EDA-funded Main Street power-line undergrounding and unanswered questions on youth space commitments.
side_b_arguments: EDA funds should not be used to underground electrical power lines along Main Street, which Council had not originally committed to funding.
Further follow-up is needed from the developer regarding promised youth/community space.
disagreements.resolution: Failed 3-3 on the initial vote; subsequently reconsidered (6-0) and postponed (6-0) to the January 4, 2010 agenda cycle.

meetings.title: City Council Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 10, 2009 City Council Work Session presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, Council acted on priority ARRA and infrastructure items by suspending the rules to unanimously approve the Third Fork Creek Trail Phase 1B construction contract (Item 10) and the ARRA 2010 Streetscape Replacement contract (Item 11), while setting additional ARRA traffic-signal and pedestrian safety contracts, financial and visitor-bureau presentations, and Rolling Hills Southside redevelopment on the schedule. Later in the session, Council suspended the rules and passed Supplemental Item 28 (Beer and Wine Privilege License Issuance) by voice vote after Howard Clement III criticized the City's focus on license revenue and limited notification to Partners Against Crime (PAC) districts, flagging the issue for budget review. City Attorney staff also briefed Council on a North Carolina Utilities Commission order rejecting steep proposed rate hikes on Duke Energy street lighting and unbundling pole and wiring capital costs for potential developer recovery.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Priority Items, and Duke Rate Case Update Scheduling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the work session to order with roll call and birthday acknowledgments. City Manager flagged priority rule-suspension requests for Third Fork Creek Trail (Item 10), ARRA streetscape, traffic signal, and pedestrian projects (Items 11, 15, 16, 17), Repower grant (Item 20), and supplemental items on beer/wine privilege licenses (Item 28), bulletproof vests (Item 29), and Simcoe zoning (Item 30), while the City Attorney scheduled a Duke Energy rate update.

agenda_items.title: Consent Review and Rule-Suspension Votes on Items 10 and 11
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council requested re-advertising Item 2 (Capital Program Advisory Committee) to broaden board diversity and questioned the December 15 deadline on ARRA Recovery Zone bonds (Item 8), which Interim Finance Director Keith Hermann confirmed did not apply to Durham's application. Council suspended the rules and unanimously approved the Third Fork Creek Trail Phase 1B contract (Item 10, January to October schedule) and ARRA Contract ER-5100-EA 2010 Streetscape Replacement (Item 11).

agenda_items.title: Item 28: Beer and Wine Privilege License Issuance and PAC Notification Debate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During discussion of Supplemental Item 28 covering 16 new businesses applying for beer and wine privilege licenses, Howard Clement III objected that only one application had reached PAC 4 and argued the City appeared overly focused on license fee income rather than neighborhood notification on permit renewals or modifications. Council agreed to flag the policy for budget review, suspended the rules, and approved Item 28 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Setting the December 21 Regular Meeting Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council approved the agenda for the next regular meeting, placing Items 1, 3-9, 12-14, 18, 19, and 21 on Consent and Items 25 and 30 on General Business Public Hearings, noting Items 28 and 29 had already been acted upon.

agenda_items.title: Duke Energy Rate Case Briefing on Street Lighting Costs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant City Attorney Sherry Rosenthal reported that the NC Utilities Commission rejected Duke Energy's proposed rate schedule that would have raised municipal street lighting rates by roughly 78% and ordered capital costs for poles and wiring separated from ongoing rates. Council discussed adopting a resolution or policy requiring developers to fund upfront street lighting capital and initial operating costs in new subdivisions and annexations.

disagreements.issue: Beer and Wine Privilege License PAC Notification and Revenue Focus (Item 28)
disagreements.summary: Howard Clement III criticized the City's handling of 16 new beer and wine privilege license applications, arguing the City appeared overly focused on fee revenue while failing to route permit modifications and renewals to Partners Against Crime (PAC) districts.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the 16 privilege licenses under current statutory rules and address PAC notification processes during the upcoming budget review.
side_a_arguments: License issuance follows existing administrative requirements and can be acted on without delay.
Process changes for notifying PAC districts can be flagged for review during the budget process.
disagreements.side_b_position: Require stronger neighborhood/PAC review of alcohol permit renewals and modifications rather than prioritizing license revenue.
side_b_arguments: Only one of the 16 businesses had appeared before PAC 4.
The City makes it look as though it is only interested in collecting license fee income rather than supporting community oversight.
disagreements.resolution: Council flagged PAC notification procedures for review during the upcoming budget process and passed Item 28 by voice vote.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 7, 2009 organizational and regular City Council meeting, Durham County Elections Director Mike Ash presented certified November 3, 2009 municipal election results, Mayor Bill Bell and re-elected council members were sworn in, and Council unanimously elected Cora Cole-McFadden as Mayor Pro Tempore (7-0). Council approved invalidating protest petitions on Items 39 and 41 (7-0) and referred the Villas at Colt Arbor rezoning (Item 35) back to staff (7-0). The sole split vote occurred on Item 39, the Hope Valley Farms zoning map change, which passed 5-2 with Ayes from Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Eugene Brown, and Farad Ali and Nays from Diane Catotti and Mike Woodard over restaurant drive-thru window placement and neighborhood buffering along Martin Luther King Jr. Parkway. Council also unanimously approved initial zonings for SecureCare Properties (Item 40, 7-0) and Primrose School (Item 41, 7-0) and a HOME Investment Partnership item (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Organizational Meeting: Certified Election Results, Swearing-In, and Mayor Pro Tem Election
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Board of Elections Director Mike Ash presented the certified abstract of the October 6 primary and November 3, 2009 general municipal election. Mayor Bill Bell and re-elected council members took the oath of office, after which Council unanimously elected Cora Cole-McFadden as Mayor Pro Tempore and heard ceremonial remarks including the introduction of Durham Economic Resource Center Director Jackie Brown.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items: Protest Petitions, Item 35 Referral, and Council Requests
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council voted 7-0 to accept the City Clerk's determination that protest petitions filed against Items 39 (Hope Valley Farms) and 41 (Primrose School) were invalid, and 7-0 to refer Item 35 (Villas at Colt Arbor) back to the administration. Howard Clement III requested a study of curbside leaf vacuuming (which the City Manager scheduled for budget retreat evaluation due to cost) and Mike Woodard requested a memorial resolution for journalist Ed Hodges.

agenda_items.title: Item 39: Hope Valley Farms Zoning Map Change Public Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council and staff reviewed site buffering along Martin Luther King Jr. Parkway and negotiated three proffered committed elements: a 36-inch masonry wall with landscaping, no restaurant drive-thru order windows facing the southwest neighborhood, and no fuel sales or convenience store. Neighbors questioned winter tree-buffer effectiveness and drive-thru orientation; Council approved the rezoning 5-2.

agenda_items.title: Item 40: SecureCare Properties Initial Zoning Map Change
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented direct translational Industrial Light (IL) zoning for SecureCare Properties on Durham-Chapel Hill Boulevard service road and New Hope Commons Drive, taking effect with annexation on December 31, 2009. With no public speakers, Council closed the public hearing and approved the zoning.

agenda_items.title: Item 41: Primrose School Initial Zoning Map Change (Z0900012A)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented direct translational RS-20 zoning for the recently annexed 1.8-acre Primrose School parcel at Ephesus Church Road and Hope Road. Counsel for an objecting neighbor noted a prior site plan had been rejected and argued neighbors should receive notice prior to annexation since a daycare minor special use permit goes to the Board of Adjustment rather than Council; Council closed the hearing and approved the initial zoning.

agenda_items.title: Pulled HOME Investment Partnership Item and Jobs Forum Announcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council took up the pulled HOME Investment Partnership consent item and approved it 7-0. Following an announcement of a Wednesday 6:00 p.m. jobs forum in Council Chambers, the meeting adjourned.

disagreements.issue: Hope Valley Farms Rezoning Drive-Thru Orientation and Parkway Buffering (Item 39)
disagreements.summary: Council divided 5-2 over whether proffered committed elements—a 36-inch masonry wall, no fuel sales/convenience store, and keeping drive-thru windows off the southwest neighborhood-facing side—adequately protected Martin Luther King Jr. Parkway aesthetics and adjacent homes.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the rezoning with the three proffered committed elements shielding the adjacent neighborhood and prohibiting fuel sales.
side_a_arguments: The applicant agreed to bar convenience stores and gas pumps and prohibit drive-thru order windows facing the southwest neighborhood.
A 36-inch masonry wall paired with landscaping provides standard headlight screening along the parkway.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the rezoning due to drive-thru orientation, parkway visual character, and neighborhood impacts.
side_b_arguments: Placing the drive-thru away from the southwest houses pushes the drive-thru circulation toward Martin Luther King Jr. Parkway, undermining its parkway character.
Deciduous tree buffers offer limited visual and noise screening for neighbors during winter months.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 5-2 with the three proffered committed elements.
